facts.label: Billing method
facts.value: Pay-as-you-go; no upfront commitment or minimum fee; monthly charge for metered use.

facts.label: Regional rates
facts.value: AWS states CloudWatch pricing varies by Region. Examples below select US East (N. Virginia), us-east-1; they are not prices for all regions.

facts.label: Logs Standard ingestion rate
facts.value: $0.50 per GB in the first paid band after the first 5 GB free.

facts.label: Logs Essentials ingestion rate
facts.value: $0.25 per GB in the first paid band after the first 5 GB free.

facts.label: Log storage and query example rates
facts.value: For Standard and Essentials, the pricing examples use $0.03 per GB-month of archived storage and $0.005 per GB scanned in Logs Insights.

facts.label: Classic custom metrics
facts.value: First paid band example is $0.30 per custom metric-month; higher volume lowers the marginal rate. Detailed monitoring also counts as custom metric usage.

facts.label: Standard metric alarm
facts.value: Pricing example uses $0.10 per alarm metric-month; high-resolution alarms and alarms with query expressions can cost more.

facts.label: Other AWS products
facts.value: Synthetics invokes Lambda and stores artifacts in S3; exports, delivery and alert destinations can add charges from their own AWS service meters.

facts.label: Ongoing free usage
facts.value: AWS lists CloudWatch as an Always Free service. Its CloudWatch pricing page lists recurring limits such as 5 GB log data, 1,800 Live Tail minutes, basic service metrics, 10 custom/detailed metrics, 3 custom dashboards and 10 standard alarm metrics.

facts.label: Logs free allowance
facts.value: First 5 GB of data across ingestion, archive storage and Logs Insights scanning is listed in the CloudWatch free-tier table; 1,800 Live Tail minutes and one Contributor Insights rule with the first million matching events are also listed.

facts.label: Metric and alarm free allowances
facts.value: The page lists AWS service basic monitoring metrics, 10 custom/detailed metrics, 1 million API requests (with named exceptions), 3 custom dashboards with up to 50 metrics each, and 10 standard-resolution alarm metrics.

facts.label: APM free use
facts.value: Application Signals' free-usage offer is limited to three months per account or the listed cap first: 100 million signals, with spans/transaction visibility governed by a separate offer. X-Ray also lists 100,000 recorded traces and 1 million retrieved/scanned traces per month free.

facts.label: Synthetics and RUM free use
facts.value: 100 Synthetics canary runs per month are listed. RUM lists a first-time trial of 1 million web events per account.

facts.label: Free account credits and time window
facts.value: New AWS customers can choose a Free plan of up to six months or until its credits are exhausted and receive up to $200 in credits. Free Tier FAQs say credits are up to $100 sign-up plus up to $100 earned; Free plan expires by six months or credit exhaustion and the account closes unless upgraded.

facts.label: Service trial
facts.value: CloudWatch RUM has a first-time free trial of 1 million web events per account. Application Signals has the separate three-month/cap offer above.

facts.label: CloudWatch Omni trial
facts.value: Eligible Omni accounts receive $1,000 in credits for 30 days. The credit covers specified OpenTelemetry log/metric ingestion and Application Signals spans; it is available to up to 10 accounts per AWS Organization.

facts.label: Account sign-up payment method
facts.value: AWS's Free Tier FAQ says a payment method is required for identity verification for a Free plan account.

facts.label: Smallest paid CloudWatch use
facts.value: No minimum fee or commitment. The first paid CloudWatch Logs Standard band in the N. Virginia pricing example is $0.50/GB ingested after 5 GB free; Essentials is $0.25/GB after the listed allowance.

facts.label: Entry APM and canary rates
facts.value: Application Signals uses signal-volume tiers; X-Ray trace record/retrieval is metered. Synthetics uses $0.0012 per canary run in the N. Virginia example before other product charges.

facts.label: Omni analysis charges
facts.value: Omni includes dashboards and alerts within quotas. Log/trace scans up to 5× monthly eligible ingestion are included; excess scans are $0.005/GB. PromQL is $0.01 per million samples; AgentCore evaluations use Amazon Bedrock AgentCore rates.

facts.label: Above allowances
facts.value: CloudWatch uses pay-as-you-go charging; exceeding free usage produces the listed usage charges. Log ingestion may also be throttled by service quotas.

facts.label: Log-query charge behavior
facts.value: Logs Insights charges by scanned volume; cancelled queries are charged for scanned data to cancellation, while failed queries are not charged.

facts.label: Usage alerts / spend cap
facts.value: AWS billing budgets and Free Tier alerts can notify about usage or thresholds. A CloudWatch-specific hard spending cap that stops CloudWatch ingestion or charges was not published in the checked pricing and billing pages.

facts.label: Alarm action control
facts.value: CloudWatch alarms can notify or trigger supported AWS actions; muting suppresses actions but not monitoring/evaluation.

facts.label: Log retention
facts.value: CloudWatch Logs defaults to indefinite retention; a log group can use a configured retention window. Expired entries are marked for deletion; physical deletion typically takes up to 72 hours and can take longer.

facts.label: Metric retention
facts.value: High-resolution data under 60 seconds: 3 hours; 1-minute points: 15 days; 5-minute points: 63 days; 1-hour points: 455 days.

facts.label: RUM retention
facts.value: CloudWatch RUM end-user telemetry is retained for 30 days; app monitor can copy telemetry to CloudWatch Logs for customer-selected log retention.

facts.label: Canary result retention
facts.value: Synthetics result history is configurable from 1 to 455 days. Artifacts written to S3 and canary logs/metrics are governed separately.

facts.label: Users, accounts and apps
facts.value: AWS IAM accounts/identities govern access; cross-account observability connects source accounts to a monitoring account. No CloudWatch seat-based subscription or universal application/project allowance was found.

facts.label: Canary resource limit
facts.value: Default CloudWatch account quota is 500 canaries per supported Region; quota is adjustable.

facts.label: Log volume measurement
facts.value: CloudWatch prices ingestion by volume received; logs are structured as timestamp/message events. Standard/Essentials storage is charged on compressed stored volume; query cost uses bytes scanned.

facts.label: Loss, filtering and limits
facts.value: Log transformations, data protection and ingestion quotas can affect what is stored or queryable; API/OTLP request and event limits apply.

facts.label: Additional log costs
facts.value: Data protection scanning, query scans, Live Tail beyond allowance, Contributor Insights, scheduled log alarms, and storage create separate CloudWatch meters.

facts.label: Operator location
facts.value: AWS, Inc. is located in the United States; AWS affiliates and contracting parties operate in other countries.

facts.label: Complete buyer eligibility
facts.value: No single CloudWatch-specific list of every eligible buyer country was found in the reviewed account agreement, service terms and Region materials.

facts.label: Main job
facts.value: Collects and analyzes AWS and application metrics, logs and traces; displays dashboards; evaluates alarms and can trigger actions.

facts.label: APM and service health
facts.value: Application Signals provides service maps, request volume, latency, faults and errors, service-level objectives, and correlated traces.

facts.label: User and synthetic monitoring
facts.value: RUM monitors real browser/mobile sessions; Synthetics runs scheduled browser/API canaries.

facts.label: Errors vs issue tracking
facts.value: CloudWatch exposes application errors, log anomalies, service faults, traces and RUM crashes; no issue-centric deduplication, owner workflow or release-regression tracker was documented for this offer.

facts.label: Hosted/self-hosted
facts.value: CloudWatch storage, query and management are AWS-managed. Customer-run agents and collectors send data to the hosted service; no complete self-hosted CloudWatch edition is offered in the reviewed product docs.

facts.label: Application languages
facts.value: Application Signals supports documented Java, .NET, PHP, Ruby, Python and Go instrumentation; its exact library/framework support differs by language and instrumentation path.

facts.label: Browser and mobile clients
facts.value: CloudWatch RUM offers a JavaScript web client and ADOT Android/iOS clients.

facts.label: Alarm destinations
facts.value: CloudWatch alarm actions include Amazon SNS, Lambda, EventBridge and supported AWS operations such as Auto Scaling; integrations can create incidents/OpsItems.

facts.label: Direct app push / paid support
facts.value: No CloudWatch-only SMS or phone credit bundle, country-wide delivery matrix or on-call operator entitlement was published in the reviewed notification/pricing docs.

facts.label: Noise reduction and incident grouping
facts.value: Metric, composite, anomaly-detection and log alarms; composite alarms can combine states and mute/suppress actions during maintenance.

facts.label: Log anomaly and scheduled log alarms
facts.value: CloudWatch Logs supports anomaly detection, query alarms and scheduled queries; alarm state can be evaluated on scheduled query results.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Monitors AWS services and workloads on EC2, ECS, EKS, Lambda and other AWS platforms; agent and OpenTelemetry collection can also cover on-premises or supported non-AWS hosts.

facts.label: Private and public checks
facts.value: Synthetics canaries can run public web checks or access private endpoints through VPC configuration.

facts.label: Telemetry ingestion
facts.value: AWS service integrations, CloudWatch agent, CloudWatch APIs, Embedded Metric Format and OpenTelemetry/OTLP carry metrics, logs and traces.

facts.label: Log size and API restrictions
facts.value: CloudWatch log event/API request size limits and throttling are documented by operation; OTLP logs endpoint documents a 1 MB single log event size.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Choose an AWS Region/account and IAM permissions; select native AWS metrics or create a log group; install/configure agent or SDK/OTLP where needed; then add queries, dashboards or alarms.

facts.label: AWS native data collection
facts.value: Many AWS services publish base metrics automatically. Additional operating-system/application logs, process metrics or custom telemetry require agent, SDK/API or OpenTelemetry configuration.

facts.label: Error grouping and issue creation
facts.value: Not applicable: CloudWatch reports log errors, anomalies, alarms and service faults but the reviewed product is not a crash/exception issue tracker that groups repeated errors into issue objects.

facts.label: Source maps and native crash symbols
facts.value: Not applicable as a dedicated error-tracker field; CloudWatch RUM/APM diagnostics are covered separately and do not make the platform a symbolication service listing.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: Not applicable: no error issue release/regression workflow is offered as part of the assessed CloudWatch observability service.

facts.label: Error context and replay
facts.value: Dedicated error-tracker breadcrumbs are not applicable. RUM does offer sampled session context and optional session replay; see A03.

facts.label: Search and query
facts.value: Logs Insights supports its query language, OpenSearch SQL and PPL in the documented feature matrix; Log Analytics brings queries, Live Tail and Contributor Insights into one console.

facts.label: Archive/export retrieval
facts.value: Logs can be exported to S3 for longer-lived access or routed by subscriptions; S3 storage, retrieval and lifecycle are separate.

facts.label: Traces, latency and errors
facts.value: Application Signals surfaces service request volume, latency, faults and errors; correlated X-Ray spans and Transaction Search help inspect request paths and affected transactions.

facts.label: Database and dependency diagnosis
facts.value: Application Signals service maps show service dependencies; traces can be correlated with AWS services. Database Insights provides separate database-specific monitoring.

facts.label: Sampling and billing units
facts.value: Application Signals counts inbound/outbound requests and SLO-generated signals; X-Ray trace storage/search charges use recorded and retrieved/scanned trace counts. Application Signals defaults to 5% X-Ray sampling in the documented setup and allows adjustment.

facts.label: Published APM rates
facts.value: Pricing examples charge Application Signals by million signals in volume tiers and X-Ray by trace recorded/retrieved; first 100,000 monthly recorded traces and first 1,000,000 scanned/retrieved traces are listed free.

facts.label: Real-user monitoring and replay
facts.value: RUM supports browser/mobile performance, errors and session details; web session replay is optional and sampled. Text inputs and visible page text are masked by default in replay.

facts.label: RUM prices
facts.value: AWS pricing example prices web RUM at $1 per 100,000 web events; first-time trial includes 1 million web events/account. Mobile OTel spans use data ingested pricing in a separate example.

facts.label: Synthetic check types
facts.value: Synthetics supports HTTP/API and scripted browser journeys, screenshots, HAR, step reports and private endpoint checks.

facts.label: Frequency and timeout
facts.value: Continuous canaries can run from once per minute to once per hour or by cron schedule. Canary timeout is configurable; creation guide says allow at least 15 seconds for cold start and instrumentation.

facts.label: Canary run price
facts.value: AWS pricing example uses $0.0012 per canary run and 100 monthly runs in the CloudWatch free-tier table.

facts.label: Probe and private location
facts.value: Canaries can use AWS-managed public locations or a customer VPC/private subnet. Available service locations are selected from the current canary configuration; no fixed advertised count was recorded.

facts.label: Canary account quota
facts.value: Default is 500 canaries per account per supported Region; quota is adjustable.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and retry
facts.value: Canaries can retry failed scheduled runs; up to two retries for most runtimes, one for canaries that time out after ten minutes.

facts.label: Maintenance and mute
facts.value: Alarm mute rules can suppress actions during scheduled windows while alarms continue to evaluate.

facts.label: Certificate/domain expiry
facts.value: No CloudWatch Synthetics native domain-expiry or certificate-expiry reminder was found in the canary guide, feature docs or pricing. A custom script could inspect a response but is not a built-in expiry check.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Not applicable: CloudWatch monitors AWS resources and applications; no customer-facing hosted status-page builder is part of the assessed service.

facts.label: Status subscribers and notification
facts.value: Not applicable: no customer status-page subscriber product is offered in this scope. Alarm destinations are internal operational notification actions, not public page subscribers.

facts.label: Status updates and incident history
facts.value: Not applicable: CloudWatch alarms and AWS's own health communications are not a customer status-page publishing service.

facts.label: Schedule and grace rules
facts.value: Not applicable: Synthetics schedules website/API checks; no missed-cron heartbeat service for external jobs was identified.

facts.label: Job failure signals
facts.value: Not applicable: no dedicated job-run heartbeat, start/end ping or job-output capture service was identified in CloudWatch docs/pricing.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable: CloudWatch backend is hosted by AWS; the customer-run agent/collector is not a self-hosted service edition.

facts.label: Export and retrieval
facts.value: Logs can be queried or exported to Amazon S3; AWS recommends subscriptions for continuous delivery. Exported objects use S3 storage/lifecycle controls and charges.

facts.label: Delete controls
facts.value: Users can delete log groups or set retention; expiry is asynchronous as described in C14. RUM event deletion follows its retention period; S3 exports require separate deletion/lifecycle settings.

facts.label: Sensitive data
facts.value: CloudWatch Logs data protection can detect and mask configured sensitive data; CloudWatch RUM session replay masks text inputs and rendered text by default.

facts.label: Encryption
facts.value: CloudWatch encrypts stored data at rest with AWS-owned keys by default; supported resources can use customer-managed KMS keys. TLS protects data in transit.

facts.label: Storage region and contract
facts.value: AWS customers select AWS Regions for content storage under the Customer Agreement. CloudWatch endpoints and feature availability are Region-specific; cross-region copies or service processing should be checked feature by feature.

facts.label: Data-processing terms
facts.value: AWS Service Terms incorporate the AWS DPA when AWS processes customer data; the DPA and Privacy Notice distinguish customer content from account information.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Amazon CloudWatch; https://aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/

facts.label: Availability
facts.value: Active AWS service; current 2026 feature announcements and guide history describe ongoing CloudWatch development.

facts.label: Recent product change
facts.value: CloudWatch Omni reached general availability on 2026-09-22 as an off-console application/AI observability experience. Its dedicated pricing is separate from standard CloudWatch dashboard/console use.

facts.label: Feature retirement
facts.value: CloudWatch Evidently was discontinued in October 2025; AWS recommends AWS AppConfig for feature-flag launches.

facts.label: Acquisition / ownership check
facts.value: AWS is the service operator. No CloudWatch acquisition notice was found in the AWS News Blog, Cloud Operations blog, What's New archive or Amazon newsroom pages searched.

facts.label: Service license
facts.value: CloudWatch is a commercial AWS managed service under AWS customer/service terms; no self-hostable server license applies.

facts.label: Collector code licenses
facts.value: Amazon CloudWatch Agent repository is MIT licensed. ADOT Collector repository states Apache License 2.0. These are optional collection components, not the CloudWatch backend.

facts.label: Documentation and support
facts.value: Public product docs and API references are available. AWS Basic Support offers account/billing support and documentation/resources; technical response promises depend on the purchased AWS Support plan.

facts.label: Service commitment
facts.value: CloudWatch has an SLA for listed APIs/functions, including metrics APIs, log ingestion APIs, alarms and specified Network Monitoring functions; coverage is not all console operations.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable: AWS operates the CloudWatch backend. Users still maintain any deployed agents, collectors and instrumented applications.

facts.label: Sampling
facts.value: PHP agent exposes a transaction sample_rate; browser agent exposes session and trace sampling percentages. A single plan-wide or per-signal quota behavior is not published.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: Browser RUM captures views, web vitals, errors, actions/resources when enabled and session context; mobile RUM covers iOS/Android sessions.

facts.label: Page limits and branding
facts.value: No public customer-facing status-page product or status-page limits found in product index, pricing or docs.

facts.label: Subscribers and channels
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted status-page offer found.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Not applicable: no customer-facing status-page offer found.

facts.label: Schedule and grace rules
facts.value: No dedicated cron/heartbeat monitoring product is listed. APM supports background-job transaction instrumentation, but job-schedule grace rules are not documented.

facts.label: Job failure signals
facts.value: No dedicated missed-check-in or cron job failure signal was found. APM may capture errors in instrumented background jobs.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Complete on-premises platform is offered, but public minimum/recommended CPU, memory, storage, databases and architecture requirements were not found.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Logs can be archived to customer-owned Amazon S3 as compressed JSON. Source maps have delete API controls. General account/event export and account deletion process are not established by these sources.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Browser RUM supports beforeSend event filtering/redaction, consent controls, URL scrubbing and replay masking; replay defaults to mask.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: iOS error events can be altered/dropped by an event mapper; crash and certain fatal events cannot be suppressed, though redaction applies where supported.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Browser agent supports US, India and EU intake regions; defaults to US. The key is tied to a region. A DPA/GDPR page is linked, but regional coverage by signal and subprocessor list were not resolved.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Trust-center URL and GDPR page were attempted; trust-center page fetch failed and /gdpr/ returned an inaccessible URL.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Atatus; official site uses Atatus name. No former product name found.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Active offer; current product pages, 2026 releases and 2025 company blog update are published. No official acquisition, shutdown or sunset notice found.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: Hosted platform is proprietary. Terms reserve Atatus ownership of its technology and restrict source access except for certain agents. No complete-platform open-source license is published for on-premises.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Public docs and email support are stated; pricing page says support is included in subscriptions and priority support is for enterprise. No response-time guarantee found.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Page supports private/air-gapped deployment but does not publish install, upgrade, backup, restore or security-patching procedures.

facts.label: Public-page monthly billing unit
facts.value: The public-page price table gives a per-page monthly subscription price. Its displayed currency is $; no ISO currency code is shown.

facts.label: Private-page monthly billing unit
facts.value: Private-page plans are shown per month and page; the pricing page does not identify an ISO currency code.

facts.label: Audience-specific monthly billing unit
facts.value: Audience-specific page starts at $300/month and is priced in fixed page tiers; exact ISO currency code is not shown.

facts.label: Monthly billing and changes
facts.value: Monthly subscriptions bill on the same calendar day each month. Monthly plan changes can be made within a page type; mid-month upgrades are prorated and downgrades create account credit, not a cash refund.

facts.label: Annual billing
facts.value: Annual credit-card subscriptions require manual setup and a signed order form; annual plan changes and invoices are handled through support. The public rate page does not show a separate annual discount.

facts.label: Tax and currency conversion
facts.value: Whether listed dollar prices include tax or how tax and buyer currency conversion are handled is not stated on the pricing page checked.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free is an ongoing public-page plan, not just a trial. One organization can have up to two Free pages. Allowance is 100 subscribers, 25 components, 2 team members, and 2 metrics.

facts.label: Free plan channels
facts.value: Current pricing lists email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams notifications on Free. The Free-plan help article lists email only and does not mention Slack or Teams.

facts.label: Free-plan customer use
facts.value: The Free pricing and terms pages do not separately state whether commercial or personal use is required or excluded.

facts.label: Public-page trial
facts.value: Public page trial has no time limit, but the page is visible only to logged-in team members until it is activated on Free or paid plan.

facts.label: Private-page trial
facts.value: Private page trial lasts 30 days and includes a trial version of Corporate-level features with up to 10 team members, 1,000 employees, and 5 metrics.

facts.label: Audience-specific trial
facts.value: Audience-specific trial lasts 30 days and includes up to 500 users, 10 groups, 10 team members, and 5 metrics.

facts.label: Trial payment-card and auto-conversion rules
facts.value: Whether a card is required at trial start and whether a trial can automatically convert to paid without activation was not stated in the trial and billing pages checked.

facts.label: Lowest paid public plan
facts.value: Hobby is the lowest paid public plan at $29/month; it includes 250 subscribers, 5 team members, and 5 metrics. It lists email, Slack, and Teams notifications, basic customization, custom domain, and REST API.

facts.label: Lowest paid private plan
facts.value: Starter is the lowest paid private page plan at $79/month; it includes 5 team members, 50 employees, and 5 metrics.

facts.label: Lowest paid audience-specific plan
facts.value: Audience-specific starts at $300/month for 500 users, 10 groups, 25 team members, and 30 metrics.

facts.label: Subscriber cap behavior
facts.value: Plan subscriber limits are published and active-plan counting excludes quarantined, unconfirmed, and deleted subscribers. Exact behavior when an active page reaches its subscriber maximum was not stated in the subscriber, pricing, or billing pages checked.

facts.label: Trial subscriber cap
facts.value: Public trial is capped at 25 subscribers, and trial counting includes active, quarantined, unconfirmed, and deleted subscribers.

facts.label: Component hard limit
facts.value: Maximum 1,100 components. At the maximum, an admin must delete existing components before adding more.

facts.label: Team-member cap behavior
facts.value: Team-member quotas are stated by plan. The team-member guide says admins cannot add another member at the limit without changing allocation or reducing members; public plan overage price is not listed on the current pricing page.

facts.label: Usage-based charges and spend control
facts.value: The pricing page advertises fixed monthly plan prices and unlimited notifications, not per-notification metering. The pages checked do not describe a customer-configured spending cap or automatic plan upgrade based on usage.

facts.label: Extra capacity prices
facts.value: Current pricing does not give public add-on rates for extra subscribers, metrics, employees, or team members.

facts.label: Incident history visibility
facts.value: Incident History appears for page viewers after the Statuspage has been operational for 14 days. The docs checked do not state a maximum incident-history retention period.

facts.label: Component uptime display
facts.value: Uptime Showcase displays a rolling 90-day historical view for a component. This is component-uptime display, not incident retention or raw monitoring data retention.

facts.label: Plan-specific history extensions
facts.value: No different incident-history retention period by public, private, or audience-specific plan was located in the pricing, user-guide, incident, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Account owners and team members
facts.value: Each account has one owner. Team members manage all pages in that account and share broad management permissions; the owner alone can remove team members. Public plan team-member counts vary from 2 on Free to 50 on Enterprise.

facts.label: Public subscriber capacity
facts.value: Public plan subscriber limits are Free 100, Hobby 250, Startup 1,000, Business 5,000, Enterprise 25,000.

facts.label: Private page employee capacity
facts.value: Private plan employee-viewer allowances are Starter 50, Growth 300, Corporate 1,000, Enterprise 5,000. Team-member quotas are respectively 5, 15, 35, and 50.

facts.label: Audience-specific page capacity
facts.value: Base tier includes 500 users, 10 groups, 25 team members, and 30 metrics. Later tier price steps are published, but later tier capacities are not mapped in the page.

facts.label: Page count and billing
facts.value: Multiple pages can be managed from one account, but each page is independently subscribed and billed.

facts.label: Product contracting entity
facts.value: Current product-specific terms name Dogwood Labs, Inc., d/b/a StatusPage.io, as the Statuspage contracting entity. The general Atlassian Customer Agreement supplements those terms.

facts.label: Buyer eligibility
facts.value: No complete list of eligible or excluded buyer countries was located in the product terms, customer agreement, or pricing page checked.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Publishes current service status, incidents, scheduled maintenance, uptime history, and metrics to external customers, internal employees, or selected customer groups. It communicates status; it is not a direct website or server monitor.

facts.label: Hosted option
facts.value: Statuspage is provided as pages hosted by Atlassian.

facts.label: Complete self-hosted option
facts.value: A complete self-hosted Statuspage edition is not offered in the current product or pricing pages checked.

facts.label: SDK and language support
facts.value: No application instrumentation SDK is required for the core status-page service. It accepts status changes through its management API, email automation, and integrations rather than instrumenting application code.

facts.label: Public plan notification channels
facts.value: Free and Hobby list email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. Startup, Business, and Enterprise add SMS and webhook to email, Slack, and Teams.

facts.label: Private plan notification channels
facts.value: Starter lists email. Growth, Corporate, and Enterprise list email, SMS, and webhook notifications.

facts.label: Audience-specific notification channels
facts.value: Audience-specific pricing lists email, SMS, and webhook notifications.

facts.label: Notification message charges
facts.value: Public pricing FAQ says all plans include unlimited notifications and there is no extra notification charge; the types vary by plan. SMS is listed as a plan feature, not a separate per-message rate.

facts.label: SMS country support
facts.value: Atlassian lists full SMS support for the United States, Canada, Great Britain, Australia, Israel, Belgium, Sweden, Switzerland, Norway, Poland, and Germany. The page flags Japan and India as potentially unreliable and other countries as variable.

facts.label: Per-event notification choices
facts.value: When creating or updating an incident or scheduled maintenance, the publisher may choose whether to notify. The docs list event-specific Email, SMS, Webhook, and Slack triggers; component status changes notify only through Webhook and Slack in the matrix.

facts.label: Component subscription filtering
facts.value: Component subscriptions let subscribers choose only the components they care about; pricing gates it on public Business and higher named public tiers, and on private Growth and above.

facts.label: Incident lifecycle and escalation
facts.value: Incidents support Investigating, Identified, Monitoring, and Resolved states, with publisher-written updates. Scheduled maintenance and postmortems are supported. The docs checked do not describe automatic paging escalation or incident-response on-call rotations within Statuspage.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Hosted web application and hosted status pages. It does not require an agent or probe installed in a customer's application or server for page operation.

facts.label: Manual status updates
facts.value: Administrators can publish incidents, maintenance, component states, and metrics from the management interface.

facts.label: Management and read APIs
facts.value: Manage API can create and update components, incidents, subscribers, metrics, team members, and other page data; it is limited to 60 requests per minute. Status API exposes page status for embeds and client integrations and is not rate-limited per the support article.

facts.label: API credential caveat
facts.value: Private and trial Status API requests require an Authorization header. Atlassian says there is no read-only API key; a key has full read/write scope, so its docs recommend a proxy rather than exposing it in browser code.

facts.label: Automated status-update paths
facts.value: Statuspage supports email automation, its API, and integrations that update components or create incidents. The user guide names PagerDuty, Pingdom, New Relic, Opsgenie, xMatters, VictorOps, and Pingometer; metrics integrations include Pingdom, New Relic, Datadog, and Librato.

facts.label: Direct monitoring input
facts.value: Direct website/server monitoring and raw logs, traces, or error-event ingestion are not the product's input model; customers or integrated monitoring tools must provide status updates.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: A typical setup is to choose a page type, add components, invite team members, set the page's timezone and visibility/customization, configure subscribers and integrations, then publish an incident or test update.

facts.label: Public page visibility and branding
facts.value: Public pages are visible without authentication. A custom domain is available on paid public plans but not Free; SSL is included on all plans. Free uses a statuspage.io subdomain.

facts.label: Public page plan ladder
facts.value: Free $0 includes 100 subscribers, 25 components, 2 team members, 2 metrics. Hobby $29/month: 250 subscribers, 5 team members, 5 metrics. Startup $99/month: 1,000 subscribers, 10 team members, 10 metrics. Business $399/month: 5,000 subscribers, 25 team members, 25 metrics. Enterprise $1,499/month: 25,000 subscribers, 50 team members, 50 metrics.

facts.label: Public branding and controls by tier
facts.value: Hobby includes basic customization and custom domain; Startup adds custom CSS; Business and Enterprise include CSS/HTML/JS. Business and Enterprise add component subscriptions and role-based access control.

facts.label: Private page visibility and domain
facts.value: Private pages require an authenticated viewer. The custom-domain guide says private pages cannot use a custom domain.

facts.label: Private page plan ladder
facts.value: Starter $79/month: 50 employees, 5 team members, 5 metrics. Growth $249/month: 300 employees, 15 team members, 15 metrics. Corporate $599/month: 1,000 employees, 35 team members, 35 metrics. Enterprise $1,499/month: 5,000 employees, 50 team members, 50 metrics.

facts.label: Private-page feature gates
facts.value: Starter lists email, custom CSS, incident templates, team SSO, email support. Growth adds SMS/webhook, CSS/HTML/JS, component subscriptions, and IP allowlisting. Corporate adds RBAC and eligible yearly PO/invoicing. Enterprise adds alerting integrations and account-representative support.

facts.label: Audience-specific page access
facts.value: Audience-specific pages use user and group permissions to show selected components and information and determine notifications. Users can be assigned to one or more audiences; the guide formerly called the feature “Access control.”

facts.label: Audience-specific page plan and branding
facts.value: Base price $300/month includes 500 users, 10 groups, 25 team members, and 30 metrics; features include email/SMS/webhooks, CSS/HTML/JS, Manage API, SSO, and component subscriptions.

facts.label: Audience-specific higher tier domain condition
facts.value: Audience-specific pages can use a custom domain except when single sign-on is enabled.

facts.label: Public subscriber types
facts.value: Public pages can accept email and, on eligible plans, SMS and webhook subscriptions. Slack and Microsoft Teams are notification integrations, not the same subscriber types as an email or phone number.

facts.label: Subscriber counting
facts.value: Active paid plans count only active subscribers toward the limit; quarantined, unconfirmed, and deleted do not count. Trial pages count active, quarantined, unconfirmed, and deleted records against the 25 cap.

facts.label: Notification triggers
facts.value: Incident creation, updates, resolution, scheduled maintenance, and postmortem events each have channel-specific triggers. Component-status changes do not send Email or SMS according to the published matrix, but do send Webhook and Slack.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications and cost
facts.value: All plans are advertised with unlimited notification count; email/SMS/webhook channel availability is plan-specific and SMS delivery varies by country.

facts.label: Manual status source
facts.value: Administrators create and update incidents and component status through the page interface; incidents have the four published lifecycle states.

facts.label: Automated status source
facts.value: Updates can be triggered by email automation, the Manage API, or supported monitoring and incident tools. Separate metric integrations can display selected upstream metrics.

facts.label: Incident history and postmortems
facts.value: Incident pages retain published updates; history becomes available after the page has been operational for 14 days. Postmortems can be attached after resolution. A maximum incident-history duration is not published in the docs checked.

facts.label: Subscriber export
facts.value: Page admins can export email, SMS, and webhook subscribers to CSV or JSON, delivered by email. Slack subscribers are not among the export types in the guide.

facts.label: Incident and component export path
facts.value: Management API provides access to incidents, components, metrics, and related page objects. No one-click full-page archive export was found in the API, user guide, or export articles checked.

facts.label: Page deletion timeline
facts.value: A page deletion has a 60-day cancellation window; the page is suspended during the process, then deletion is processed after the window and may take up to 24 more hours.

facts.label: Subscriber personal information
facts.value: Statuspage can collect email addresses and phone numbers to send notifications; the product-specific terms treat end-user information and page configurations as Customer Data.

facts.label: Sensitive-data filtering and masking
facts.value: Product and security pages checked do not publish Statuspage-specific controls to mask or redact personal data in incident text, subscriber records, or page configuration.

facts.label: Data-processing agreement
facts.value: Atlassian publishes a Data Processing Addendum effective August 17, 2026.

facts.label: Hosting and processing providers
facts.value: Atlassian says Statuspage runs on its AWS-backed Micros/PaaS platform. Its subprocessor list identifies service providers for Statuspage, including communications processors; listed processing locations do not establish a customer's selected storage region.

facts.label: Statuspage data residency
facts.value: Atlassian's residency guide lists data-pinning support by product and does not list Statuspage among the eligible apps shown. The pages checked do not publish a Statuspage-specific selectable storage region or pinning option.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Atlassian Statuspage; current official product URL is https://www.atlassian.com/software/statuspage. The product terms use the contracted name Statuspage and the entity name StatusPage.io.

facts.label: Former name and ownership change
facts.value: Statuspage joined Atlassian in an acquisition announced July 14, 2016.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: Product, pricing, help, and legal pages are active. Current pricing lists current public, private, and audience-specific plan offers.

facts.label: Acquisition, shutdown, or sunset notices
facts.value: The only acquisition found is Atlassian's 2016 acquisition. No shutdown or sunset notice was located in the current pricing, Statuspage blog archive, Statuspage article board, company-news archive, or current product terms checked.

facts.label: Product changelog coverage
facts.value: Atlassian's organization administration article says Statuspage release notes are not included in the regular app-update feed. I did not find a separate public Statuspage changelog in the product resources or article archive checked.

facts.label: Separate JSM status-page feature
facts.value: Jira Service Management announced its own native status-page capability in 2026. The announcement concerns JSM, not retirement of Statuspage.

facts.label: API-key migration deadline conflict
facts.value: The current support article says old keys will be deprecated and query-string api_key use discontinued June 30, 2026. An Atlassian announcement dated April 23, 2026 says query-string use ends May 15, 2026. Both deadlines have passed; no later correction was located.

facts.label: Software license and source code
facts.value: No customer-downloadable or self-hosted Statuspage software license or official complete-service repository is published on the product, pricing, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Documentation and support
facts.value: Public docs and user guide are available. Free explicitly includes Atlassian Community support. Private pricing lists email support for Starter through Enterprise; Private Enterprise also lists an account representative.

facts.label: Public paid support entitlement
facts.value: The public pricing table does not clearly specify a response-time commitment or a per-tier support response target for paid plans.

facts.label: Smallest ongoing paid option
facts.value: PAYG is the public usage-based option; no Application Insights-specific minimum monthly commitment is stated on the public rate page.

facts.label: Paid-plan feature boundary
facts.value: Standard tests are billed per scheduled run; App Insights telemetry ingestion and retention remain separate workspace meters.

facts.label: Daily ingestion cap
facts.value: Default Application Insights cap is 100 GB/day; the portal can raise it to 1,000 GB/day, and higher capacity requires Microsoft support.

facts.label: Ingestion throttling
facts.value: Service limit lists 32,000 events/second, measured over a minute; higher limit requires support contact.

facts.label: What happens at the daily cap
facts.value: Telemetry beyond the cap is ignored for the rest of the UTC day; normal collection resumes at the start of the next day.

facts.label: Cost after exceeding allowance
facts.value: Ingested volume above the free allowance is billed at the regional PAYG rate unless the cap or another limit stops it; rates and contractual discounts vary.

facts.label: Hard spend control
facts.value: Application Insights daily data cap stops ingestion after the configured volume; it is not a dollar-denominated subscription cap.

facts.label: Azure budget alerts
facts.value: Budgets can notify at configured cost/forecast thresholds but do not stop resource usage or charges.

facts.label: Per-resource usage controls
facts.value: Sampling and the App Insights daily cap can reduce or stop telemetry ingestion; no per-app monthly spend cap was found.

facts.label: Raw log retention choices
facts.value: App Insights log data can be retained 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 270, 365, 550, or 730 days; over 90 days can incur retention cost.

facts.label: Aggregated metrics retention
facts.value: Metrics Explorer aggregates are retained at one-minute granularity for 90 days.

facts.label: Debug snapshot retention
facts.value: Debug snapshots are retained for 15 days.

facts.label: Retention extension price
facts.value: Numeric East US/USD cost for retention beyond 90 days was not readable on the current price page; extra retention is billable.

facts.label: People and access
facts.value: Azure role-based access control governs who can view and manage the resource; no App Insights seat price is listed.

facts.label: App/resource counts
facts.value: Application Insights resources are Azure resources; no fixed account-wide app or project limit for this product was published in the pages checked.

facts.label: Availability-test count
facts.value: Up to 100 availability tests per Application Insights resource.

facts.label: Vendor home region
facts.value: Microsoft Corporation is headquartered in the United States

facts.label: Buyer eligibility
facts.value: Azure account availability and free-account eligibility depend on the customer's billing country; no Application Insights-only country list was found

facts.label: Main job
facts.value: Collects, analyzes, and displays application performance and diagnostic telemetry; includes failure, performance, search, and transaction views

facts.label: Adjacent signals
facts.value: Collects logs/traces and supports browser real-user telemetry; availability tests monitor public HTTP/HTTPS endpoints

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Application Insights backend is Microsoft-hosted. Customer-run SDKs/agents send telemetry but do not host the backend.

facts.label: Supported server languages
facts.value: Current supported OpenTelemetry distros: .NET, Node.js, Python, and Java. Classic APIs and framework-specific auto-instrumentation remain separate migration paths.

facts.label: Browser JavaScript
facts.value: Official Application Insights JavaScript SDK instruments browser apps for page views, usage, performance and exceptions; it is not the OpenTelemetry web SDK.

facts.label: Framework and platform coverage
facts.value: Docs cover Azure App Service, Functions, VMs, containers/Kubernetes, and supported apps in other hosting environments; code-based instrumentation or supported automatic attach is required.

facts.label: Mobile platforms
facts.value: Application Insights has mobile/browser telemetry paths, but a current standalone native crash-monitoring SDK support matrix was not found in the app overview or SDK documentation checked.

facts.label: Built-in smart-detection email
facts.value: Smart Detection can email failure/performance anomaly notifications when sufficient telemetry exists; recipients and rule settings can be changed.

facts.label: Action Group channels
facts.value: Azure Monitor Action Groups document email/SMS, push/voice, webhook, Azure Function, Logic App, Automation Runbook, ITSM and related actions.

facts.label: Alert delivery charges
facts.value: Azure Monitor pricing treats some notification types and alert rules as separately billable; exact notification charges depend on action type and usage.

facts.label: SMS/voice price by country
facts.value: Country-specific SMS/voice limits and public delivery charges could not be established as a single App Insights rate; pricing depends on the Azure Monitor notification meter and destination country.

facts.label: Automatic failure alerts
facts.value: Smart Detection detects unusual failure-rate changes and links to related requests, exceptions, dependencies and traces.

facts.label: Custom alert conditions
facts.value: Metric and log-query alert rules can target availability, failures, metrics or custom KQL conditions; action groups choose delivery.

facts.label: Suppression and planned maintenance
facts.value: Alert processing/suppression rules and temporary disabling of rules/tests are documented; ongoing maintenance calendars with recurring on-call suppression were not found.

facts.label: On-call escalation schedule
facts.value: No native person rotation, acknowledgement escalation ladder, or on-call schedule is described in the Application Insights alerts, Action Groups, or pricing docs checked.

facts.label: Cloud and on-prem deployment
facts.value: Instrumented services can run on Azure, other cloud providers, or on-premises; telemetry is sent to Microsoft's hosted backend.

facts.label: Containers/serverless
facts.value: Microsoft documents Application Insights instrumentation for Azure Functions, App Service, containers and AKS; collector support and setup differ by runtime.

facts.label: Private network ingestion/query
facts.value: Application Insights supports Azure Monitor Private Link for supported ingestion/query paths; workspace associations and private query settings must be configured.

facts.label: Standard-test network fit
facts.value: Standard availability tests probe publicly reachable HTTP/HTTPS endpoints. For nonpublic endpoints, docs advise monitoring an internal signal from inside the network rather than using a private test agent.

facts.label: Current ingestion path
facts.value: Current server instrumentation uses Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro for .NET, Node.js and Python, and Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro for Java; browser apps use the Application Insights JavaScript SDK.

facts.label: OpenTelemetry signal support
facts.value: Azure Monitor exporter/distro supports sending telemetry using OpenTelemetry protocols and SDK conventions; support varies by language and signal.

facts.label: Manual/custom telemetry
facts.value: SDK and OpenTelemetry APIs can send custom events, metrics, spans and log records; telemetry can be enriched or filtered before export.

facts.label: Legacy ingestion/authentication
facts.value: Instrumentation-key-only global ingestion is deprecated; connection strings are recommended. Query API keys are a separate authentication feature with unresolved post-March-2026 enforcement status.

facts.label: SDK support policy
facts.value: Microsoft publishes Application Insights SDK support guidance and advises updating unsupported/old SDK versions; current SDK versions and language policies differ.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Create a workspace-based resource and select/link a Log Analytics workspace; add the appropriate language SDK or enable supported auto-instrumentation; configure its connection string; verify incoming telemetry and add alerts as needed.

facts.label: Error capture
facts.value: Application Insights collects exception/crash telemetry, failed requests and failed dependency calls when supported instrumentation is enabled.

facts.label: Failure grouping and issue lifecycle
facts.value: Failures view groups and analyzes failed operations and related telemetry, but the checked product docs do not document a persistent issue-deduplication, merge, assignment or resolve lifecycle like a dedicated bug tracker.

facts.label: Error volume and sampling
facts.value: Source-level sampling can lower error/trace volume; ingestion sampling may also drop data and make failures or traces incomplete. No grouped-issue dropped-event counter was found.

facts.label: Stack traces and code context
facts.value: Exception details can show stack traces and related request/dependency/trace telemetry; support varies by runtime and instrumentation.

facts.label: Browser source maps
facts.value: JavaScript/Node exception stacks can be unminified using source maps stored in a linked Azure Blob container; the container and access must be configured.

facts.label: Native symbolication
facts.value: A current native iOS/Android symbol-upload or crash-symbolication workflow was not established in the SDK, FAQ, or overview pages checked.

facts.label: Release and deployment context
facts.value: Deployment/release annotations and version metadata can be associated with telemetry; current Azure Pipelines release annotation methods are documented.

facts.label: Classic release annotation API
facts.value: Classic release annotation/API-key path is legacy and affected by old API-key retirement guidance; migrate integrations to current documented release annotations.

facts.label: Fix/regression tracking
facts.value: Application Insights shows version/deployment context but no issue-level regression, assignment or fixed-version workflow was found in the failures and release docs checked.

facts.label: User and request context
facts.value: Telemetry can include operation/correlation IDs, user/session, device, browser and custom properties depending on SDK/configuration.

facts.label: Session replay
facts.value: No session replay or recorded screen/video feature was found in the Application Insights product, browser SDK, or pricing pages checked.

facts.label: Request and dependency diagnosis
facts.value: Performance and transaction diagnostics link requests to dependency calls, traces and related failures; Application Map shows connected components.

facts.label: Distributed trace view
facts.value: End-to-end transaction diagnostics correlate spans/operations across components; Application Insights supports OpenTelemetry-based tracing.

facts.label: Live performance diagnostics
facts.value: Live Metrics provides near-real-time application telemetry; profiler and snapshot debugger are separate code-level tools with specific runtime/support conditions.

facts.label: Slow database query diagnosis
facts.value: Dependency telemetry can identify slow/failing database and HTTP calls when the SDK can instrument the client library; profiler detail varies by stack.

facts.label: Sampling options
facts.value: OpenTelemetry supports fixed-rate and rate-limited trace sampling; sampler and defaults vary by language/distro version.

facts.label: Trace integrity and logs
facts.value: Application Insights sampling uses trace-aware decisions; logs may follow trace sampling depending on language defaults; metrics are not sampled.

facts.label: Data billing basis
facts.value: Ingestion charges use measured telemetry data volume after collection/sampling; request counts alone do not yield an exact monthly price.

facts.label: Browser real-user monitoring
facts.value: JavaScript SDK supports real-user monitoring including page views, browser performance, client-side exceptions and AJAX/fetch dependency telemetry.

facts.label: Mobile real-user monitoring
facts.value: No current native mobile real-user monitoring allowance, supported app matrix or session-based price was established in the product/SDK pages checked.

facts.label: Current check type
facts.value: Standard availability test sends HTTP/HTTPS requests to a publicly reachable endpoint; supports status/content criteria, request method, body, headers, redirects and optional dependent-resource loading.

facts.label: TLS and certificate check
facts.value: Standard test validates TLS/SSL certificate validity and can fail at a configured pre-expiry lifetime threshold; it validates the final redirected URL.

facts.label: URL Ping legacy test
facts.value: URL Ping is a deprecated single-step HTTP/HTTPS check that remains available until September 30, 2028, when existing tests are removed.

facts.label: Unsupported private, DNS and port checks
facts.value: Standard tests require reachable web endpoints; docs do not describe dedicated DNS, TCP-port, or private test-agent checks. For private targets Microsoft recommends an internal health signal and alert.

facts.label: Standard test frequency
facts.value: Default test interval is five minutes per location; with five locations a site is tested on average every minute.

facts.label: Timeout
facts.value: Test timeout is configurable; a response or dependent resource not received within the chosen period is a failure. A universal default/minimum timeout was not stated in the page checked.

facts.label: Probe selection and counting
facts.value: Up to 16 locations per Standard test; Microsoft recommends at least five. Each location runs on the configured frequency and contributes test executions.

facts.label: Example probe geographies
facts.value: Listed Standard test locations include Australia East, Brazil South, several US regions, East Asia, Japan East, North/West Europe, Southeast Asia, UK and sovereign-cloud locations.

facts.label: Private test agents
facts.value: No private probe agent is documented; tests run from Microsoft probe locations. Internal/no-ingress targets should emit a health metric/log from within the network.

facts.label: Failure confirmation
facts.value: Optional retry mode reports failure only after three successive failed attempts, independently at each test location.

facts.label: Alert location threshold
facts.value: Availability alert guidance recommends a minimum threshold of 3/5 locations; alert logic can require multiple locations to agree.

facts.label: Maintenance behavior
facts.value: Tests can be disabled during maintenance; alert rules can be disabled or customized for planned downtime.

facts.label: TLS certificate expiry
facts.value: Standard tests support certificate validity and proactive failure before a configured certificate expiry window.

facts.label: Domain expiration
facts.value: No registrar-level domain expiration monitoring or renewal reminder feature was found in the availability, product or pricing pages checked.

facts.label: Customer status page
facts.value: Application Insights is not documented as a public customer-facing status-page hosting service.

facts.label: Status-page subscribers
facts.value: No external subscriber list or customer outage-notification feature is documented for Application Insights.

facts.label: Status updates and incident history
facts.value: No customer status-page incident posting or public incident history workflow is documented.

facts.label: Scheduled job monitor
facts.value: Application Insights can receive custom telemetry/metrics from jobs, but a dedicated missed-cron heartbeat monitor with grace windows is not documented.

facts.label: Job failure signals
facts.value: No dedicated missed ping, start/finish signal, or job-run history product is documented in the App Insights product/SDK guides checked.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable: no self-hosted Application Insights backend is offered; only customer-side SDKs, agents, or app code are installed.

facts.label: Query and export
facts.value: Telemetry is queryable through Application Insights/Log Analytics experiences and query APIs; workspace diagnostic settings can route supported data to destinations such as Storage or Event Hubs.

facts.label: Purge and deletion
facts.value: Purge APIs can delete selected telemetry matching supported filters; deleting an Application Insights resource removes the resource, while workspace data follows workspace lifecycle/retention.

facts.label: Continuous Export
facts.value: The classic Continuous Export feature is retired; use workspace-based diagnostic settings or supported query/export tools.

facts.label: Data portability and API query retirement
facts.value: Query access is available via supported REST APIs, but API-key authentication has a retirement notice; current enforcement and any extension are unclear.

facts.label: Data collected
facts.value: Typical telemetry includes requests, dependencies, exceptions/crashes, performance counters, client/server context, traces, and custom events/metrics.

facts.label: IP address handling
facts.value: Client IP may be used for geolocation, then the stored IP field is zeroed by default.

facts.label: Sensitive request content
facts.value: POST bodies are not logged automatically; custom request/response body logging can expose personal data and increase ingestion cost.

facts.label: Telemetry filtering
facts.value: SDK telemetry processors and OpenTelemetry processors can filter, modify or enrich telemetry before it reaches the service; ingestion transformations are also documented.

facts.label: Browser identifiers and cookies
facts.value: JavaScript SDK supports cookie/session configuration and disabling cookie use; browser user/session identifiers can be collected when enabled.

facts.label: Data location
facts.value: Application Insights data is stored in the Azure region selected when the resource is created; moving a resource and its historical data to another region is not supported.

facts.label: DPA and privacy terms
facts.value: Microsoft publishes a Data Protection Addendum for covered online services and a privacy statement; exact contractual commitments depend on the customer's agreement and service terms.

facts.label: Data residency promise beyond resource region
facts.value: No additional Application Insights-specific selectable residency guarantee beyond the Azure resource/workspace region was found in the DPA, service FAQ, Azure region guide or product terms checked.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Azure Monitor Application Insights; Application Insights is a capability within the Azure Monitor family

facts.label: Current product status
facts.value: Active hosted product; no whole-product shutdown or acquisition notice found in current official checks

facts.label: Classic resource retirement
facts.value: Classic Application Insights ingestion stopped June 15, 2025. Automatic migration attempts are complete; remaining classic resources must be converted manually to workspace-based resources to resume ingestion. Existing data remains queryable.

facts.label: .NET Classic API SDK 2.x
facts.value: Deprecated; retires March 31, 2027. Microsoft recommends migration to OpenTelemetry-based SDK 3.x or preferably its OpenTelemetry distro.

facts.label: Node.js Classic API SDK 2.x
facts.value: Retired; migrate to the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro or current Application Insights SDK 3.x path

facts.label: URL Ping test retirement
facts.value: Deprecated; retirement moved from September 30, 2026 to September 30, 2028. Existing tests are removed on the revised date; migrate to Standard tests and verify alert cutover.

facts.label: Multi-step web test retirement
facts.value: Microsoft Q&A answers state an August 31, 2024 retirement and migration date; the current pricing page still lists a monthly multi-step test meter. Current availability and enforcement are unresolved.

facts.label: Query API keys
facts.value: Scheduled retirement date was March 31, 2026; Microsoft says to use Microsoft Entra ID. Current enforcement status could not be confirmed because the date has passed while current Advisor guidance still says the keys are retiring.

facts.label: Continuous Export retirement
facts.value: Classic Continuous Export was disabled May 15, 2024; use workspace-based resources and diagnostic settings/export paths instead.

facts.label: Backend license and source
facts.value: No self-hosted Application Insights backend source or license is offered in the product and deployment docs checked. Open-source SDKs are clients, not the service.

facts.label: Public documentation
facts.value: Product guides, FAQs, SDK support notes, API references and migration pages are publicly available.

facts.label: Technical support options
facts.value: Azure provides paid support plans and subscription support channels; no Application Insights-specific response-time promise is established in product docs.

facts.label: Community help
facts.value: Microsoft Learn Q&A supports public Azure Monitor questions, but response time is not guaranteed.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable to the hosted backend; customers still maintain their own SDK/agent and app deployment versions.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: The self-hosted software has no license or subscription fee. The operator pays for any Hub host, monitored systems, storage, backups, and external notification services they choose.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Yes. MIT-licensed Hub and Agent can be used on an ongoing basis, including commercially; there is no vendor account quota or paid tier described.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: A vendor-hosted evaluation trial does not apply to the self-hosted project; no hosted service is offered in the reviewed official sources.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: No paid hosted plan applies to this self-hosted open-source edition.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Beszel does not meter vendor-hosted usage in the self-hosted edition. Local disk capacity, hardware, and configured retention determine local resource limits.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Network monitor configuration permits intervals from 1 to 3600 seconds; the docs do not describe a paid overage or run cap.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: A spending cap, usage-bill alert, or automatic bill stop does not apply to a self-hosted edition with no vendor bill.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: 1m system and container statistics are retained for 1 hour.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: 10m system and container statistics are retained for 12 hours.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: 20m system and container statistics are retained for 24 hours.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: 120m system and container statistics are retained for 7 days.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: 480m system and container statistics are retained for 30 days.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: When an account's alert history exceeds 250 records, the Hub prunes it to the newest 200 records for that user.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Systemd service details show the last 200 journal lines; the journal itself remains under the host operating system's retention policy.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: I found no published retention duration for network monitor samples in the network monitoring guide or current deletion code checked.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: The Hub supports multi-user accounts, administrator sharing, and read-only access to shared systems.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: OAuth2 and OIDC login are supported; automatic OAuth user creation is disabled by default and can be enabled with a Hub setting.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: No maximum number of users, systems, or projects is stated in the account, getting-started, or installation docs reviewed.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: Official sources reviewed do not publish a company operator, maintainer country, or buyer-country restrictions. The public repository is under an individual maintainer account.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Collects host CPU, memory, swap, ZFS ARC, disk capacity and I/O, network traffic, load, temperature, fan, GPU, and battery metrics.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Collects CPU, memory, network, status, and health metrics for Docker and Podman containers.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Shows S.M.A.R.T. disk health, eMMC wear, Linux mdraid health where available, and ZFS/Btrfs pool health, capacity, and I/O.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: GPU collection can report utilization, temperature, memory, and power for supported Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Jetson, and experimental Apple Silicon paths.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Additional disks, partitions, and remote mounts can be added; network-mounted filesystems do not provide disk I/O statistics.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Provides systemd service state, resource use, restart counts, lifecycle and recent journal logs.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Agents can probe ICMP, TCP, HTTP, and DNS targets and report response time and packet loss.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Self-hosted only in the reviewed official offer: install a Hub and run an Agent on each monitored system. No vendor-operated hosted plan is advertised in the site or documentation.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: The Hub can run as a Docker/Podman container or a binary; the Agent can run as a container or an installed binary/package.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Beszel uses host Agents and native OS/container collectors; the docs do not offer application-language SDKs for instrumenting app exceptions.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Notification adapters include Generic webhooks, Bark, Discord, Gotify, Google Chat, IFTTT, Lark, Mattermost, Matrix, MQTT, ntfy, OpsGenie, Pushbullet, Pushover, Rocket.Chat, Signal, Slack, Teams, Telegram, Twilio, WeCom, and Zulip.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Beszel publishes no channel-credit charge; any provider, SMS, hosting, or messaging cost is billed by the external service the operator configures.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Threshold alerts can be configured for most system metrics, and alerts can be enabled or disabled for each system.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Documented system alert types include CPU, memory, bandwidth, disk use, temperature, load averages, GPU, battery, and CPU state.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Container health alerts can include recent log excerpts in notifications.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: A network monitor loss alert uses packet loss over the past hour; the default threshold is 5%, it needs at least three probes, and it resolves at or below the configured threshold.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: S.M.A.R.T. failure and worsening storage-pool health can notify automatically; the docs say those conditions are not currently configurable in the same way as metric thresholds.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: The docs reviewed describe thresholds, notifications, quiet-hour settings in the project release history, but do not document incident acknowledgement, escalation schedules, or alert grouping.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Users can set quiet hours for notification suppression; one-time windows that have ended are removed by the Hub.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Hub deployment options are Docker, Podman, or a standalone binary.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Agents are available as containers, standalone binaries, or platform packages, including Windows and macOS package-manager paths, Linux/FreeBSD installs, and a Home Assistant add-on.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: The Agent can monitor local systems and private-network targets; the setup guide says the Hub need not be exposed publicly for basic monitoring.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Docker and Podman are supported for the Hub and Agent. Host monitoring features may need host networking, read-only container socket access, or mounted system interfaces.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: The Hub supports reverse-proxy deployment; WebSocket proxying is needed for agents using universal tokens, and APP_URL is used to generate links and agent configuration.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Docker Swarm deployment is documented with one Agent in global mode per node and internal Hub-agent network examples.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: The Agent sends supported host and container metrics to the Hub using Beszel's Agent connection; a system is added in the Hub and started with its generated key and token.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Network monitor probes are configured in the Hub and run by the selected Agent using ICMP, TCP, HTTP, or DNS.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Optional heartbeat monitoring sends outbound GET, POST, or HEAD requests to an external monitoring endpoint; the feature is disabled when no URL is set.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: The docs reviewed do not describe OTLP, general syslog ingestion, application SDKs, or arbitrary log ingestion.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Install the Hub as a container or binary, persist its beszel_data directory, and access the web UI on port 8090.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Create the initial Hub administrator, add a system, and use the generated key/token values when starting the Agent.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Install the Agent on each host using Docker/Podman, binary, or available package route; configure its Hub address and credentials.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Hub and Agent provide local health commands for Docker healthchecks; the guide recommends intervals of 60 seconds or longer due to CPU overhead.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: ICMP probes report response time and packet loss; raw sockets, an allowed datagram socket, or a system ping command can provide ICMP support depending on host setup.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: TCP monitors test a target host and port; the default port is 443.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: HTTP monitors use GET, follow redirects, and treat request errors or status codes of 400 or higher as loss.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: DNS monitors test name resolution and report response behavior; the queried DNS server can be configured.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Probe interval is configurable from 1 to 3600 seconds and defaults to 30 seconds.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: ICMP, TCP, and DNS time out after 3 seconds; HTTP uses a 10-second timeout.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Each selected Agent runs its own probe. Selecting multiple systems creates one monitor per system, so results show the view from each system's network.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Private and local targets can be probed by an Agent with network access; the vendor does not publish a global probe-location network.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: A network-loss alert checks the previous hour, requires at least three probes, uses a configurable threshold (5% default), and resolves when loss falls to or below that threshold.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Pausing or deleting a network monitor stops its probes and closes its alert without sending a resolution notification.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: I found no published universal retry schedule, multi-location consensus rule, or maintenance-window behavior for network probes in the network-monitor guide.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: HTTPS network monitors check TLS certificate expiry beginning with Agent v0.21.0.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Fixed warning lead times before certificate expiry are not stated in the release notes or network-monitor guide checked.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Hub needs persistent writable storage for its beszel_data directory and listens on port 8090 by default. The project describes the Hub as PocketBase-based but publishes no numerical minimum CPU, memory, or disk size.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Agent default listen port is 45876; the Agent can use SSH or an outgoing WebSocket connection to the Hub.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: The Hub installer supports Linux and FreeBSD, Docker/Podman deployment, and manual binary compilation for any platform.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Agent install paths include Linux/FreeBSD scripts, Windows and macOS package routes, Home Assistant, and Docker/Podman. Collector availability varies by platform.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Container metrics need access to the Docker/Podman socket; host network, systemd, GPU, SMART, and storage-pool collection can need extra mounts, capabilities, devices, or utilities.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: No numeric minimum or recommended CPU, memory, or disk profile for a stated host count was found in the overview, Hub, Agent, and getting-started docs checked.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: The Hub includes backups to local disk or S3-compatible storage and can restore those backups.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: The Hub exposes PocketBase REST API access for reading and updating data; the API guide warns response structure can change in minor releases.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: No separate user-facing export format, deletion schedule, or data-erasure workflow was found in the backup, REST API, or installation docs reviewed.
