facts.label: Deployment model
facts.value: Vendor-hosted analysis/UI; runtime probe and local Agent forward performance data to Blackfire servers. Player runs on customer infrastructure.

facts.label: Runtime coverage by layer
facts.value: Deterministic profiling: PHP and Python. Continuous-profiler docs list PHP, Python, Go, Java, Ruby, Rust and Node.js.

facts.label: Current continuous-profiler requirements
facts.value: PHP >=8.2 NTS; Python >=3.7; Node.js >=16; each cited configuration requires Blackfire Agent >=2.13.

facts.label: Framework and CLI integration
facts.value: PHP/Python instrumentation; current docs describe Symfony Messenger and Laravel queue-worker auto-monitoring as opt-in beta; other CLI consumers can be instrumented manually.

facts.label: Notification channels
facts.value: Email, Slack, PagerDuty, Opsgenie and Microsoft Teams; pricing also describes webhooks. Channels are environment-specific.

facts.label: SMS / phone charges and delivery terms
facts.value: No native SMS/call credit bundle, country tariff, per-notification price or contractual delivery time found in pricing, notifier docs or terms.

facts.label: Thresholds, routing and escalation
facts.value: Warning/alarm thresholds with duration; alarm takes precedence. Filter by transaction, HTTP code/method/host or machine; choose channels; escalate after configurable unchanged/changed state duration.

facts.label: Frontend alerting
facts.value: Backend alert interface also supports browser throughput, TTFB, FCP, LCP, CLS and INP.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Customer probe/Agent on local machines and servers; Linux/macOS/Windows configurations documented; Docker/CI runner for Player; private/VPN targets reachable from customer runner.

facts.label: Profiler coexistence limits
facts.value: Installer warns about conflicts with XHProf, Pinba, Suhosin and Uopz; consider disabling XDebug or pcov when profiling.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Language probe sends raw performance data to Agent, which forwards to Blackfire. CP uses runtime profilers through Agent; browser key/snippet sends frontend observations.

facts.label: Generic OTLP / syslog ingest
facts.value: No public general OTLP or syslog ingest endpoint for arbitrary third-party traces/logs found in the docs index, architecture/configuration, monitoring or CP guides.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Create paid organization/environment; install language probe and Agent, configure credentials; add CLI/browser profiling client; enable/sample monitoring. CP requires separate runtime profiler setup.

facts.label: Frontend and synthetic setup
facts.value: Enable frontend at organization/environment, use browser key and automatic PHP/Python script injection or manual snippet. For synthetics write .bkf scenario and run Player --report with client credentials and environment.

facts.label: Slow request and dependency diagnosis
facts.value: Simple request metrics, extended spans/SQL/service calls and deeper function-level deterministic CPU/I/O/memory/network profiles; dependency service break-down and top-impact calls.

facts.label: Continuous flame graphs
facts.value: Runtime-specific probabilistic function samples; flame graph/table/split views and timeframe comparison.

facts.label: Automatic profiling and deployment context
facts.value: Automatically profile ten most impactful named transactions once/day; Profile Next Request can capture one matching request. Monitoring timeline accepts deployment/event markers.

facts.label: Backend sampling and counting
facts.value: Configurable per-environment base percentage; selected request counts as one monitoring trace. Extended sample rate chooses extra span detail from selected traces.

facts.label: CP sampling and GB definition
facts.value: CP is probabilistic; Node example defaults to 100 Hz and 45,000 ms collection, Python period defaults 45 seconds. Billable GB's raw/compressed/binary basis and host-to-GB conversion were not found.

facts.label: Real-user browser performance
facts.value: TTFB, FCP, LCP, CLS, INP, page resources and geography; per-visit traces and SPA/multi-page journey; frontend transaction names correlate to same-named backend transactions.

facts.label: RUM allowance and sampling
facts.value: One million frontend observations/month in rate card; usage docs count browser traces. Environment browser sample rate chooses percentage of requests; quota may be expanded separately.

facts.label: Synthetic types and assertions
facts.value: Player is an HTTP crawler/scenario client: visit, click links, submit forms, inspect status/body/DOM and add backend performance assertions. Customer runner reaches private/VPN endpoints.

facts.label: Frequency and timeout
facts.value: Current checks run on the customer's schedule/CI; no vendor-operated minimum interval or per-check timeout promise found in current Player/synthetic docs.

facts.label: Locations / counting
facts.value: Where the customer runs Player determines location and private reachability. Profiles/reports use Blackfire entitlement; no current vendor-managed public location list or full-flow run tariff is advertised.

facts.label: Failure and maintenance
facts.value: Assertions fail scenarios; CLI exits 64 for scenario failure, 65 fatal error and 66 non-fatal error. Customer pipeline/scheduler handles pause windows and reruns.

facts.label: Expiry warnings
facts.value: No dedicated certificate/domain-expiry monitor, warning window or DNS-expiry feature found in current synthetic docs, Player reference, pricing or docs index.

facts.label: Complete self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the vendor-operated backend reviewed; local Agent/probe and MIT Player are client components.

facts.label: Export and sharing
facts.value: Player supports JSON output and report links; deterministic profile performance summaries can be copied as images; public profile/comparison embeds use oEmbed.

facts.label: Complete telemetry export
facts.value: No documented bulk raw monitoring/CP/browser export format, read API with rate limits or archive destination found in index, pricing, usage, dashboard or sharing docs.

facts.label: Profile and account deletion
facts.value: Owned profiles can be batch-deleted irreversibly. Terms allow deleting plans at any time and terminate access; privacy notice provides account-setting access/update/deletion requests and DPO/support contact.

facts.label: Purge timing / recoverability
facts.value: Terms say provider deletes the Plan without undue delay after termination; no precise backup-purge deadline or post-cancel raw-data export grace period found.

facts.label: Default profiling minimization
facts.value: SQL/HTTP arguments and credentials anonymized before hosted submission; no source code, database contents or user-session data collected by ordinary profiler; method/class/file names and resource metrics are collected.

facts.label: Debug add-on exception
facts.value: Opt-in debugging disables pruning/anonymization for selected requests and can include SQL argument values; prepared SQL statement arguments remain uncollected.

facts.label: Frontend privacy model
facts.value: Vendor says browser monitoring/analytics sets no cookies and stores no PII or tracked individual identity; trace view can still show anonymous visit journey, device/browser, country and resource URLs.

facts.label: Transport and visibility
facts.value: Encrypted SSL transport; keyed Agent access; profiles private unless explicitly shared publicly.

facts.label: Storage-location evidence
facts.value: FAQ names an Amazon data center; legal notice says the commercial website is hosted in Ireland. No specific current telemetry region or customer-selectable region found.

facts.label: DPA and data terms
facts.value: Blackfire FAQ says it is not an end-user-data processor and no DPA is necessary; standalone terms prohibit personal data in submitted content. Current unified privacy notice covers account/contact data and international transfers.

facts.label: Identity
facts.value: Blackfire / Blackfire.io; https://www.blackfire.io/; operated by Platform.sh SAS doing business as Upsun.

facts.label: Ownership
facts.value: Acquisition by Platform.sh completed in July 2021; current parent brand is Upsun.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: Current standalone Development and Production subscriptions remain advertised; acquisition page says available independently of hosting.

facts.label: Hosted synthetic sunset
facts.value: Blackfire-hosted periodic builds, webhook-triggered builds and native build integrations removed May 30, 2026; migrate to customer-run Player --report.

facts.label: Personal Agent sunset
facts.value: Personal Agent is sunset; complete removal announced for December 2026. Every paid plan now includes a Sandbox environment.

facts.label: Hosted service license
facts.value: Commercial proprietary service; limited subscription rights, provider retains service IP; customer retains submitted content ownership.

facts.label: PHP SDK license
facts.value: MIT; official blackfireio/php-sdk repository.

facts.label: Player license
facts.value: MIT; official blackfireio/player repository.

facts.label: Docs and support entitlement
facts.value: Public docs and support desk; terms offer commercially reasonable support efforts without a specific support obligation unless separately agreed.

facts.label: Support-site check
facts.value: Linked support portal returned HTTP 403 to the public fetch.

facts.label: Complete self-host upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable to the vendor-operated backend reviewed; local Agent/probe and MIT Player are client components.

uptime.math: Five monitors fit the five included ones. The estimate is €4.99 a month, which includes one monitored server.

For 100 monitors: €4.99, plus €1.01 for each monitor above the 5 included, comes to €100.94 a month, including one server.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Hosted prices are in euros. Server monitoring is metered by the hour and invoiced monthly; displayed prices are monthly reference prices for 30 days of use.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Displayed prices exclude VAT; applicable tax is added at checkout based on the buyer's location.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Annual and multi-year server reservations are prepaid and discounted; the published discounts are 10% for 12 months, 15% for 24 months, and 20% for 36 months.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free plan: €0 per month, up to 3 servers, 100 included metrics per server, 60-second resolution, 1-day metric retention, 6-month event retention, and 5 uptime monitors per account.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free plan includes core CPU, memory, disk, and network metrics, email alerting, and community support.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free plan includes 5 uptime monitors per account, with a 5-minute check interval; additional monitors are priced only on paid plans.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: New accounts receive a 15-day Professional trial without a payment card; after the trial, an account with no payment method returns to Free.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: The FAQ says a payment method on file causes the account to move to Professional billing after the trial, based on actual usage.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Starter is the lowest paid plan at €4.99 per monitored server per month, billed hourly and invoiced monthly.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Professional costs €10.99 per server per month; Enterprise is quote-based.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Starter includes 100 metrics per server and caps at 200; Professional includes 1,000 and caps at 2,000. Extra metric packs of 50 are €0.50/month on paid plans.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Starter and Professional log ingestion is listed at €0.50/GiB with a daily limit of 1 GiB; treatment of attempted ingestion above the limit is not stated.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Monitors above the 5 included on paid plans are charged at €1.01 per monitor per month; the public pages do not describe an automatic plan upgrade.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Pricing describes hourly measurement and monthly invoices, but no account-wide hard spending cap was stated in the pricing page and FAQ checked.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: A per-server metrics maximum is listed by plan; no separate per-project budget stop was found in the pricing pages checked.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Metrics retention is 1 day on Free, 30 days on Starter, and 13 months on Professional; Enterprise can set custom retention.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Event retention is 6 months on Free, 12 months on Starter, and 24 months on Professional; Enterprise is custom.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Hosted log retention is 30 days on Starter and Professional.

facts.value: Standalone Glouton local TSDB defaults to 15 days and has a configurable local retention setting.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Free is limited to 3 servers; Starter, Professional, and Enterprise list unlimited servers.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: A public status page can publish one or more applications; page count and audience limit were not specified in the status-page doc checked.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Log ingestion is priced by GiB on Starter and Professional with a 1 GiB/day limit; the French and English pages conflict on the rate.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Glouton Cloud agent can collect container, service, system, and file logs; OTLP logs can be received over gRPC or HTTP.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Public docs do not state a maximum log-line size, accepted rate per second, or whether data above the daily limit is rejected, sampled, or dropped.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Pricing lists log ingestion at €0.50/GiB on Starter and Professional, with no separate query or archive retrieval charge shown.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Our calculation: 5 GiB × €0.50 = €2.50/month; 25 GiB × €0.50 = €12.50/month, assuming evenly distributed usage within 1 GiB/day.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Our calculation: 100 GiB × €0.50 = €50.00 at the listed unit rate, but 100 GiB over 30 days averages 3.33 GiB/day and exceeds the 1 GiB/day limit; exact bill is unknown.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: Bleemeo SAS is a French company registered in Toulouse, with its registered office in Labège, France.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: No country-based buyer restriction was found on the pricing page or French terms checked.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Hosted monitoring covers server and operating-system health, service/application metrics, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud resources.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Uptime monitors check external services and URLs; Glouton can also act as a private probe for internal endpoints.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Hosted log management ingests, parses, searches, and alerts on log lines.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Public customer status pages show the live health of selected applications, services, and uptime monitors.

facts.value: Bleemeo Cloud is the vendor-hosted monitoring service and uses Glouton agents to collect server data.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Glouton can run by itself with local storage and a local panel, without a Bleemeo account; it can also send data to a Prometheus-compatible endpoint or MQTT broker.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Documented custom-metric clients include Go, Java, Python, Ruby, .NET, Rust, Node.js, and PHP; Prometheus scraping and StatsD are also documented.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: The self-hosted Glouton agent is written in Go and documents host, container, service, JMX, StatsD, and Prometheus collection paths.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Email, mobile push, and webhooks are listed as notification channels; the pricing table includes them on all plans.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: SMS integrations are named for Twilio, MessageBird, and OVH; pricing matrix and FAQ disagree about whether every channel is available on Free.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation

facts.label: Deployment fit

facts.label: Deployment fit

facts.label: Deployment fit

facts.label: Sending data in

facts.label: Setup path

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Community Edition quick start starts the Compose bundle, then the operator connects Grafana to SquirrelDB; production setup adds database, broker, and security configuration.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: HTTP monitor settings can check a selected response status; authentication and custom request options are described in monitor configuration docs.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Private probes can reach private-network URLs through a Glouton agent.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: A public page says the paid and free monitor interval, but a maximum check timeout and supported frequency range were not found in the pricing or uptime configuration pages checked.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance

facts.value: Operator can pause monitors, choose intervals, check retention, worker capacity and log collection. No app-level monetary spend cap is documented; third-party compute/provider bills need their own controls.

facts.label: Check retention default
facts.value: Server requirements says default retention 90 days, adjustable in Settings > Monitor history. Tagged AppSettings model declares checkTTL default 30. Display can request 30/60/90-day bars, but that does not guarantee all raw data remains.

facts.label: Docker logs and operational records
facts.value: Optional direct-Docker collection reads latest 200 log lines/container/check and stores them for 7 days. Capture-backed Docker does not provide logs. Application Logs are Checkmate's own server records.

facts.label: Teams and allowances
facts.value: Role/team collaboration and monitor ownership are supported, with no license-metered seat/monitor allowance. User, Admin and Superadmin roles; first account becomes Superadmin.

facts.label: Limited Docker log capture
facts.value: Direct Docker monitor can collect latest 200 lines/container on each check, kept 7 days; Capture-backed Docker lacks container log data.

facts.label: General log billing scenario
facts.value: General GB log-ingest/query/archive price comparison does not apply to the established snapshot/internal-log features. Software has no per-GB license charge; storage and providers remain operator costs.

facts.label: Country and eligibility
facts.value: Bluewave Labs is based in Canada; terms specify Ontario law. Software use includes business/individual deployments under AGPL; monitoring must be authorized and lawful.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Uptime/protocol checks, response times, PageSpeed/Lighthouse, hardware through Capture, Docker state/resources/log snapshots, incidents, alerts and public status pages.

facts.label: Deployment choices
facts.value: No vendor-hosted Checkmate account/service or billing relationship. Complete self-hosted app image plus required MongoDB; third-party hosting providers are deployment options under their own contracts.

facts.label: SDK requirements
facts.value: External checks need no app instrumentation SDK. Hardware Capture runs on Linux, Windows, macOS/Raspberry Pi and Go-capable systems; it exposes authenticated REST metrics.

facts.label: Channels
facts.value: SMTP email, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Matrix, Rocket.Chat, ntfy, Pushover, PagerDuty, webhooks and Twilio SMS are documented.

facts.label: Delivery costs and countries
facts.value: No Checkmate included sending credits, SMS destination-country tariff or voice allowance published. SMTP account and Twilio SMS sender/recipient/account configuration are external.

facts.label: Noise and incidents
facts.value: Recent check results feed configurable monitor status windows/thresholds; state changes create/resolve incidents and notify selected channels. Maintenance suppresses notifications while checks continue; paused monitors stop checking.

facts.label: Escalation details
facts.value: PagerDuty integration sends to an external incident-management service. No native timed multi-level escalation/acknowledgement/quiet-hours policy found in notification/incident/maintenance docs.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: App is multi-arch Linux amd64/arm64 image; Docker host/LAN/VPS/Pi deployment, MongoDB 8.0 in reference Compose. Capture supplies remote host metrics; direct Docker socket, remote Docker mTLS or Capture metrics supported.

facts.label: Monitoring data paths
facts.value: App makes active checks; Capture REST metrics are fetched with an API secret; direct Docker APIs provide state/stats/log snapshots. Management REST API uses JWT bearer auth and JSON monitor import/export.

facts.label: Setup
facts.value: Run app+MongoDB Compose, set JWT secret and CLIENT_HOST, put TLS proxy in front as needed; create first Superadmin, monitors and channels. Hardware needs Capture; PageSpeed needs Google API access/key for higher limits.

facts.label: Checks and assertions
facts.value: HTTP GET/HEAD, expected status extension, equal/include/regex body checks and JMESPath JSON extraction; ping, TCP port, DNS records, gRPC, WebSocket/game, HTTPS certificate info and optional PageSpeed.

facts.label: Private/authenticated targets
facts.value: Check from app/worker network, configure outbound proxy or custom CA for internal TLS. Capture requires API secret; remote Docker requires client cert/key. No general HTTP OAuth/login-recorder support found in HTTP docs.

facts.label: Frequency
facts.value: Current UI offers 15 seconds–30 minutes for every monitor type. Tagged monitor default interval 60000 ms. No hourly/daily dropdown; backend accepts wider interval values per docs.

facts.label: Timeout and scheduling limits
facts.value: Exact default/request-timeout range and automatic HTTP retry count were not published in checked HTTP/interval/API docs or monitor config schema.

facts.label: Origins and geography
facts.value: Primary checks run on operator app/worker infrastructure. Optional Globalping spans North America, Europe, Asia, Oceania, South America and Africa, with separate 5/10/15/30-minute geo interval.

facts.label: Confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Checkmate evaluates recent-check windows/thresholds; incidents open/resolve on state change. One-off/recurring maintenance suppresses alerts, with checks still stored. Geo results do not change primary status.

facts.label: Certificate/domain expiry
facts.value: HTTPS monitor displays presented cert expiry; WHOIS domain lookup on detail view displays registrable-domain expiry, cached and N/A when registry omits it. TLS validation failure marks check down.

facts.label: Status-page controls
facts.value: Public pages with selected monitors/sub-components, own domain (one domain/page), logo/name/color/timezone, five themes/modes and custom CSS. Unpublished pages only visible to logged-in team members.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: No native public email opt-in/unsubscribe list, subscriber quota/rate or customer subscriber export established in status docs or v3.13.1 status schema.

facts.label: State source and history
facts.value: Selected monitor state/check history drives pages; Latest or 30/60/90-day daily buckets with page timezone. Incidents resolve automatically or manually. No separate public narrative-update/subscriber announcement workflow established.

facts.label: Job schedules and grace
facts.value: Cron feature is advertised in site text, but period/cron syntax, timezone/DST, grace/deadline evaluation and expected-duration rules are not documented in checked guides/schema.

facts.label: Job signals
facts.value: Native job success/failure/start/end endpoints, captured stdout/stderr and run-history retention not established for latest tagged release.

facts.label: Log viewing
facts.value: Container logs visible from Docker details; Application Logs filter Checkmate server logs by severity/service/method/message. No general multi-app log ingestion/search/archive platform established.

facts.label: Runtime requirements
facts.value: App container + MongoDB 8.0, persistent volume, Linux amd64/arm64 Docker host. Docs say 1+ GB RAM Linux VPS/Pi; macOS/Windows development. Current worker coordination uses MongoDB, not Redis.

facts.label: Sizing limits
facts.value: Requirements gives an illustrative 300 monitors at one-second intervals using ~3 GB/month storage and generic modest-host guidance; no controlled sizing for all fixed comparison workloads found.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Admins/Superadmins export monitors as JSON and import copies through Settings > Data/API. Imports replace IDs, create new monitors, do not update existing ones and do not preserve cross-instance notification IDs.

facts.label: Full data removal/portability
facts.value: No complete historical export format/limit or upstream backup/restore/purge guarantee found in current install/API/privacy guides. Operators must manage MongoDB volume, backups, credentials and external notification copies.

facts.label: Sensitive fields
facts.value: Public status payload exposes target URL/port only when showURL is enabled; tagged global default false. Docker TLS private key encrypted by ENCRYPTION_KEY and omitted from API response; custom CA trust supported.

facts.label: Outbound telemetry and third parties
facts.value: Daily anonymous installation heartbeat enabled by default includes instance UUID/version/platform/queue/runtime and counts by monitor type; TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false disables it after restart. Notifications go to configured external providers.

facts.label: Residency and DPA
facts.value: Monitoring/accounts/credentials stay in operator-selected MongoDB infrastructure; Bluewave Labs says it has no access. No hosted storage-country selector or Checkmate SaaS DPA applies. Third-party notification/geo/hosting choices have their own policies.

facts.label: Identity
facts.value: Checkmate, checkmate.so; upstream github.com/bluewave-labs/Checkmate, maintained by Bluewave Labs.

facts.label: Availability
facts.value: Upstream not archived/disabled; latest non-prerelease API returned v3.13.1, published 2026-10-22T18:55:29Z. No whole-product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in official site/repository/release checks.

facts.label: Deprecated deployment paths
facts.value: Legacy checkmate-client, checkmate-backend, checkmate-mongo and checkmate-backend-mono-multiarch images are no longer updated. Use ghcr.io/bluewave-labs/checkmate plus MongoDB. Old UPTIME_APP_* client variables are no longer read.

facts.label: License and repository
facts.value: AGPL-3.0, exact license in v3.13.1 upstream tag. Free use/modification/distribution subject to AGPL; modified network-served versions must provide corresponding source as required.

facts.label: Help and SLA
facts.value: Public docs, Discord and GitHub issues; no paid support tier. Security policy points to GitHub private advisory reporting. Terms disclaim warranties/continuous availability.

facts.label: Upgrades/security and backup
facts.value: Current migration path replaces old images/client variables, keeps existing MongoDB data volume and backs up data directory first. Security reports use private GitHub advisories; releases publish changes.

facts.label: How billing works

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview price and final billing unit have not been announced. Its May preview post said pricing was not finalized; the current waitlist page still offers only preview access.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Open Source has no software license fee under its listed component licenses; hosting, storage, backups and operations are not free unless the user supplies them.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: No continuing free Managed ClickStack Cloud plan is listed. The Cloud offer starts with a temporary 30-day, USD 300 trial, then moves to PAYG.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud private preview is access-limited; no public ongoing-free quota or post-preview price is published.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: ClickHouse Cloud trial: USD 300 credits for 30 days, ending at whichever comes first: credit exhaustion or 30 days; then organization moves to PAYG. If a card is added, credits are used first and the card is charged only when they are depleted or expire.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: Whether a payment card is required to enter the Cloud trial was not stated in the current public pricing FAQ or terms checked.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Basic is the smallest Cloud tier. It shows up to 1 TB storage, 8–12 GiB total memory, daily backups retained 1 day and one AZ; price is metered, not a fixed ClickStack fee.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: February 2026 official webinar said Managed ClickStack had no additional purchase/SKU and was included across Cloud tiers. The July 2026 GA post and current Cloud price page do not restate a ClickStack line-item fee.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud has no public price, paid plan, included allowance or minimum because the official offer remains private preview.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Basic tier is listed with up to 1 TB storage; Scale lists unlimited storage. Exact ingestion/query behavior when Basic reaches 1 TB is not specified on the pricing, billing, or ClickStack docs pages checked.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Cloud trial ends on credit exhaustion or day 30 and converts the organization to PAYG; PAYG use requires a supported payment method and bills monthly in arrears at current tier rates.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview has not published ingest allowance, overage, sampling, shutoff or upgrade rules.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Managed Cloud has configurable maximum autoscaling limits and spend alerts by billing period at email, console UI or Slack; threshold notifications fire at 50%, 75%, 90% and 100%. The alert is not a hard organization spend cap.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: PAYG payment method auto-charge starts at USD 1,000 due; after the first successful payment it rises to USD 5,000 and after the second to USD 10,000. This is an invoice collection threshold, not a spending cap.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview page does not publish spend controls, caps or usage alerts.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Open Source default table retention is 3 days; customer can configure common or per-signal TTL for logs, traces, metrics and sessions. Expired data is removed on ClickHouse merges, not necessarily at the exact TTL time.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Managed ClickStack product page markets indefinite retention for high-cardinality logs, metrics and traces. The generic TTL guide says 3 days by default and the Managed quickstart collector example sets 720h (30 days).

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview materials describe managed storage but publish no default/maximum retention duration or archive/search split.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Managed ClickStack has no per-user or per-host price in the February 2026 offer statement; current Cloud rates price compute, storage and transfer. No included team, source, project or seat limit was found in the current pricing/docs pages.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Exact included users, services, projects, sources and alert recipients were not published in the current Managed ClickStack prices or docs checked.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview has no published user/source/service counts or seat fees.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Managed ClickStack Cloud meters compressed stored bytes for Cloud table storage; compute time, backups and data transfer are separate meters. No per-event or per-host fee is advertised.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview handles OTLP ingestion, buffering and scaling, but has no published raw/compressed GB allowance, maximum event size, sampling/drop rule or ingestion counter.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Managed ClickStack Cloud has storage, backup, compute and egress charges; Cloud storage and backup are counted separately. No separate scan/query fee is listed in the current Cloud rate table; query activity consumes metered compute.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview has not published query, storage, export, backup or data-transfer rates.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: ClickHouse lists headquarters in the Bay Area, California and Amsterdam, Netherlands; its terms name ClickHouse, Inc. Buyer-country eligibility list was not found. Cloud terms require compliance with US export-control and sanctions rules.

facts.label: Eligible buyer countries
facts.value: An exhaustive supported-country or prohibited-country list was not published in the terms, pricing, Cloud documentation or company newsroom checked. US sanctions/export-control compliance is required.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Logs, traces, metrics, browser session replay, application exceptions and performance investigation; real-time alerting. Detection/diagnosis from ingested data.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Self-hosted: Open Source includes ClickHouse, ClickStack UI (HyperDX), ClickStack OTel Collector and MongoDB app state; customer runs them.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Managed ClickStack: ClickHouse and UI run in ClickHouse Cloud; customer still runs its OTel collector and controls pipeline/schema.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud: ClickHouse manages OTLP ingestion endpoint, buffering, scaling, storage and query serving; current official waitlist describes private-preview access.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Official SDK/integration docs list browser JavaScript, Node.js, Python, Go, Java, Ruby on Rails, Elixir, Deno, NestJS, Next.js, React Native and AWS Lambda; standard OpenTelemetry SDKs and agents are also supported.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Native Slack webhook/API, PagerDuty API and generic webhooks. Docs say Slack API and PagerDuty integrations are supported only in ClickHouse Cloud; generic webhook is separately listed.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Private-preview ClickStack Cloud announcement describes alerting only as future/preview capability; no current channel list or alert delivery fee is published for the preview.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Email, push, SMS and phone notification costs/restrictions are not published as native ClickStack alert channels in the feature page checked.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Search and dashboard-chart alerts support recurring evaluation and evaluation history; alerts can be centrally managed. Latest changelog adds filtering by state/name/tags.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Anomaly-detection alerts are a separate documented feature using baseline and threshold detection.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Open Source supports all-in-one Docker for evaluation and separated UI, ClickHouse and collector for production; ClickStack docs include Docker Compose and Helm paths.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Documented application paths include browser, Node.js, Python, Go, Java, React Native, AWS Lambda and Kubernetes collector integration.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud is advertised as fully managed/serverless. It accepts telemetry at an OTel endpoint; the May 2026 example endpoint is in AWS us-east-2.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Managed ClickStack accepts OTLP over HTTP port 4318 or gRPC port 4317 through the customer's OTel collector; ClickStack OTel SDKs and compatible OTel SDKs/agents are documented.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Vector may write directly to ClickHouse tables; Fluentd and other compatible agents can feed the OTel collector. Vector users define compatible schema and timestamps.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview directs users to a managed OTLP endpoint for OpenTelemetry data; endpoint handles ingestion, buffering, scaling, storage and query serving.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Open Source: run the all-in-one Docker image for a local trial, send a test OTLP event and view it; for production deploy ClickHouse, UI and collector separately, configure storage/TTL, access and backups.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Managed ClickStack: create a Cloud service, configure/deploy an OTel collector gateway, set SDK/agent endpoint and credentials, then create or use compatible sources/schemas in ClickStack.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview: join private-preview waitlist, configure an OTel collector exporter to the managed endpoint and token, then explore the ClickStack UI.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: Node.js SDK documents automatic tracing/logging/metrics, uncaught exceptions with stack trace and code context, and manual exception recording; Browser SDK captures exceptions and can attach React error-boundary errors.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: Public docs describe searching exception events and viewing them in traces/replays; they do not describe an issue inbox with duplicate grouping/merge controls or a universal handled/unhandled event counter.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: Node.js SDK can send uncaught exception stack traces and code context. ClickStack displays OTel exception stacktrace attributes.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: ClickStack team demo identifies JavaScript source-map upload/mapping for minified browser errors as an Enterprise feature; no source-map allowance is stated in the Cloud tier price table.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: Dashboard release markers use telemetry service.version by default, or a configured version expression, to show when a new service version first appears.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: Browser SDK records DOM changes, mouse, clicks, scroll, keyboard, console, network requests and JS exceptions, and correlates replay with backend traces/logs. User identifiers/custom attributes can be attached.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: ClickStack supports log search, SQL, Lucene-style filtering, traces and dashboards over ClickHouse tables. Managed ClickStack uses object storage/caching for long-term Cloud data; Cloud billing charges compute for queries, not a published per-query count.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: ClickStack Cloud preview is described as a serverless query experience over hosted data; the preview post does not publish a retrieval fee, archive tier or data-age limit.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: Trace waterfall, linked logs, service maps, database query visibility and browser/backend correlation support request-level investigation. ClickStack is not documented as a code profiler.

facts.value: Sampling is applied by the customer’s SDK/OTel collector if configured; ClickStack can apply sample-rate-aware trace aggregates to sampled data. Its collector guide discusses tail sampling.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: Managed ClickStack product page says it does not sample, roll up or discard high-cardinality telemetry; this is a product claim and does not prevent customer-side OTel sampling.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: Browser SDK supports browser session data, network timing and exceptions; May 2026 Browser RUM dashboard template covers Core Web Vitals LCP, INP, CLS, page load, long tasks, JS exceptions, API failures and traffic dimensions.

facts.label: Free over-limit behavior
facts.value: Current Workers Free logs have a 200,000-event/day allowance; after Dec 1 the pooled Free tier stops new ingestion once 0.5 GB/day is reached, then resumes at 00:00 UTC.

facts.label: Paid over-limit behavior
facts.value: Current Workers Paid logs are billed at $0.60 per additional million events. From Dec 1, Paid Observability overages continue automatically at separate ingest and storage rates.

facts.label: Account event ceiling and truncation
facts.value: Workers Logs has a 5 billion-log/account/day ceiling; a 1% head sample applies for the rest of the day after the ceiling. An individual log is limited to 256 KB; excess is truncated and flagged.

facts.label: Sampling effect
facts.value: Sampling before persistence reduces both billed ingestion and stored data under the upcoming GB meter. The trace and log sample rates can be configured separately from 0 to 1.

facts.label: Usage visibility
facts.value: Cloudflare says Billable Usage shows current ingestion/storage usage, remaining allowances, and estimated charges.

facts.label: Hard spending cap
facts.value: The reviewed usage-based billing and Observability pricing docs describe alerts and usage visibility, not a hard Observability spend cap that stops Paid ingestion.

facts.label: Workers Logs retention through Nov 30
facts.value: Workers Free: 3 days. Workers Paid: 7 days.

facts.label: Workers Logs and traces retention from Dec 1
facts.value: Default retention is 7 days in the pooled Observability pricing. Configurable 30-, 90-, and 365-day options are described as future plans, not current entitlements.

facts.label: Worker metrics retention
facts.value: Worker metrics can be inspected for up to three months, in time windows no larger than one week. Zone analytics covers the last 30 days.

facts.label: Issue detail retention
facts.value: The Issues dataset has a 7-day default retention. Issue occurrences are queryable for seven days; issue records may remain listed after occurrence detail expires.

facts.label: Workers and project limits
facts.value: Observability data follows Workers and account scope. The Workers plan limits table lists 100 Workers on Free and 500 by default on Paid; a separate Observability project cap was not stated.

facts.label: Seats and Observability-specific project cap
facts.value: No Workers Observability-specific user-seat price, recipient cap, or project count was published in the product, pricing, account, or alert docs checked.

facts.label: Log meter and loss
facts.value: Until Nov 30, Workers Logs bills by event count according to Workers plan. From Dec 1, shared Observability bills by uncompressed ingestion GB before storage compression. Sampling reduces metered data.

facts.label: Log limits
facts.value: One log is limited to 256 KB; excess is truncated. Above 5 billion logs per account/day, Cloudflare applies 1% sampling for the rest of that day.

facts.label: Query and dashboard charges
facts.value: Cloudflare says queries, dashboards, alerts, and analytics in the new Observability model do not incur an additional charge.

facts.label: Separate Log Explorer price
facts.value: Legacy Log Explorer datasets cost $1 per GB ingested, include 30-day retention, and have no additional query charge. They do not consume the pooled Observability allowance.

facts.label: Export and destination charges
facts.value: Logpush exports use separate export meters; destination services may add their own fees. OTel post-Dec 1 pricing is not specified in the reviewed docs.

facts.label: Vendor home region
facts.value: Cloudflare lists its headquarters in San Francisco, California, United States.

facts.label: Buyer eligibility
facts.value: Product-specific country restrictions or a list of eligible Workers Observability buyers was not found in the product, pricing, terms, or privacy pages checked.

facts.label: Main job
facts.value: Collects and explores Worker logs, runtime metrics, traces, and failures; helps find errors and slow operations.

facts.label: Logs
facts.value: Collects invocation events, custom console logs, errors, and uncaught exceptions; offers near-real-time tailing and dashboard search.

facts.label: Metrics
facts.value: Shows requests, errors, invocation status, subrequests, CPU time, wall time, execution duration, memory percentiles, and deployment markers.

facts.label: Traces
facts.value: Follows Worker handlers, outbound fetch calls, bindings such as KV and R2, and supported RPC calls; supports custom spans.

facts.label: Failure issues
facts.value: Detects and groups Worker exceptions, failed invocations, Worker 5xx responses, and logged errors into issues.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Cloudflare operates the Observability backend. The product monitors Workers running on Cloudflare; no self-hosted edition of the dashboard or data store is offered in the reviewed docs.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Automatic logging and tracing are part of the Workers runtime and do not require a separate SDK. Source-map docs cover JavaScript and TypeScript; no full Observability language/framework compatibility matrix was found.

facts.label: Framework support list
facts.value: A comprehensive list of frameworks and minimum versions for log, issue, trace, and metric collection was not published in the product and integration docs checked.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Observability alerts support email on all plans, webhooks on all plans, and PagerDuty on Business and higher plans. The pricing page says alerts have no separate Observability charge.

facts.label: Issue routing
facts.value: Issues beta automations can send diagnostic context to coding agents, generic webhooks, chat, or incident-management destinations. The Cloudflare API MCP server can also publish new or recurring Issues as MCP Events. Destination services can have their own fees.

facts.label: SMS and phone
facts.value: The reviewed Observability alert and issue-routing docs do not publish built-in SMS or phone delivery, credits, or country rates.

facts.label: Alert rules
facts.value: Custom monitors run SQL queries on a schedule and can alert by threshold, anomaly detection, or SLO; platform notifications are also available.

facts.label: Issue grouping and automation triggers
facts.value: Issues groups related failures from the same Worker. Automations run at an occurrence threshold or after recurrence following 1 hour to 365 days of inactivity.

facts.label: Acknowledgement and escalation
facts.value: A published on-call schedule, repeated alert escalation policy, or acknowledgement timer for Workers Observability alerts was not found in the alert and Issues docs checked.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Supports Workers running on the Cloudflare platform; configuration is through the dashboard, Wrangler, or Cloudflare CLI. No host agent is required.

facts.label: Outside Workers support
facts.value: The checked product docs focus on Workers and connected Cloudflare resources. A supported agent for customer-managed servers, external containers, or mobile apps was not published in the product pages checked.

facts.label: Data sent in: logs and events
facts.value: Captures runtime invocation data and developer output such as console logs and errors. Custom logs are emitted by Worker code; Workers Logs is not described as a general external OTLP log-ingestion endpoint.

facts.label: Data sent in: traces
facts.value: Runtime tracing automatically creates spans for supported Worker operations; custom spans can be added with the Workers tracing APIs.

facts.label: Data sent in: runtime metrics
facts.value: Requests, invocation statuses, duration, CPU, wall time and memory metrics are generated by the Workers platform and can be queried through Cloudflare's GraphQL metrics API.

facts.label: Metrics export
facts.value: Workers infrastructure metrics and custom metrics cannot currently be exported through the Workers OpenTelemetry export path. Cloudflare's October 2026 blog describes easier metrics export as future work.

facts.label: Data sent out: OTel
facts.value: Workers logs and traces can be exported to configured OpenTelemetry destinations. Persist can be set to false to send data externally without retaining it in Cloudflare.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Logs are on by default for newly created Workers. Tracing must be enabled separately in Wrangler or the dashboard; deploy the Worker after changing configuration.

facts.label: Enable Issues and source maps
facts.value: Issues can be enabled through Wrangler, dashboard, or Cloudflare CLI and only processes new traffic. Wrangler 4.134.0 or later is required for its documented Wrangler setup. Source maps upload by default from Wrangler 4.150.0 when maps are present.

facts.label: Error detection and grouping
facts.value: Issues detects uncaught exceptions, failed invocations, Worker 5xx responses, and console errors, then groups related failures from the same Worker. It can also report handled errors logged with console.error.

facts.label: Issue controls
facts.value: Issues have Active, Resolved, and Ignored states; an occurrence after resolution reopens an issue. The minimum automation occurrence threshold is one.

facts.label: Source locations
facts.value: Uploaded JavaScript and TypeScript source maps remap captured stacks to original file names and lines. Wrangler 4.150.0+ uploads maps by default if generated and present.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: Issue occurrences show the Worker version that produced the failure, and metric charts have deployment markers. Commit linking, release annotations, regression detection, and automatic fix tracking were not established in the Issues docs checked.

facts.label: Commit and fix workflow
facts.value: A source-control release mapping or “fixed in release” workflow was not published in the product and issue docs checked.

facts.label: Error context
facts.value: Issue details can show stack traces, related logs and traces, Worker version, invocation, and request details. Trace attributes include operation status, durations, and supported runtime metadata.

facts.label: Session replay
facts.value: A browser or mobile session-replay feature for Worker users was not published in the Workers Observability docs checked.

facts.label: Search and live logs
facts.value: Workers Logs can be streamed near real time and searched in the dashboard by Worker and fields. The query builder supports filters and SQL over datasets, with charts and custom dashboards.

facts.label: Archive
facts.value: The reviewed Workers Logs docs describe retention and export destinations, but do not publish a separate archive tier, archive retrieval fee, or cold-storage restore workflow for Worker logs.

facts.label: Trace diagnosis
facts.value: Automatic traces show timing and outcomes for Worker handlers, outbound fetches, KV/R2/Durable Object bindings, and supported RPC calls; custom spans can be added.

facts.label: Runtime performance diagnosis
facts.value: Runtime metrics show request counts, error statuses, CPU and wall-time quantiles, execution duration, memory percentiles, and deployment markers. Request duration is shown only when Smart Placement is enabled.

facts.label: Profiling
facts.value: A hosted continuous profiler or database-query profiler for Worker code was not published in the Workers Observability pages checked.

facts.label: Sampling mode and default
facts.value: Workers tracing is head-sampled with a default rate of 1 (100% when enabled); the rate can be set from 0 to 1. Logs have their own head-sampling setting.

facts.label: Tail sampling and error retention
facts.value: Tail-based sampling, such as “keep only errors or slow requests,” is not supported in the current trace docs.

facts.label: Cost and retention effect
facts.value: From Dec 1, persisted traces use the shared GB ingestion and storage meter. Setting persist=false exports without storing in Cloudflare; sampling before arrival reduces both ingestion and storage.

facts.label: Browser and mobile real-user monitoring
facts.value: Browser page timings, client JavaScript errors, mobile freezes, and RUM session allowances were not published as Workers Observability features in the product and docs checked.

facts.label: Synthetic check types
facts.value: Not applicable: Workers Observability observes actual Worker execution and does not offer a synthetic website/API/port/DNS check product in the reviewed scope.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Not applicable: no synthetic check scheduler or probe timeout is part of this Workers telemetry product.

facts.label: Probe locations and counting
facts.value: Not applicable: the product collects Workers telemetry and does not sell selectable synthetic probe locations.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no synthetic check retry, multi-probe confirmation, or maintenance window setting in the Workers Observability docs checked.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Not applicable: this is not a certificate or domain-expiry monitor.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Not applicable: Workers Observability is not a customer-facing status-page product.

facts.label: Status subscribers and updates
facts.value: Not applicable: no hosted customer status-page or subscriber notification feature is included in Workers Observability.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Not applicable: there is no status-page incident history or component update workflow in this product.

facts.label: Schedule and grace rules
facts.value: Not applicable: Workers Observability does not define job schedules, time zones, or missed-job grace periods. Cloudflare Cron Triggers are a separate Workers runtime feature.

facts.label: Scheduled handler failures
facts.value: Workers tracing supports scheduled handlers and Workers Logs include cron invocation events. The pages checked do not document a heartbeat or alert for a scheduled run that never starts.

facts.label: Missed heartbeat or run history
facts.value: A dedicated expected-run heartbeat, missed-run grace setting, and long-term scheduled-job history were not published in the Observability docs checked.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable: Cloudflare operates the Workers Observability backend, and no self-host edition is offered.

facts.label: Export options
facts.value: Dashboard export can download logs and traces as JSON or CSV. Workers Logpush and OpenTelemetry export provide configured destinations; Tail Workers can filter or transform telemetry.

facts.label: Worker Logpush cost
facts.value: Workers Trace Events Logpush is available only on Workers Paid; 10 million requests/month are included and additional requests cost $0.05/million after filtering or sampling.

facts.label: Other Logpush export pricing
facts.value: For standard Logpush exports, 25 GB/month/account are included for internal destinations, then $0.03/GB; external destinations include 25 GB, then $0.10/GB; transformations include 1 GB, then $0.04/GB. Destination charges are extra.

facts.label: OTel export pricing after Dec 1
facts.value: The official October 2025 Workers tracing blog lists 10 million exported events/month and $0.05 per additional million on Workers Paid. Current docs say persistent telemetry joins the GB meter on Dec 1, but do not state whether this older OTel export allowance/rate also changes then.

facts.label: Delete and retention controls
facts.value: Disabling persistence prevents new exported data from being stored in Cloudflare. Data otherwise expires according to the published retention period. A Workers Observability API or dashboard control to delete selected stored log/trace records was not found.

facts.label: Sensitive data in traces
facts.value: Trace docs state that header values are not captured, while header names/operations are; URLs and query strings are captured. The Workers API supports a redact_query_string setting for logs and traces.

facts.label: Sensitive application data
facts.value: Console logs, stack traces, request details, and custom span attributes can carry application data. Issues docs advise against sending secrets, tokens, or sensitive request content. A general automatic password or PII masking rule was not published.

facts.label: Default masking policy
facts.value: The checked product, export, privacy, and data-processing pages did not publish a Workers Observability-wide default scrubber for passwords, tokens, or personal information.

facts.label: Data residency
facts.value: The product, pricing, privacy, DPA, and data-localization pages checked do not name a selectable storage region or a Workers Observability telemetry residency location.

facts.label: DPA and processing terms
facts.value: Cloudflare publishes a DPA v6.4, effective April 3, 2026. It applies to customer data processed by Cloudflare under the main service agreement and describes processor roles and subprocessors.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Cloudflare Workers Observability; https://www.cloudflare.com/products/workers-observability/

facts.label: Availability
facts.value: Active product with current product, documentation, and changelog pages.

facts.label: Beta and acquisition history
facts.value: Workers Tracing and Issues are beta. Baselime was acquired in 2024; Cloudflare announced an expected standalone Baselime sunset toward end of 2024. No official Workers Observability retirement notice found.

facts.label: Newsroom and blog check
facts.value: Cloudflare's current Observability blog post describes the unified product and upcoming pricing; the press release documents the Baselime acquisition. No product shutdown announcement was found in the official press page, acquisition archive, or searched product updates.

facts.label: License and source code
facts.value: Not applicable to the hosted service: Cloudflare does not offer a self-hostable Workers Observability edition or license for its service backend.

facts.label: Documentation and support
facts.value: Cloudflare publishes public Workers Observability docs, pricing, API references, developer changelog, community forum, and developer Discord. A product-specific response-time promise was not found.

facts.label: Support entitlement
facts.value: A Workers Observability-specific support SLA, included ticket entitlement, or guaranteed response time was not stated in the product, pricing, terms, or public support pages checked.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable: Cloudflare operates the service backend. Users maintain their Worker code and Wrangler configuration; no backend upgrade or backup procedure is offered.
