facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Cloud Hosted Standard starts “as low as” $99/month, based on a production configuration with 120 GB storage and two zones; exact node instance charges vary with usage. Standard lists APM, logs, metrics and managed global synthetic access.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Serverless Logs Essentials and Complete have no fixed monthly price on the public rate card; charges follow ingest/retention and add-ons. The first published logs ingestion/retention bands are $0.35/GB and $0.036/GB-month for Essentials, and $0.50/GB and $0.040/GB-month for Complete in the checked US East table.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Current self-managed Platinum is existing customers only; Enterprise is available. The subscription page directs new buyers to sales rather than publishing a price. Gold is discontinued.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Serverless usage is billed by consumption; Elastic says usage is on demand without quotas/restrictions in its billing model. A managed OTLP endpoint can still return 429 when request rate/burst limits are exceeded.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: On trial expiry, resources suspend; subscribing within 30 days restores access, otherwise trial data is deleted.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Hosted budgets and notifications warn at 75% and 100% of target, but budgets do not stop resources or charges. Deleting a deployment stops its billing immediately, rounded up to the hour.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Budgets track an organization or selected Cloud resources and send email warnings at 75% and 100%; users choose notification roles. Budgets are monthly and reset on the first day of each calendar month.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: A budget target is not a hard spending stop: official docs say projects continue to run and generate costs after the target is reached. No separate hard cap was published in the reviewed budget and billing pages.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Cloud Usage page shows month-to-date usage; organization budgets and credit-consumption notices provide additional monitoring.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Serverless data is stored indefinitely by default until the customer configures data-stream retention; each stream can have a different retention period. Ingest is billed before compression and retention by GB-month.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Self-managed OpenTelemetry streams have no default deletion period; backing indices roll over at 50 GB or 30 days, but data is not automatically deleted unless a delete phase is configured. Stack retention can be set through ILM/data-stream lifecycle.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Hosted snapshots are billed separately from index disk, with a 100 GB/month snapshot storage allowance and 100,000 snapshot API requests/month across account deployments.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Enterprise Hosted adds searchable snapshots for longer-lived logs, metrics and APM data; the public pricing page does not state one universal duration.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Serverless organization supports up to 500 projects; raise the limit through Elastic Support. Trial organizations can have three active Serverless projects at once.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Cloud roles control user access. Public pricing lists plan support-contact allowances (Standard 2, Gold 6, Platinum 8, Enterprise 8); this is not a limit on product users.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: No per-user or per-service price is listed for Hosted or Serverless Observability; billing is by deployment resources or project usage.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Serverless bills normalized, enriched data after ingest pipeline and before compression. Metrics in TSDS mode are priced at 25% of standard rate; other telemetry is at standard rate.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Hosted bills cluster capacity, data transfer and snapshots rather than a fixed “logs included” allowance. Data-in transfer is free; outbound/inter-node transfer can be charged.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Log ingest can be shaped and filtered in pipelines before indexing; exact rejected-event behavior depends on the input and ingest path. The managed OTLP endpoint can return 429 on configured throughput/burst limits.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Fixed per-project log event count, event-size cap and default serverless ingest cap were not published in the checked billing, log-ingest and limits docs.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: No per-query rate is listed as a separate Observability Serverless charge on the reviewed pricing/billing pages; disclosed primary meters are ingest, retained volume, egress and selected add-ons.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Hosted snapshot storage/API requests, data transfer and optional inference/workflow/test charges are billed separately from node capacity.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Logs Essentials first-tier standard log ingest is $0.35/GB; Complete is $0.50/GB in the checked AWS Northern Virginia table. High-volume tiers lower the marginal rate.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Logs Essentials first-tier retention is $0.036/GB-month; Complete is $0.040/GB-month in the same displayed region.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: The public Serverless marketing page's “as low as” rates ($0.07/GB ingest, $0.017/GB-month retention for Essentials) are volume-tier minima, not the first-band prices. Complete advertises “as low as” $0.09/$0.019 for non-metrics.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Serverless price card does not list a per-query charge for Observability; ingestion, retention, egress and optional add-ons are the listed cost drivers.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: Elastic N.V. is incorporated in the Netherlands and lists Amsterdam as its European headquarters. Elastic operates globally. The public materials checked describe a professional/business service; no complete country-by-country buyer eligibility list was published on the reviewed product, pricing or agreement pages.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Logs, metrics, traces/APM, infrastructure monitoring, RUM, synthetics, profiling, alerting, SLOs and incident investigation. It detects from telemetry and checks; it does not sell a customer status-page product.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Logs Essentials includes log analysis, dashboards, integrations, alerts and notifications. APM, infrastructure/host views, SLOs, Synthetics and broader full-stack experiences are listed in Complete, not Essentials.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Hosted Elastic Cloud Hosted uses customer-selected deployment size and version; Serverless is a fully managed Observability project with autoscaling.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Self-managed Elastic Stack can run on-premises, in private or public cloud, or via supported orchestrators. The Observability solution uses Elasticsearch, Kibana and whichever agents/integrations the workload needs.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Elastic APM agents are maintained for Java, Go, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby and .NET; RUM JavaScript and Android/iOS agents are also listed. OpenTelemetry SDK/collector paths are supported, with agent-specific compatibility limits.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: APM covers supported server frameworks and database/cache/external HTTP calls; supported technology/version lists are maintained per agent.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: More than 400 out-of-the-box integrations are described in current docs; the product page says 450+.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Alerting connectors include email, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, Slack, webhook, Jira/Jira Service Management, Opsgenie, ServiceNow, and other integrations. Channel account fees are separate from Elastic charges.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Hosted Cloud tiers list 2 / 6 / 8 / 8 support contacts from Standard through Enterprise. Support plans are separate from incident-notification connectors.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Serverless organization support level is Standard included (limited), Gold 5%, Platinum 10%, or Enterprise 15% of consumption.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Direct SMS or phone-call notification as a built-in alert connector was not described in the checked connector catalog; no built-in SMS/phone charge was published there.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Alert actions can run on each alert, at scheduled intervals, or when an alert changes/recoveries; rule conditions and filters scope notifications.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Synthetics can retest failures (default on for project monitors), set consecutive-run conditions, and use maintenance windows to prevent planned maintenance alerts.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Users can acknowledge and unacknowledge Observability alerts in the current release; cases provide a place to track and investigate an issue.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Elastic's 2026 release notes show AI investigation and workflow capabilities developing; exact future availability or feature delivery is not guaranteed by the roadmap.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Elastic Cloud supports customer-selected AWS, GCP and Azure hosting regions; Serverless and Hosted have separate region lists.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Self-managed installs run on supported Linux/Windows platforms, virtual or physical hosts, and supported Kubernetes/cloud deployments; Elastic documents a multi-node setup with Elasticsearch, Kibana, Fleet Server and Elastic Agent.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Synthetics supports customer-run private locations for internal endpoints; private locations need Fleet Server and Elastic Agent and connect outward to the Elastic Stack.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Browser synthetic monitors run on Chromium; lightweight network checks run from Elastic's managed locations or private locations.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Logs can arrive through Elastic Agent, Beats, Logstash, integrations and OpenTelemetry; app logs can also be correlated with trace IDs.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Metrics support OpenTelemetry, Prometheus remote write/PromQL and Elastic Agent integrations.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Traces and application errors use Elastic APM agents, OpenTelemetry, and supported tracing intake paths.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Browser/mobile experience data can be sent by Elastic RUM agents. OpenTelemetry Browser RUM is a technical preview with stated limitations.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Hosted setup: create an Elastic Cloud organization and Hosted deployment or Serverless Observability project, choose provider/region and tier, then point integrations/agents/OTel clients at the endpoint and ingest telemetry.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Self-managed setup installs Elasticsearch and Kibana, secures them, then optionally installs Fleet Server/Elastic Agent and configures integrations/APM intake. The official tutorial estimates one to two hours for its example, not every production setup.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Synthetic checks can be created in UI or a version-controlled Node.js project using YAML for lightweight checks and JavaScript/TypeScript for browser journeys.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: APM captures unhandled errors/exceptions automatically and accepts error/log events; error groups are based primarily on stack trace and can be counted over time.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: Browser RUM captures client-side errors and user/browser context. RUM agent can filter stack frames from error grouping.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: Stack traces, error culprit and exception metadata appear in APM. RUM source maps can map minified JavaScript frames back to source when service name/version and bundle path match.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: Source map upload API default maximum payload is 1 MB; Kibana server.maxPayload can be changed for larger maps.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: APM service version can be set to a release number or commit reference. Source map match uses service name and service version; deployment annotations can be added through APM APIs.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: A dedicated regression/fix-state workflow for error groups was not published in the reviewed APM error, release, deployment and API docs.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: Error context can include service/environment/framework, host/process, URL, user fields (if supplied), custom metadata and related transaction IDs.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: RUM ties client errors and performance events to browser/device and trace context; current docs do not describe session playback/replay.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Logs support full-text and structured search, ES

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Data streams can use hot/warm/cold/frozen lifecycle tiers; Enterprise Hosted adds searchable snapshots for log, metrics and APM archives.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Kibana CSV export is limited for large results; official docs recommend Elasticsearch APIs for bulk extraction and snapshots for backup.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: APM traces include incoming requests, database queries, cache calls and external HTTP requests; trace waterfall and service map show related services and dependencies.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: Agents can capture database statements and runtime metrics; Universal Profiling provides code-level profiling without application instrumentation.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: LLM Observability traces and evaluates LLM application inputs/outputs and costs; current Cloud Hosted pricing lists it under Observability.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: APM supports head-based sampling and tail-based sampling. Sampling rate is configurable; tail-based sampling has deployment-specific configuration/feature requirements.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: APM agents decide whether to sample transactions; errors are retained regardless of sampling decision.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: There is no per-request pricing meter on the public APM pricing pages; Hosted uses node/instance resources and Serverless meters normalized GB ingested/retained.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: RUM browser agent captures page load timing, resource/network timing, browser errors and user interactions; supported agent families include JavaScript, iOS and Android.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: RUM browser trace sampling defaults to 100% (transactionSampleRate: 1.0); unsampled transactions retain basic duration/result but drop spans and context/labels.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: Serverless RUM signals are billed as telemetry ingest and retained data; no separate per-session or session-replay price is published.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Current Synthetics offers HTTP/S status/content checks, TCP port checks, ICMP ping checks, and real-browser journeys.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: HTTP monitors support status/body assertions and request options; TCP/HTTP support TLS; browser journeys can automate user flows. Private endpoints can use private locations or managed probes with access controls.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Synthetics monitor schedule is configurable in minutes; browser test actions/navigation default to 50 seconds, and browser journeys are limited to 15 minutes per run with retry able to make total runtime 30 minutes.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: A single plan-wide minimum/maximum interval and lightweight-check timeout were not stated in the reviewed pricing and monitor configuration pages.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Managed Synthetics tests can run from Elastic's selectable locations; monitors can run from multiple locations. Private locations run on customer infrastructure.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Managed browser tests charge $0.0123 per test run, metered in 60-second increments. Lightweight checks cost $28 per selected location per month per Elastic Stack for up to 1,000 simultaneous test capacity; private-location runs have no execution fee.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Serverless managed lightweight testing is a Complete-only add-on at $28/location/month; browser journeys are $0.0123/test run. These rates are separate from logs/traces/retention.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Project monitors retest when an up monitor goes down by default; a second failure creates an error and can trigger an alert.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Synthetics has monitor-status rules and TLS rules; consecutive-run thresholds and maintenance windows can reduce false alarms.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Maintenance windows apply to private locations after a configurable sync interval; default is five minutes, valid range 5–1,440 minutes.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Synthetics TLS rules can alert when HTTP/TCP certificates expire within a configured day threshold or exceed an age limit.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Domain registration expiry monitoring was not described in the checked Synthetics check types, TLS rules or pricing pages.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Logs Essentials and Complete include search, ad hoc analytics and dashboards; lifecycle controls define when data is deleted and may move data through tiers on self-managed/Hosted Stack.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Searchable snapshots are listed for Hosted Enterprise, not assumed for lower Cloud Hosted tiers or Serverless.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: APM uses distributed traces, service maps, transaction/span breakdowns, database/cache/external-call timing and code-level profiling.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: Head- and tail-based sampling are available; per-agent sample rates are configurable, and tail-based sampling requires applicable APM Server/cluster configuration.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: RUM measures browser/mobile page load, network/resource timing, errors and user interactions. RUM telemetry is charged as ordinary Serverless data ingest/retention, not per user session.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Elastic operates the Elastic Cloud service status page for its own regions and components. The checked Observability features/pricing docs do not offer a customer-facing hosted status-page builder.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Not applicable to a customer status-page product; Elastic Cloud service-status subscribers can receive vendor updates by email, Twitter or RSS/Atom.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Not applicable to a customer-facing status page. Elastic's own Cloud status page has regional/component updates and a public status API.

facts.label: Schedule and grace rules
facts.value: No dedicated scheduled-job monitor was identified in the checked Observability product overview, APM and Synthetics feature pages; Heartbeat schedules network service checks rather than receiving job start/completion pings.

facts.label: Job failure signals
facts.value: No dedicated missed-ping/start/end job check-in workflow was documented in the checked APM, Heartbeat, Synthetics and API pages. App exceptions/logs can still be sent as ordinary telemetry.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: A self-managed basic stack needs hosts for Elasticsearch and Kibana; optional APM Server/Fleet Server/Elastic Agent/integrations depend on signals and deployment pattern. Elastic recommends at least 4 GB RAM per Elasticsearch node for production.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Official installation tutorial uses three Elasticsearch nodes plus separate Kibana, Fleet Server and Elastic Agent hosts; supported operating-system/architecture details are in the support matrix.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Observability data is stored in Elasticsearch data streams and can be queried through REST APIs and official clients. Kibana CSV export is intended for moderate-size reports, not bulk export or backup.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Self-managed backup uses a configured snapshot repository; repository types include S3, GCS, Azure, shared filesystem and read-only URL.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Deleting a Hosted deployment stops billing immediately (rounded to the nearest hour) and erases on-disk data; Serverless project deletion loses all data, with prior usage still billed. Cloud contract says customer content is deleted within 45 days after subscription ends and service use stops, subject to legal/backup exceptions.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: APM agents or ingest pipelines can filter/redact selected event fields. Elastic warns that request bodies, headers, query strings, user fields, IPs, SQL statements and stack variables may contain sensitive data.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Browser RUM is disabled by default on self-managed APM Server because it accepts unauthenticated browser connections; configure allowed origins and rate limits before enabling.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: AI Assistant docs warn prompts may include alerts, configuration, queries, logs and chat data; data sent to a third-party provider is not anonymized by default. A customer can disable AI features or configure an anonymization pipeline.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: RUM records page timing, user/browser errors, URLs and user interaction data; no session-replay masking control was found because the reviewed RUM docs do not describe replay as a feature.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Hosted customer selects a supported AWS, Azure or GCP region; Serverless region is chosen at project creation and cannot be changed afterwards.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Elastic offers a DPA for personal data in its Cloud Service, publishes subprocessor information, and states customer data is hosted in the selected region.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Self-managed data stays under customer infrastructure; Elastic says it does not access customer content in self-managed deployments unless cloud-connected services or support are involved under their terms.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Elastic Inference Service may process requests in a different nearby region than the hosted deployment; its region list and routing depend on service use and region preferences.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Elastic Observability; canonical URL https://www.elastic.co/observability. The solution is built on Elasticsearch and Kibana.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Active offer. Current pricing, 2026 company announcements and current release notes show Elastic Observability in active development.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Elastic completed the Deductive AI acquisition on 2026-08-24. Elastic says the technology adds AI-assisted production incident investigation and root-cause analysis; integration roadmap details were still to come in that announcement.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Elastic completed the Keep acquisition on 2025-05-21. Its alert correlation, noise reduction and workflow automation were announced for integration with Elasticsearch and Kibana; the acquisition blog said Keep would remain open source.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Elastic completed the Jina AI acquisition on 2025-10-09. The release describes multimodal and multilingual models and retrieval technology for the wider Elastic platform.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: The legacy Uptime app is deprecated from version 8.15; Elastic directs users to Synthetics. No Elastic Observability shutdown or sunset was published in the checked product page, release notes/deprecations, blog or newsroom.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: The default Elasticsearch and Kibana distribution is under Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2). Eligible source code can be used under AGPLv3, SSPL 1.0 or ELv2 as stated in source headers; code under x-pack is ELv2-only.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: The free self-managed Basic subscription is available at no charge. The license FAQ says select features are available under SSPL or Apache 2.0; the exact license remains file/component-specific.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: Paid self-managed Platinum and Enterprise are commercial subscription entitlements, not a blanket open-source license. Platinum is existing customers only; Gold is discontinued; Enterprise remains offered.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Public product and versioned reference docs, GitHub repositories, Elastic Discuss forum and community channels are available.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Hosted Standard lists web support with a 3-business-day target for Cloud platform matters; Gold lists business-hours phone/web support; Platinum and Enterprise list 24/7/365 and 1-hour / 30-minute urgent response targets respectively.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Self-managed paid support is governed by subscription/support agreement; Basic public pricing does not list a response-time SLA.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Customer handles sizing, upgrades, security, lifecycle and snapshot repository/backup setup; Elastic publishes upgrade, backup/restore and security guidance.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Elastic advises taking a snapshot before upgrade; Elasticsearch cannot be downgraded after upgrade begins, and rollback needs a compatible snapshot.

facts.value: Raw frames remain alongside mapped/retraced results; partial mapping possible; no substitution from a nearby build. Caught iOS Swift errors use capture-call stack and are not dSYM-mapped.

facts.value: Register build order as unique positive integer, then mark a mapped issue fixed in a registered release. Same/newer registered release reopens it; older stays resolved; unknown builds increase uncertainty.

facts.value: No edit/delete of current release-order registry; no retrospective rescan; current fixed-release cycle only; native release policies outside completed release-aware regression scope.

facts.value: No distributed backend spans, database-query tracing or service code profiler established for documented offer.

facts.label: Event subscription model
facts.value: USD fixed-capacity plan, measured in successful ingested events/month. 2026 Pro unit rate is USD 3/M; entry is USD 150/month for 50M events, not a per-seat or host charge.

facts.label: Separate metrics allowance
facts.value: Time-series metric observations consume a separate datapoints/month allowance: Free 100M; Pro entry 250M and up to 3.75B at maximum Pro capacity. They do not consume events unless sent as legacy event-based metrics.

facts.label: Period, renewal and tax
facts.value: Pro is billed in advance monthly or annually; sales tax is extra. Upgrades prorated immediately; downgrades use the next billing cycle without a mid-cycle refund. Fees are generally non-refundable/non-cancelable.

facts.label: Enterprise commitment
facts.value: Custom annual Enterprise plans start at 10 billion events/year; additional capacity and volume discounts are negotiated. Public per-event invoice rate/minimum contract amount not found.

facts.label: Ongoing free allowance
facts.value: Free forever: 20M events plus 100M time-series datapoints per calendar month, two Triggers, tracing, BubbleUp and OpenTelemetry support; unlimited seats/querying advertised.

facts.label: Free card and use conditions
facts.value: Official Honeycomb comparison page says Free requires no credit card and includes 20M events/month. Terms admit individual and organizational customers; no separate non-commercial-only Free restriction found in checked terms.

facts.label: Enterprise trial
facts.value: Enterprise evaluation is advertised by request. Public trial landing page gives feature examples but no fixed duration, included event capacity, card requirement or automatic-charge rule; MSA defers evaluation period to order form.

facts.label: Paid entry
facts.value: Pro starts USD 150/month, 50M events/month plus 250M datapoints/month; 100 Triggers, two SLOs, SSO and Honeycomb support. Larger Pro capacities reach 750M events and 3.75B datapoints.

facts.label: Paid optional products
facts.value: Frontend analysis and Archive/rehydration are Enterprise add-ons; Private Cloud is custom. Telemetry Pipeline separately advertises starting USD 0.10/GB.

facts.label: Free / Pro event overages
facts.value: First overage month: email warning. Second consecutive month: 10 days to reduce volume or upgrade; then API randomly accepts one in ten events and rejects nine. Unthrottle requires at least 72 hours below daily targets.

facts.label: Metrics enforcement and Enterprise
facts.value: Datapoint quota is independent and follows the same warning/10-day enforcement timeline. Both metrics and event usage must remain within limits for 72 hours to clear throttling. Enterprise is exempt from this throttling; order form governs overages.

facts.label: Burst protection
facts.value: Above twice the daily target, excess above the daily target can be excluded from monthly counting while still stored/queryable. Up to three burst-protected days/month separately for events and datapoints.

facts.label: Usage visibility and warnings
facts.value: Usage page tracks volume/daily target and warnings; selected Team Owners receive overage, burst and ingestion-limit emails. Sampling/filtering before Honeycomb reduces counted usage.

facts.label: Hard cap and per-app budget
facts.value: No configurable hard USD ceiling or per-dataset monetary spending cap found in pricing, usage, cost management, team notification docs or terms. Free/Pro enforcement limits data after a grace process instead.

facts.label: Events and logs retention
facts.value: Fixed 60-day retention from ingestion date, including Free/Pro. Changing plan retains existing data up to the applicable retention window.

facts.label: Time-series retention
facts.value: Current usage guide says 13-month fixed retention by default for time-series metric datasets; longer configured environment retention is honored.

facts.label: Extended retention and shorter retention
facts.value: Enterprise extended event retention is a quote-priced add-on. For shorter retention/deletion, usage docs direct customers to Support.

facts.label: People and recipients
facts.value: Unlimited seats are advertised. Trigger setup says no limit on recipient count; each recipient receives trigger state notifications as configured.

facts.label: Apps, datasets and environments
facts.value: Datasets group services/events within environments; API keys are scoped to environments. Security docs list 100 API keys/team, increasable through Support. No numeric plan-specific dataset/environment maximum located in checked plan/manage docs.

facts.label: Precise event counting
facts.value: A trace span counts as one event; each OpenTelemetry SpanEvent and Link also counts as one event. Each successfully ingested log record counts toward the same EPM pool.

facts.label: Legacy annual extension
facts.value: During grace, existing legacy customers can commit to a full annual term at legacy rate plus 20%; no monthly legacy extension. Otherwise move to a 2026 tier based on current plan, not actual consumption.

facts.label: Annual price detail
facts.value: Monthly and annual Pro choices are advertised, but current fixed annual tier totals/discount percentages were not found in pricing FAQ, change-plan guide or 2026 change notice.

facts.label: Unpublished plan-specific app caps
facts.value: No exact Free/Pro dataset or environment maximum located in pricing, environment/dataset management or team notifications, although notifications acknowledge enforcement of such limits.

facts.label: Log allowance and limits
facts.value: Each stored log is an event shared with traces. Public pricing FAQ limits events to 1 MB and 2,000 columns/attributes; oversize events rejected. Rejected/malformed/rate-limited events do not count.

facts.label: Sampling and loss
facts.value: Filter/sample before ingestion to reduce billed records; events rejected under Free/Pro quota throttling are not stored. Operational rate limits can return HTTP 429 separately from monthly quotas.

facts.label: Query and extra charges
facts.value: Unlimited querying/seats are advertised for core plans. Archive, extended retention, Frontend and Telemetry Pipeline are separate paid scopes; no core per-scan/per-query unit surcharge is listed.

facts.label: Archive and data-transfer rates
facts.value: No public complete archive rehydration/scan/export rate card or incremental retention price found in archive, pricing FAQ, usage and terms; add-ons direct customers to sales/account team.

facts.label: Home country
facts.value: United States: legal operator Hound Technology, Inc., d/b/a Honeycomb, with a San Francisco, California business/contact address.

facts.label: Buyer restrictions
facts.value: Individual users must be at least 18. Terms restrict embargoed jurisdictions, sanctioned/denied persons and use prohibited by applicable local law.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Application observability: traces, log analysis, time-series metrics, error investigation, triggers and SLOs. Investigation and alerting are the documented jobs.

facts.label: Frontend product boundary
facts.value: Frontend Observability and its Web/iOS/Android/React Native Errors views are Enterprise add-ons; basic OTLP trace/log analysis is available on lower tiers.

facts.label: Hosted service
facts.value: Vendor-hosted Honeycomb SaaS offers Free, Pro and Enterprise. Enterprise can also use Honeycomb-managed dedicated Private Cloud hosting.

facts.label: Self-managed / customer-hosted
facts.value: Honeycomb Private Cloud runs the full platform on AWS. Honeycomb-managed customer-hosted and fully self-managed models are documented, including air-gapped capability.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Supported OpenTelemetry versions across languages; official setup routes cover .NET, Node.js, Python, Go, Java, Ruby and browser JS; Honeycomb Android, Swift/iOS and React Native paths exist.

facts.label: Alert channels
facts.value: Email, Slack, PagerDuty, Microsoft Teams and custom webhooks. Webhook templates can connect other destinations; PagerDuty can route to its own on-call escalation.

facts.label: Credits and direct phone prices
facts.value: No Honeycomb native SMS/call rate, phone-country list or included phone-message credit allowance found in pricing, trigger and integration docs.

facts.label: Trigger confirmation and repetition
facts.value: Threshold must hold for one to five consecutive evaluations. Default limited mode sends triggered/resolved messages; continuous mode notifies every matching run and omits recovery. Per-group recovery mode is also documented.

facts.label: Quiet periods and limits
facts.value: Triggers can be disabled or scheduled in UTC day/time windows. GROUP BY evaluation checks at most 1,000 groups; narrow the query for full coverage. Free has two rules; Pro 100; Enterprise starts 300.

facts.label: SLO alerting
facts.value: Pro includes two SLOs; Enterprise starts 100. Burn alerts detect reliability-budget consumption and route through configured recipients.

facts.label: Runtime deployment fit
facts.value: OpenTelemetry instrumentation, browser SDKs, Android/iOS clients, Kubernetes/Collector paths and AWS Lambda extension. Private Cloud supports controlled/air-gapped AWS environments.

facts.label: Telemetry ingestion
facts.value: OTLP via supported OpenTelemetry exporters; Honeycomb Event/Batch API accepts structured events. Ingest API key and region-specific endpoint required; logs and spans share the event allowance.

facts.label: Log and metric paths
facts.value: OpenTelemetry SDK/Collector logs, structured JSON/libhoney and file/forwarder integrations; time-series metrics use dedicated metrics datasets with separate observations allowance.

facts.label: Core setup
facts.value: Choose account region, create Team/environment, get ingest key, install supported OpenTelemetry SDK/agent or configure Collector, set service name and export endpoint, then generate and inspect telemetry.

facts.label: Private Cloud setup
facts.value: Work with account team on sizing/deployment, provision AWS components, integrate SAML/identity, email gateway and optional custom Slack app, then instrument applications.

facts.label: Core error coverage
facts.value: Investigate instrumented failed spans, exception events and error log records with full trace context. SDK coverage and filtering determine what reaches Honeycomb.

facts.label: Frontend error grouping
facts.value: Enterprise add-on Errors view groups/displays errors by message/type, error count, last seen and related sessions; Users Impacted is web-only, Devices Impacted is mobile-only.

facts.label: Log-pattern grouping
facts.value: Optional OpenTelemetry Drain processor derives log templates before export; group/filter/sample by the resulting pattern attribute in Honeycomb.

facts.label: JavaScript source maps
facts.value: Customer-run Collector source-map processor replaces minified stack symbols, loading maps from local disk, S3 or GCS. Web SDK compatibility starts 0.12.0; Collector requires CGO/glibc.

facts.label: Android and iOS symbols
facts.value: Collector Proguard processor uses Android mapping files; dSYM processor uses iOS build symbols. Files can be on local disk, S3 or GCS and are versioned by build UUID. SDK minima: Android 0.0.20, Swift 0.0.14.

facts.label: Deployment/version context
facts.value: SDK service.version attributes identify app builds; environment/dataset markers annotate deployments and other changes on charts.

facts.label: Fix/regression workflow
facts.value: No documented automatic resolved-in-release, regression reopen, commit-to-error assignment or manual issue merge/split workflow found in Errors, trace, marker or SDK guides.

facts.label: Error and session context
facts.value: Frontend error detail shows stack, attributes, first/last occurrence and related sessions, with links to session Timeline Analysis. Full traces/logs can carry customer-added user/tenant/release attributes.

facts.label: Visual session replay
facts.value: No DOM/video replay viewer, replay recording quota or replay price established in frontend Errors, product, Web SDK, pricing or archive docs. Session timelines show telemetry relationships.

facts.label: Log search
facts.value: Query Builder filters/groups structured fields, severity and messages; Explore Events has log-style display and search. Correlated trace/span IDs link application logs to traces.

facts.label: Archive and rehydration
facts.value: Enterprise add-on queries archived full-fidelity OpenTelemetry traces/logs in customer S3, rehydrating data missing because of sampling or normal retention expiry.

facts.label: Slow requests and databases
facts.value: Trace waterfalls expose span duration, errors and attributes; database spans show specific queries when instrumented. Heatmaps and BubbleUp help isolate unusual attributes and slow requests.

facts.label: Service map entitlement
facts.value: Service Map is listed in Enterprise, not Free or Pro. Core lower tiers still have distributed trace waterfalls.

facts.label: Continuous code profiling
facts.value: No first-party continuous CPU/heap profiling collector, retained-profile allowance or profiling rate established in current instrumentation, trace, pricing and frontend docs.

facts.label: Sampling strategies
facts.value: SDK deterministic head sampling supported; Refinery performs whole-trace tail decisions using dynamic, rule-based, throughput or probability sampling. Can retain errors while sampling routine success.

facts.label: Sample weighting versus invoice
facts.value: Sample rate metadata weights supported analytical calculations; Usage mode disables weighting. Monthly event allowance counts actually ingested records, not all requests represented by a sampled trace.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: Enterprise Frontend add-on has Web/iOS/Android launchpads and Core Web/Mobile Vitals with attribution and end-to-end trace propagation. Swift SDK supports iOS 13+ and enables unhandled-exception instrumentation by default.

facts.label: RUM pricing and session allowance
facts.value: No public session allowance, per-session frontend tariff or fixed add-on price found in pricing, frontend product/Errors and SDK docs; Enterprise account quote required.

facts.label: Private Cloud requirements
facts.value: AWS-based distributed services include EC2/EKS/ECS/Lambda, S3/RDS, ElastiCache, VPC and multiple availability zones; authentication, email and optional Slack integrations required.

facts.label: Numeric sizing
facts.value: No public fixed minimum CPU/RAM/disk or workload-to-AWS-instance sizing found in Private Cloud overview/architecture/deployment docs; account team sizes by throughput, retention and query concurrency.

facts.label: UI data retrieval
facts.value: Explore Events downloads CSV or JSON, selecting displayed fields or all fields; maximum 1,000 rows per download.

facts.label: Query API
facts.value: Query Data API is Enterprise. Create Query Result supports at most seven days of data per query, with endpoint limits 10/minute or 1/minute with Relational Fields; results are aggregates.

facts.label: Deletion
facts.value: Team Owners can delete datasets/environments with deletion protection disabled; deletion is permanent and can take minutes. Column-level/finer deletion requests go through Support.

facts.label: Leaving and purge timing
facts.value: Terms put pre-termination export on customer and permit deletion after termination; DPA says destroy customer personal data when account deleted, subject to law/policies. No fixed all-backup purge deadline found.

facts.label: Sensitive-data filtering
facts.value: Collector processors can remove attributes, redact patterns, hash values and filter telemetry before export. Protect API keys and scrub sensitive request/user data upstream.

facts.label: Encryption and access
facts.value: Security docs state encryption at rest and in transit; ingest keys can be enabled/disabled per environment. SSO is Pro+, AWS PrivateLink is Enterprise.

facts.label: Optional AI data handling
facts.value: Honeycomb Intelligence can be disabled; docs describe controls on AI processing. Customer telemetry is governed by DPA/terms, rather than the website privacy notice alone.

facts.label: Hosted storage choices
facts.value: Customer selects US-based or EU-based account at signup with distinct ui/api endpoints. Self-managed Private Cloud can keep data in the customer's AWS account.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Public DPA last updated 2025-05-22. Public subprocessor list names AWS for hosting/AI with US/EU residency selection, plus separate support, analytics and AI services.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Honeycomb; https://www.honeycomb.io/; supplied by Hound Technology, Inc., doing business as Honeycomb.

facts.label: Availability and acquisition
facts.value: Active product. Honeycomb announced its acquisition of Grit on 2025-04-10 to improve instrumentation and AI capabilities.

facts.label: Shutdown, sunset and ownership search
facts.value: No whole-product closure or announced acquisition of Honeycomb found in checked blog, News & Announcements, newsroom press releases and official-domain searches. /newsroom and /press guessed routes returned 404; /news/press-releases works.

facts.label: 2026 Pro change
facts.value: From 2026-07-01, new Pro rate USD 3 per million events, four tiers up to 750M/month; legacy rate USD 1.30/M. Legacy grace ends 2026-12-31, then migration at applicable billing boundary.

facts.label: SDK lifecycle notices
facts.value: Beelines and Honeycomb OpenTelemetry Distributions are unsupported; use supported upstream OpenTelemetry. Refinery 3.x is supported; the table gives Refinery 2.x maintenance only until 2026-04-01.

facts.label: Platform rights
facts.value: Honeycomb retains proprietary rights in the Service; access is contractual under Terms/MSA. No public open-source license or complete backend source release established for SaaS or Private Cloud.

facts.label: Open-source adjunct licenses
facts.value: Refinery and the OpenTelemetry Collector symbolicator have Apache License 2.0 LICENSE files in their official repositories.

facts.label: Private Cloud license detail
facts.value: Public deployment docs describe receiving software/packages/support, but no standalone Private Cloud license text, source rights or redistributable license grant was found in docs, terms or the public MSA.

facts.label: Help and support
facts.value: Public docs, Support Knowledge Base and Pollinators community. Pro includes Honeycomb support; Enterprise adds onboarding, enterprise support and Refinery support.

facts.label: Operational responsibilities
facts.value: Managed model: Honeycomb installs, updates weekly, patches, monitors and scales. Self-managed: owner installs, upgrades, backs up/tests recovery, patches and monitors; Honeycomb supplies weekly packages and Enterprise support.

facts.label: Public recovery details
facts.value: Detailed deployment/networking docs arrive closer to deployment; no complete public backup/restore command sequence or supported Private Cloud release/EOL matrix located in public architecture/models/lifecycle docs.

facts.label: Extra log charges
facts.value: No log-specific per-seat or per-query charge; 30-day search included. Base paid plan required, accepted ingestion above allowance metered only after alpha pricing begins; external platform drains can charge separately.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Uptime/HTTP/network/DNS checks, Playwright browser flows, cron healthchecks, server resource metrics, log ingestion/search, incident response/on-call and customer status pages.

facts.label: Deployment
facts.value: Vendor-operated monitoring/API/storage/status pages; installable server agents send system metrics to hosted service; cron clients send outbound pings.

facts.label: Runtime and client compatibility
facts.value: External protocol checks need no app SDK; browser runtime 2026.05 is Node 24/Playwright 1.59.1, JS/TS; legacy 2023.04 Node 16/Playwright 1.33. Logs support OTLP/HTTP SDKs and JSON/syslog.

facts.label: Channels and plan gates
facts.value: Free includes email/Slack/Teams; paid adds SMS, phone, PagerDuty/Opsgenie and other configured integrations. Native docs list Discord, Telegram, Google Chat and webhooks.

facts.label: Teammate SMS billing
facts.value: Essentials 20, Pro 75, Business 200 SMS credits/month across all account projects; extra 20 credits US$5, optional auto-recredit.

facts.label: Voice alert delivery and price gap
facts.value: All paid plans support calls through escalation policies; at most 1 call within 5 minutes across multiple monitor outages. No separate call-credit/rate or exhaustive country coverage established.

facts.label: Healthcheck delivery restrictions
facts.value: Missed-job alerts broadcast to project members/email and entitled SMS plus Slack/Discord/Telegram/PagerDuty/Opsgenie. No native on-call/escalation, Teams, phone or webhook for healthchecks per dedicated guide.

facts.label: Alpha log alert restrictions
facts.value: Log rules open an incident and dashboard bell notification only; currently do not page escalation policies or notification channels.

facts.label: Routing and acknowledgement
facts.value: Paid step-based escalation can page individual/everyone/on-call with delays; without policy all configured channels fire simultaneously. Acknowledgement stops repeat alerts, escalation continues until resolved.

facts.label: Grouping and schedules
facts.value: Grouping at project/policy level, windows 10 seconds to 1 hour or disabled; policy overrides project. On-call schedules 1/3/unlimited on Essentials/Pro/Business, with multi-timezone rotations/overrides.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Public endpoints checked remotely; private scheduled jobs can send outbound HTTPS. Server agent supports Linux/systemd and macOS/launchd amd64/arm64, Windows 10/Server 2016+ amd64; root/admin required.

facts.label: Data ingestion
facts.value: HTTP/network probes; heartbeat HEAD/GET/POST; server OTLP/HTTP; app logs HTTP JSON/NDJSON, OTLP/HTTP JSON/protobuf and RFC5424 syslog/TLS. Management APIs use bearer JSON requests.

facts.label: Setup paths
facts.value: HTTP: create project/monitor, choose protocol/region/interval/assertions, add channels/policy. Browser: provide Playwright script/envs. Cron: create schedule/grace and wire /start plus success URL.

facts.label: Logs/agent setup
facts.value: Create paid log source, select retention/copy one-time token, configure sender/drain; server install token enrolls local privileged agent to hosted pipeline.

facts.label: Protocol coverage and assertions
facts.value: HTTP/HTTPS default 2xx, configurable exact/range statuses, redirect behavior, required body keyword, custom methods/headers/body; ICMP, TCP port, DNS and Playwright browser protocols.

facts.label: IPv4/IPv6 and authentication
facts.value: HTTP/port/ICMP monitor uses one address family, IPv4 default or IPv6 only; both paths require two monitors. Authenticated requests use custom headers/body; browser credentials use encrypted envs.

facts.label: Frequency by plan
facts.value: Free 300 seconds minimum; Essentials/Pro 30 seconds; Business 20 seconds; Enterprise custom. API enum supports 10,20,30,60,120,180,300,600,1800,3600,21600,43200,86400 seconds.

facts.label: HTTP timeout gap
facts.value: No exact configurable HTTP connect/response timeout bound or default established in checked monitor settings, creation schema, operational FAQ, logs and response-time guide.

facts.label: Browser runtime, cadence and limits
facts.value: Minimum 300 seconds on paid plans; API browser frequencies 300/600/900/1800/3600/21600/43200/86400. Headless Chromium, 2-minute global run cap, default 30-second per-test timeout configurable within run budget.

facts.label: 18 uptime regions
facts.value: San Francisco, N. California, N. Virginia, NYC, Toronto; São Paulo; London, Paris, Frankfurt, Amsterdam; Seoul, Mumbai, Bangalore, Singapore, Tokyo; Sydney; Bahrain; Cape Town.

facts.label: Region rotation and independent counting
facts.value: One check executes from one selected region at a time, rotating; failure triggers immediate checks from other selected regions. To independently run 3 locations every minute, create 3 single-region monitors per endpoint.

facts.label: Browser locations
facts.value: Browser checks run from Frankfurt and San Francisco; both selected by default in API; select a supported region for the one-location scenario.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and recovery
facts.value: On first failure, all other selected regions check immediately; all fail opens outage, any succeeds prevents outage. Browser failures retry from a second region; guide says recovery is confirmed but no exact general recovery-count threshold published.

facts.label: Maintenance
facts.value: Available all plans; schedule start/end, selected monitors stop checks, optional selected-page notice. Can recur weekly/monthly; notify now, X minutes before, or not at all.

facts.label: Certificate cadence and expiry
facts.value: Daily TLS check, around 04:00 UTC; initial threshold 1/3/7/15/30/60/90 days or never; reminders 30/15/7/3/1 below threshold. Validity/chain/hostname/revocation/outdated TLS checked.

facts.label: Domain expiry and DNS
facts.value: RDAP with WHOIS fallback; daily when expiry within 45 days, otherwise weekly. Dashboard new monitors 14-day threshold; API/MCP default off unless domain_alert_days set; threshold 7/14/30/60/90 or never.

facts.label: Search, tail and export
facts.value: Structured text/phrase/prefix/field/attribute/trace-ID search; no general OR; max1,000 chars/20terms, one query7days within last30.120searches/min/project, live buffer5,000, export10,000lines; broad queries can be refused.

facts.label: Pro and Business pages

facts.value: Subscriber notifications off stops email/SMS/Slack/Teams for creation/updates/resolution/maintenance and rejects new signups with403 subscriptions_off; existing subscribers retained. Unconfirmed signups deleted after30days.

facts.label: Status update sources
facts.value: Monitor outages automatically change affected service and create incidents; manual incidents/updates support investigating/identified/update/monitoring/resolved, post-mortems and maintenance. Every published update notifies chosen affected-service subscribers.

facts.label: Schedule, grace and timezone
facts.value: Simple interval or5-field cron plus timezone; API timezone defaultUTC, grace units seconds/minutes/hours/days. Product FAQ dashboard grace min1minute/default10minutes; cron follows schedule, handles DST.

facts.label: Paired start/success and failure
facts.value: Append /start to measure run duration, then ping root URL on successful completion;HEAD/GET/POST accepted. Missing ping after grace opens outage; next success resolves. No job exit code/output stored.

facts.label: Job history and billing count
facts.value: Last20pings retained, withtime/IP/method/user-agent and/start duration;24-hour chart. Each healthcheck consumes1shared monitor slot, not a published per-ping bill.

facts.label: Monitoring and log export
facts.value: Paid CSV reports, reporting/API JSON and subscriber API; Logs supports CSV/NDJSON export up to 10,000 newest matching lines, plus line JSON copy.

facts.label: Deletion controls
facts.value: Dashboard can delete monitors/incidents/subscribers; Owner can delete project and its data. Terms give 30-day export period; DPA returns/deletes processor data within 30 days after termination, law exceptions.

facts.label: Stored data and secrets
facts.value: Browser screenshots/traces can expose visited data. Browser env values encrypted and never returned by API; up to 50 variables, each 4,096 bytes. Log source token shown once, fingerprint stored; revoke takes effect within a minute.

facts.label: Log incident masking
facts.value: Five recent matching lines attached to a log alert incident are redacted for tokens, bearer/basic credentials, JWTs, common keys, password-like values, emails, card numbers and IP suffix.

facts.label: Unestablished global masking
facts.value: No universal pre-ingestion log-field scrubber, screenshot/replay default masking, per-request-body filter or tenant configurable at-rest key scheme established.

facts.label: Transport/storage security
facts.value: Published policies state TLS1.2+ in transit, LUKS disk/managed database encryption at rest, encrypted backups; DPA specifies LUKS/AES-256; passwords bcrypt-hashed.

facts.label: Primary region and transfers
facts.value: Primary account/application/database/backups in DigitalOcean Frankfurt, Germany; global probes process transient checks. Other providers handle status pages, communications, analytics and authentication internationally under safeguards.

facts.label: Logs/AI location limitation
facts.value: Logs and Ask Hyperping currently unavailable on EU-only accounts; exact log storage region and full AI-provider subprocessor/data-retention terms not established in checked current feature/legal pages.

facts.label: DPA and processors
facts.value: Public DPA covers processor data, controller role for vendor's own contacts; 14-day advance processor-change notice, 7-day objection, emergency replacement exception. Processor list offers notice subscription by email.

facts.label: Identity
facts.value: Hyperping; official site hyperping.com; contract with Hyperping SAS, Paris. App and API retain hyperping.io hostnames.

facts.label: Shutdown/acquisition search
facts.value: Active Free and paid offers; no service-wide shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in checked official product/about/blog/legal/status pages.

facts.label: Legacy status-page maintenance ends
facts.value: Official migration guide says status-page v1 is no longer maintained and recommends v2; no hard retirement date given. Old CNAME status.hyperping.io changes to cname.hyperping.io.

facts.label: Current alpha and runtime editions
facts.value: Logs and Ask Hyperping labelled alpha; Logs unavailable for EU-only accounts. New browser checks default runtime 2026.05; legacy 2023.04 remains for existing checks, no automatic migration.

facts.label: Complete-service code/license
facts.value: Not applicable to established hosted edition; terms reserve service IP and grant limited access/use rights.

facts.label: Support and contractual response
facts.value: Public docs/API plus email/chat support. SLA for paid plans: initial critical response within 1 hour; high 4 hours; medium 1 business day; low 2 business days. Business/Enterprise priority.

facts.value: Kener does not instrument application runtimes through language-specific error SDKs. Website and service checks are configured in Kener; scheduled jobs can call a heartbeat URL over HTTP.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs

facts.label: Alert channels and costs

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Alert rules evaluate status, latency or uptime; configurable failure and success thresholds determine TRIGGERED and RESOLVED states. Severity can be CRITICAL or WARNING, and an alert can create an incident.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Confirmation grace period can require 1–60 consecutive check results before status changes are committed; default 1 means the feature is off. Alerts separately use failure and success thresholds.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Active maintenance windows override realtime monitor status on the public page. Recurring schedules use iCalendar RRULE; subscribers can be notified at reminder, start, completion and cancellation transitions.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Acknowledgement is part of the incident workflow, but no paging rotation, automatic repeat interval or escalation schedule was found in the alerting docs.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Deploy on Docker or Node.js. For source/Node deployment, current docs require Node.js 24.14 or newer and Redis; a relational database is used, with SQLite as the default and PostgreSQL/MySQL supported.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Monitor checks run from the self-hosted instance. Private endpoints and internal services can be checked if that server has network access; public status pages require the operator to expose the intended URL.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Kener publishes responsive public web pages and can run under a configured base path such as /status; no native mobile monitoring SDK is listed.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: REST API v4 provides authenticated operations for monitors, pages, incidents, maintenances, site configuration and monitoring data. The API documentation labels it a self-hosted API.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Heartbeat monitors accept GET or POST requests at /ext/heartbeat/{tag}/{secret}. A caller can report completion from a cron job, worker or external system.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Built-in checks include HTTP/API, Ping, TCP, DNS, SSL, SQL, heartbeat, GameDig, gRPC, Docker, group and Prometheus monitors. Kener is not documented as an OTLP log, trace or error-event backend.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Docker Quick Start: clone the official repository, set KENER_SECRET_KEY and ORIGIN, then run docker compose up -d; the page is exposed on port 3000 by default.

facts.label: Setup path

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: The v4 monitor overview lists API/HTTP(S), Ping/ICMP, TCP, DNS, SSL/TLS, SQL, Heartbeat, GameDig, gRPC, Docker, Group and Prometheus monitors. API monitor supports methods, headers, request bodies and custom evaluation; DNS validates expected record values.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: HTTP, TCP and other checks can target private endpoints if the Kener server can reach them. Authentication headers/body are supported for API checks; no separate private-probe service is required.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Monitors use cron expressions. The docs give 1-minute, 5-minute and 15-minute examples; the API example schedules every minute. A general supported range or minimum below one minute was not stated.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Timeouts are set by monitor type rather than one global plan value. API monitor defaults to 10,000 ms; TCP defaults to 1,000 ms; SSL defaults to 10,000 ms; Ping defaults to 1,000 ms with three packets.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Kener publishes no paid/free frequency tiers, as the software is self-hosted and does not meter runs.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Checks run from the instance operator deploys. Kener does not publish a selectable global probe map, a vendor private-probe option or location-based run billing.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Cross-region agreement or a vendor-managed retry network does not apply to the self-hosted checker.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry

facts.value: Docker + PostgreSQL 14 or newer tested; mount kuvasz.yml, configure database/admin secrets, run Compose, open port 8080 and add monitors/integrations through UI/API or YAML.

facts.label: Check types and HTTP assertions
facts.value: HTTP/HTTPS, SSL, ICMP, TCP connect, DNS record/code/drift checks, Docker health/resources and incoming push heartbeats. HTTP supports methods, expected status codes/headers, keyword case/negation and response-time thresholds.

facts.label: Check interval and HTTP timeout
facts.value: HTTP scheduled interval minimum 5 seconds; global HTTP read timeout defaults to 30 seconds and cannot exceed 30. Slow checks can delay the next nominal interval.

facts.label: Other protocol intervals and timeouts
facts.value: ICMP/TCP/DNS/Docker minimum interval 5 seconds. TCP/DNS/Docker timeout defaults to 5,000 ms, configurable 1–30,000 ms. Push expects at least a 10-second interval.

facts.label: Locations, private networks and counting
facts.value: Origin is wherever the operator deploys Kuvasz. Homepage explicitly says no built-in location-specific monitoring: deploy separate instances for several locations. HTTP/TCP can instead use selected HTTP CONNECT or SOCKS5 proxies.

facts.label: Failure confirmation
facts.value: Configurable consecutive failure-count threshold defaults to 1. Push missed-heartbeat failures count at most once per heartbeat interval and reset on a received heartbeat.

facts.label: Maintenance and host-connectivity check
facts.value: Maintenance can be manual, recurring cron + duration, or one-off start + duration; select monitors/categories or all. Optional connectivity check suspends locally initiated checks while host egress is unavailable.

facts.label: Certificate/domain expiry
facts.value: HTTP monitor SSL checking defaults off; when enabled, warns at a configurable expiry threshold default 30 days, minimum 0. Domain-registration expiry is explicitly listed unsupported.

facts.label: Page counts, branding and access
facts.value: One built-in page plus multiple custom pages. Default page only works with 100 or fewer enabled monitors. Custom pages choose named monitors/categories and can be public or authenticated; title, logo, favicon and colour palette are configurable.

facts.label: Own domain and extra page limits
facts.value: Own-domain/subdomain status pages documented through a reverse proxy; no numerical custom-page/component quota or branding-removal entitlement published.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: No public subscribe/unsubscribe workflow, subscriber allowance, customer-email credits or per-update delivery pricing established.

facts.label: Update source and freshness
facts.value: Monitor-driven status and automatic incidents; private/public human notes can annotate incidents. Page refreshes in place every minute; default server cache lifetime is 5 minutes.

facts.label: Public incident display
facts.value: 30-day uptime/latency/history view, limited by shorter retention; only public notes appear. Error details, private notes and notified integrations remain private; SSL incidents are not displayed.

facts.label: Job timing and grace
facts.value: Heartbeat interval in elapsed seconds, minimum 10; grace-period default 0 seconds, plus configurable consecutive-missed-interval threshold default 1.

facts.label: Failure and heartbeat signals
facts.value: GET or POST /api/v2/push-monitors/heartbeats/{clientSecret} marks Up; /failure marks Down explicitly and can accept a JSON error message. Missing pushes become Down after timing/confirmation rules.

facts.label: Run output and start/end coverage
facts.value: No separate start signal, paired start/end run record, execution-duration timer or stdout capture allowance established.

facts.label: Runtime and hardware
facts.value: Docker plus PostgreSQL minimum tested version 14. Official up-to-1,000-monitor guidance: Kuvasz 768 MB RAM and at least 1 CPU; database benchmark allocation 512 MB RAM.

facts.label: Disk sizing and larger installs
facts.value: Official check-history approximation is 200 bytes/check (Docker about 330); disk = checks/day × (retention days + 1) × bytes/check. Up to 5,000 monitors: app 1.5 GB with -Xmx768M, database 1 GB in its tests.

facts.label: Configuration export, import and deletion
facts.value: YAML export/import for monitors, status pages and maintenance windows through UI and REST API; DELETE removes monitors and recorded events/metrics.

facts.label: History retrieval and metrics export
facts.value: JSON REST lists/stats/events/incidents; 4.6.0 adds paginated v3 lists. Prometheus scrape and OTLP metric export are optional and disabled by default.

facts.label: Sensitive URLs and outbound payloads
facts.value: sensitive-url defaults false; enabling it masks the HTTP monitor URL in metrics, logs and notifications. Cross-origin propagation of custom headers defaults false; cookies stay within their originating origin/check.

facts.label: Configuration secrets and access
facts.value: Environment placeholders, separate configuration files/Docker secrets, OIDC allowlist and separate REST/MCP keys are documented. Proxy/Docker host credentials remain in config rather than the database.

facts.label: Storage location
facts.value: Monitoring data is in the operator's PostgreSQL database; location is chosen through deployment/database configuration, not a vendor region selector.

facts.label: DPA, privacy and data terms
facts.value: No product DPA, subprocessor list, published privacy policy or hosted data-region agreement established.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Kuvasz Uptime, also called Kuvasz; official site https://kuvasz-uptime.dev/ and repository kuvasz-uptime/kuvasz.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Active project; latest non-prerelease API result is 4.6.0, published 2026-10-25T14:56:09Z; repository is not archived or disabled.

facts.value: API v1 end of life was 2025-12-31, with removal scheduled for the next feature release. 4.6.0 deprecates the full-list v2 endpoints in favour of paginated v3 lists; other v2 operations remain.

facts.value: GNU Affero General Public License version 3 (AGPL-3.0 as labelled by the project); complete official source in kuvasz-uptime/kuvasz.

facts.label: Help and support
facts.value: Public documentation, API reference, GitHub bug reports and security email admin@kuvasz-uptime.dev; optional Ko-fi/GitHub sponsorship.

facts.label: Updates and supported versions
facts.value: Update image tag and restart unless release notes say otherwise; UI/settings can check for updates. Security policy supports 3.x and 4.x; 1.x and 2.x unsupported.

facts.label: Backup, restore and security
facts.value: YAML backup/import/dry-run covers configuration; whole PostgreSQL history backup/restore remains the operator's responsibility. Standalone Docker runs root by default; non-root recipe and Helm non-root/read-only defaults are documented.

facts.label: OpenTelemetry telemetry limits
facts.value: Per project: 3,600 requests/hour separately for traces, metrics and logs; 2,000,000 combined spans/metric points/log records per UTC day, including no more than 200,000 log events. A single decompressed body is capped at 1 MiB; 500 items/request; 2,000 spans/run.

facts.label: Bill controls

facts.label: Data retention — incident history
facts.value: Closed incidents are retained for one year and pruned nightly; active incident state is not removed by ping-record pruning.

facts.label: Data retention — failure detail and signature
facts.value: Posted failure-detail bodies stay with incidents for one year. A one-way failure hash and scrubbed 512-character excerpt stay until that monitor is deleted.

facts.label: Data retention — alert delivery records
facts.value: Delivered-alert records are retained 90 days. Waiting deliveries are not pruned by age.

facts.label: Data retention — monitor and account configuration
facts.value: Monitor configuration and account email remain until deleted.

facts.label: Data retention — trace metadata
facts.value: Agent span and trace metadata are retained 30 days; run summary totals, dependency aggregates and daily usage totals are retained 90 days.

facts.label: Data retention — agent logs and error text
facts.value: Agent log events are retained 30 days. Failed-tool error text is retained with its span/log event for 30 days and capped at 512 characters after redaction by default.

facts.label: Data retention — opted-in prompt and command content
facts.value: Not stored by default. If the monitor owner opts in, retained for 30 days with secret-shaped values redacted on ingest.

facts.label: Data retention — ingest diagnostics
facts.value: Telemetry accept/refusal diagnostics are retained seven days; no key or request body is stored in them.

facts.label: People, apps and projects — accounts and monitor counts
facts.value: No monitor cap is advertised for individuals. No limit on project count or additional account users/seats is published.

facts.label: People, apps and projects — destinations
