facts.label: People, apps and projects — status pages
facts.value: Free individual accounts have one public status page per project; private pages are unlimited.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Agent logs are accepted over OTLP/HTTP. They share a 2,000,000-record daily project budget with spans and metric points; at most 200,000 log events/day. Per-request cap is 500 records; request/hour limit is 3,600. Over-limit sends are refused with 429.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Not applicable to the current individual offer: no query or storage charge is published, and the individual account is free.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: Country of the operator and a buyer-country eligibility list are not stated in the checked About, Terms or Privacy pages. Terms choose Georgia law; that is not evidence of the operator's home country.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Dead-man's-switch monitoring for cron and scheduled jobs, CI/CD runs, public HTTP endpoints, and AI-agent runs; also offers agent traces, metrics and logs. Monitors detect failures; public status pages communicate selected monitor state.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: The complete monitoring service is vendor-hosted. The public repository contains CLI/MCP client pieces, not the hosted monitoring backend; no full service self-host instructions were found.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: A monitor can receive plain HTTP requests from any language or shell; no embedded SDK is required for heartbeat checks. Official setup guides include Python, Node.js, Ruby, Go, PHP, Bash, Java, .NET, Rust and Deno.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs — destinations
facts.value: Nine destinations are documented: verified email, Slack, Discord, Telegram, HTTPS signed webhook, ntfy, Pushover, Microsoft Teams and Google Chat.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs — delivery
facts.value: Free individual offer includes alerting; verified email is attached to a new monitor automatically. No additional channel charge or message quota is published.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation — event types
facts.value: Eight event types: down, fail, recovery, every-run, success, started, blocked and note. An explicit failure opens an incident immediately; next success closes it.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation — routing and templates
facts.value: Destinations can be assigned per monitor and event; users can set per-event message templates. Monitors can be paused to stop alerting.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation — repeat and escalation policy
facts.value: A timed escalation chain, repeat interval and on-call schedule are not described in the checked alert docs.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation — flap damping
facts.value: HTTP docs say a failure that recovers within the damping window does not page. Exact damping duration is not published on the page.

facts.label: Deployment fit — public HTTP
facts.value: HTTP probes run without installing an agent and are limited to publicly reachable URLs. Private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses are refused.

facts.label: Deployment fit — jobs and scheduled workloads
facts.value: Heartbeats use an outbound URL request, so any environment that can make HTTPS requests can report. Official guides cover cron, Kubernetes, systemd, serverless schedulers, CI workflows, orchestrators and common hosted job platforms.

facts.label: Deployment fit — CLI
facts.value: Optional lastping CLI binaries are documented for macOS and Linux, amd64 and arm64; Windows builds are linked from the repository releases.

facts.label: Sending data in — ping API
facts.value: Heartbeats accept HTTP success, start, fail, exit-code, blocked and progress/note signals on unique monitor URLs. Plain HTTP GET/POST works; the cron guide recommends curl with retry flags.

facts.label: Sending data in — CI webhooks
facts.value: Signed CI events are supported for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and Jenkins. The docs describe workflow/run URLs and failure context; GitHub step names require subscribing to workflow-job events.

facts.label: Sending data in — OpenTelemetry
facts.value: Agent traces, metrics and logs can be sent over OTLP/HTTP using protobuf or JSON; gzip is accepted. gRPC is not accepted. Traces include model/tool spans, tokens, estimated cost and dependencies.

facts.label: Setup path — heartbeat
facts.value: Create a monitor, choose interval/cron schedule and grace, copy its unique URL and append a curl request after success. Verified email is attached automatically.

facts.label: Setup path — HTTP, CI and agent traces
facts.value: HTTP monitors are configured in the console with URL, method, interval, timeout, expected status and optional body keyword. CI uses a provider webhook. Agent traces use an OTLP exporter or setup instructions from the agent/MCP connection.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: Not an application exception tracker. It opens incidents for missing/failed job, CI, HTTP and agent-run signals; failure signatures group repeat job/agent failures, but general uncaught exception capture is not the product type.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: Source maps, native symbols and application stack traces do not apply to the documented dead-man's-switch and agent-run product.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: Application release tracking and regressions are not part of the documented monitor product. CI incidents include run/branch/commit links, which are build context rather than error-release tracking.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: User-session replay and browser breadcrumbs do not apply to this product. Agent spans and run steps are covered under agent telemetry fields.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: HTTP/HTTPS URL probe with GET, HEAD or POST; expected specific status or any 2xx; optional body-keyword assertion. This is not a browser journey, DNS, port or private-probe product in the checked docs.

facts.label: Check frequency
facts.value: HTTP interval is 30 seconds through 24 hours; default 60 seconds. Every interval is included for individuals.

facts.label: Timeout and assertions
facts.value: Timeout is configurable from 1–30 seconds, default 10 seconds. Probe checks reachability, expected status, and optional matching text in the first 64 KB of the response.

facts.label: Probe locations and counting
facts.value: HTTP docs do not list selectable probe locations, multi-location quorum or a per-location run-count rule. Data storage in Frankfurt does not establish probe geography.

facts.label: Private probes
facts.value: No private HTTP probe deployment is documented; HTTP checks refuse private IPs. Heartbeat checks can cover private jobs by sending an outbound ping.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and recovery
facts.value: HTTP grace is at least 2× the probe interval, preventing a single slow/dropped probe from paging by itself. The next successful probe closes an incident.

facts.label: Maintenance and retry rules
facts.value: The checked HTTP docs do not specify a scheduled maintenance window or configurable retry-count policy. A per-monitor pause exists in the general monitor docs.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Certificate-expiry and domain-expiry alerts are not described in the HTTP check reference or monitoring guide.

facts.label: Status-page limits and visibility
facts.value: Pages can be public or private. Free individual accounts allow one public status page per project; private pages are unlimited.

facts.label: Branding and custom domain
facts.value: Public page URL is under lastping.dev/status/<slug> and also app.lastping.dev/status/<slug>. Custom domains, white-labeling and branding controls are not documented.

facts.label: Subscribers and page notifications
facts.value: The docs describe shareable public/private pages, but do not describe a subscriber list or email updates to page subscribers. Monitor alert destinations notify the account owner, not necessarily status-page readers.

facts.label: Status update source and history
facts.value: A page reflects the status of selected monitors and includes uptime bars and incident history for up to 90 days. Updates are tied to monitored checks.

facts.label: Manual updates
facts.value: The checked status-page docs do not say whether an operator can post manual incident or maintenance notices.

facts.label: Schedule and grace rules
facts.value: Heartbeat schedules support a simple interval or cron expression with a selected IANA timezone. Grace controls how late a job may be; the API validates 60–31,536,000 seconds for heartbeat/CI monitors.

facts.label: Daylight-saving handling
facts.value: Docs accept an IANA timezone but do not specify LastPing's own daylight-saving transition behavior.

facts.label: Job failure signals and history
facts.value: Jobs can send success, start, explicit fail, exit code, progress step and note/log signals. Missing pings open incidents; a next success recovers. Ping/run-step data is kept 90 days; incidents one year.

facts.label: Job-specific output and CI failure context
facts.value: Optional /fail body carries failure detail; CLI wrapper can attach stderr tail. CI alerts can include a run URL, branch, commit and provider-reported failing stage where the provider supplies it.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: Agent tracing shows model/tool-call spans, dependencies, errors, latency percentiles, tokens and cost. It is scoped to agent runs and does not document general web-app request APM or profiling.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: The checked tracing docs give ingestion budgets and rejection behavior but do not state a user sampling control or sampled-request billing model.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: Browser/mobile real-user monitoring does not apply to the documented cron, HTTP-probe and agent-run product.

facts.label: Log search and archive
facts.value: Standalone general log search, archive tiers and archive retrieval are not described. Agent log events are a limited part of agent telemetry and have 30-day retention.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the complete service: official pages describe a fully hosted platform; the public repository contains clients, not the server.

facts.label: Export and deletion — export
facts.value: Terraform export can download HCL for monitors, destinations, routes, templates and status pages. API endpoints can list recent pings and incidents; a complete raw-history archive/export format was not found.

facts.label: Export and deletion — deletion
facts.value: Users can delete monitors and associated ping history/incidents in the console. Account deletion is self-serve and immediate; email fallback promises deletion within 14 days.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls — defaults
facts.value: Prompt, command and tool content is dropped at ingest unless the monitor owner opts in. Secret-shaped values such as keys, tokens and passwords are redacted either way.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls — failure bodies and excerpts
facts.value: /fail can store up to 10,000 bytes of plain-text failure detail. Stored excerpts are scrubbed; failed-tool error text is redacted and limited to 512 characters by default.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls — request protection
facts.value: HTTP monitors refuse private, loopback and metadata addresses. Outbound alert webhooks block private/local and metadata destinations; webhook messages carry HMAC signatures.

facts.label: Storage regions
facts.value: AWS eu-central-1, Frankfurt, Germany. The policy says data at rest and core ping processing stay in Frankfurt; AWS global edge services are administered from us-east-1.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessor terms
facts.value: No DPA or named transactional email provider was linked in the checked Terms and Privacy pages. AWS is named as cloud provider.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: LastPing; canonical marketing and product identity at lastping.dev. No former product name found.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Active offer and current “Start free” invitation. No whole-product shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in the official pages checked. Changelog's newest dated release is 2026-10-06.

facts.value: The CLI and stdio MCP client repository is MIT. The hosted service is not in that repository; no server license or self-hosted edition was found.

facts.value: No response-time commitment found; Terms say the service is best-effort and has no free-tier uptime SLA.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable to the hosted backend. Users maintain any local CLI/MCP client they choose to install.

facts.value: Upload dSYM files manually or from XCArchive with the supplied scripts, usually in the release pipeline.

facts.label: Cross-platform symbols
facts.value: React Native Android plugin uploads composed JS source maps; iOS uses Xcode upload_build_phase.sh. Obfuscated Flutter needs generated Dart/native symbols.

facts.label: Symbol quotas and code context
facts.value: Per-plan symbol storage/retention/upload quotas and a general repository code-context guarantee were not found.

facts.label: Release/build association
facts.value: Events and spans carry app version/build metadata; stack mappings and build sizes are associated with uploaded builds.

facts.label: OTA patch association
facts.value: React Native patch UUID plus optional patchVersion tags events and matching source maps; Expo Metro plugin can inject the ID.

facts.label: Fix/regression and commit workflows
facts.value: Public error-issue resolved-in-version, automatic regression reopening, commit comparison and release-health gates were not established.

facts.label: Session context and replay
facts.value: Ordered screens, gestures, logs, network calls, errors and lifecycle changes with CPU/memory charts; default replay window five minutes before captured incidents.

facts.label: Visual context and platform exceptions
facts.value: Crash screenshots are optional and masked; no iOS crash screenshot and no Android 11+ ANR screenshot. Layout snapshots supply screen wireframes.

facts.label: User/request context and in-app reports
facts.value: User/session IDs and custom attributes link sessions; HTTP URL/method/status/latency/failure reason; bug reports permit 4000-character descriptions and five attachments.

facts.label: Replay billing and quota
facts.value: Replay/context bytes contribute to the shared data allowance; no distinct replay-session price or numeric replay-session allowance is listed.

facts.label: Search and retention
facts.value: Session search matches log bodies, IDs, event types, class names and exception traces; filters include version/device/network and custom attributes.

facts.label: Archival/replay of old logs
facts.value: A supported archive destination, restore path, archived-query rate and log-specific export contract were not found.

facts.label: Mobile trace diagnosis
facts.value: Nested custom spans with status, attributes and checkpoints can time HTTP requests, local database queries, functions and multi-step app flows.

facts.label: Native screen/network diagnosis
facts.value: Automatic first-frame spans for Android Activities/Fragments and iOS ViewControllers; client HTTP latency/status aggregated by endpoint patterns.

facts.label: Code profiling
facts.value: Android trigger-based profiling supplies Perfetto traces/heap dumps on supported OS versions; WorkManager needed for background uploads.

facts.label: Trace and HTTP sampling
facts.value: Traces and HTTP events default to 100%; dashboard can reduce to 0.001%. Launch metrics are also sampled separately.

facts.label: Profiling sampling and billing unit
facts.value: OS rate limit is one profile per trigger type/hour; extra SDK sampling is available. Plan billing remains bytes, including attachments.

facts.label: Real-user mobile performance
facts.value: Cold/warm/hot launches, first-frame load, HTTP failures/latency, CPU/memory series, Android ANRs and version-gated iOS hangs.

facts.label: Minimum machine requirements
facts.value: x86-64/amd64 Linux VM; Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or Debian 12; at least 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM and 100 GB boot disk; ports 80/443.

facts.label: Backend dependencies
facts.value: Docker/Compose or Podman; PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, object storage/MinIO, Valkey, Apache Iggy, API/ingest/worker/dashboard, cleanup/alerts and symbol services.

facts.label: Apple system-symbol storage
facts.value: For full iOS system-framework symbolication the guide asks for at least 500 GB additional disk and Google Drive API configuration.

facts.label: Read/export APIs
facts.value: JSON dashboard APIs retrieve sessions, errors and traces; session replay includes attributes, CPU/memory series and events grouped by thread.

facts.label: Downloadable artifacts
facts.value: Build mappings can be downloaded as mapping.txt, original native/JS files, or reconstructed .dSYM.zip. Android profiles can also be downloaded.

facts.label: Account privacy rights
facts.value: Personal-data access, correction and deletion requests may be made through settings or privacy@measure.sh, subject to legal retention.

facts.label: Telemetry deletion and bulk export gaps
facts.value: No complete public workflow for per-user telemetry erasure, immediate app/account telemetry deletion, bulk export format or export throughput guarantee was found.

facts.label: Network-data privacy defaults
facts.value: HTTP bodies and headers off unless URLs are explicitly enabled; six named sensitive headers are always excluded.

facts.label: Screenshot masking
facts.value: Default masks all text and media before upload; Android/Compose, UIKit, React Native and KMP use native inspection; SwiftUI starts fully masked.

facts.label: Collection and identity controls
facts.value: SDK start/stop and delayed autoStart; user ID clear/set; guidance to use hashed/anonymized IDs; log regex exclusions and severity filters.

facts.label: Cloud infrastructure and encryption
facts.value: Customer data is hosted on Google Cloud Platform; GCS uses AES-256 encryption at rest; APIs use TLS 1.2 or higher.

facts.label: Storage region, DPA and processor list
facts.value: No specific cloud storage region/region selector, public DPA text or complete named subprocessor list was located.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Measure; official site https://measure.sh/. The repository is measure-sh/measure.

facts.label: Active offer
facts.value: Free and Pro cloud subscriptions are advertised; a complete self-hosting guide and public releases remain available.

facts.label: Feature maturity
facts.value: The Memory dashboard is labelled beta. Several newer error features require versions beyond the getting-started examples.

facts.label: Software license and repository
facts.value: Apache-2.0; official repository https://github.com/measure-sh/measure.

facts.label: Docs and public support channels
facts.value: Public docs, GitHub issues, Discord community, hello@measure.sh; security reports via GitHub advisory or security@measure.sh.

facts.label: Support promises
facts.value: Plan-specific support response times, dedicated support entitlement and contractual uptime SLA were not found.

facts.label: Upgrade guidance
facts.value: Choose a stable vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH backend tag; fetch/checkout it and rerun installer; follow each required bridge migration in order.

facts.label: Newer migration instructions
facts.value: v0.14.x guide requires downtime, an analytics backfill and pausing cleanup during the backfill; released target availability unresolved.

facts.label: Backups, restores and security support period
facts.value: No complete official backup/restore runbook or release-support/EOL timetable was found. Security disclosure is documented.

apps.name: Middleware
apps.line: Monitors application errors, logs and uptime, with public status pages.

free.text: 100 GB/month telemetry, 14-day retention; card required

errors.math: Error events aren't what gets billed. The cost depends on telemetry data in GB and other usage.
Error events aren't what gets billed. The cost depends on telemetry data in GB and other usage.
Error events aren't what gets billed. The cost depends on telemetry data in GB and other usage.

uptime.math: An estimate for checks from one location. The own-domain status-page cost and the paid requirements aren't known.
An estimate for checks from one location. The own-domain status-page cost and the paid requirements aren't known.
An estimate for checks from one location. The own-domain status-page cost and the paid requirements aren't known.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Free Forever is $0 with monthly allowances. Pay As You Go meters telemetry at $0.30 per GB of metrics, logs and traces, plus separate RUM, synthetic, browser-test and OpsAI usage rates. The rate page shows $ but does not state a currency code.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Pricing calculator describes data volume as the sum of uncompressed logs, metrics and traces. Pricing FAQ says billing is measured daily by type/source and only data stored after pipeline drops is charged.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free Forever plan: $0; monthly 100 GB telemetry, 1,000 RUM sessions, 20,000 synthetic checks, 10 browser test runs and 2 million OpsAI tokens; unlimited users; 14-day retention; community support. Above-limit use is chargeable. A credit card is required to activate it; terms require business use and adult contracting capacity.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: Pricing page FAQ says 14 days of free use with unlimited ingestion; an August Google Marketplace announcement also says 14 days then PAYG.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: The newer Free Forever table and dated 2026-09 plan release advertise ongoing monthly allowances rather than a trial-only tier. Trial card/auto-conversion behavior is not resolved.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Pay As You Go has no advertised base subscription price; listed usage rates begin at $0.30 per GB of metrics/logs/traces, $1 per 1,000 RUM sessions, $1 per 5,000 synthetic checks, and $10 per 1,000 browser test runs.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: A required monthly minimum or minimum invoice amount for a self-serve paid account is not stated in pricing, billing FAQ, or terms. Terms allow recurring payment and make taxes additional; the pricing FAQ says PAYG can be cancelled anytime.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Free Forever includes monthly quotas; the September release says only usage above monthly allowances is charged. PAYG pricing lists per-unit rates for overage usage.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Configurable ingestion caps can automatically stop metrics, logs, traces, RUM, synthetic and browser usage when reached; a user must manually resume. Caps are enabled on request.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Ingestion caps are a documented hard ingestion stop after the configured signal/usage limit; access is enabled on request.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Billing/Usage shows plan, usage by product SKU, and estimated daily cost. A published account-wide dollar spend cap or automatic stop tied to invoice total was not found.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Free Forever: 14 days retention.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: PAYG: default 30-day retention.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Enterprise/custom contracts: custom retention. Privacy policy describes paid telemetry/log retention as 30 days by default and says customer requirements can extend it up to 180 days.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: On-premises data stays in customer-controlled cluster/object storage; public on-prem docs do not state a default search/retention period.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Hosted Free Forever includes unlimited users. FAQ says all plans allow unlimited users; SSO and role-based controls are described for paid tiers.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: The public maximums for projects/applications, synthetic monitors/browser tests, status pages and subscribers are not stated; published quotas are monthly usage allowances instead.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Free Forever allowance is shared telemetry volume up to 100 GB/month; PAYG telemetry rate is $0.30/GB. Pricing defines calculator data volume as uncompressed logs+metrics+traces, while FAQ excludes data dropped by pipeline.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Collection docs say agent collects 100% of logs by default; configurable Log Pipelines can filter/drop at source or ingestion. October 2026 release adds configurable telemetry caps that stop ingestion when reached.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Pricing includes “unlimited queries & search” for logs and lists no separate query-scan charge; main hosted meter is telemetry volume.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Enterprise cold-query storage uses customer's blob storage; public pricing does not specify any Middleware fee, retrieval fee or export charge for that option.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: Middleware Inc. lists headquarters in San Francisco, California, and an India office in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. The public terms require users to be at least 18 and to use the service solely for business purposes.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Application and infrastructure performance, APM traces, logs, frontend/backend errors, RUM, synthetic uptime/API/browser checks, alerting, OpsAI investigation, and public status pages. It detects from telemetry/checks and communicates status.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Hosted Free Forever and Pay As You Go plans are advertised; BYOC is custom-priced. The FAQ says private-cloud/on-prem use is limited to enterprise contracts.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: On-premises platform runs in the customer's EKS or AKS cluster; UI, ingestion, storage and alerting stay in that environment and customer S3 or Azure Blob storage. Installer access and installation guide come from Middleware.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: APM support matrix lists Java/Kotlin/Scala, Python, Node.js/NestJS/Next.js, .NET, Go, PHP, Ruby, Rust, C++, Elixir and Erlang; exact auto-instrumentation method differs by language/runtime.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: RUM SDK platform guides cover browser/JavaScript, Next.js, iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Alert-rule docs list email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Jira, Zenduty and webhook; multiple channels can be configured. No per-message charge is listed.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Status-page subscribers receive email notifications on incident creation and updates. The feature is beta; message quota or delivery charge is not published.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Alert rules support warning/critical thresholds, evaluation windows, grouped attributes with single/multi/custom aggregation, and repeat notifications while conditions remain active. Synthetic checks can require a configured failure count across locations and repeat on an interval.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Hosted APM supports Linux, Kubernetes, ECS, IIS and serverless integrations; APM support matrix describes methods and supported runtimes. RUM also supports web and native/cross-platform mobile SDKs; browser capture may be blocked by CSP/ad blockers or restricted by allowed origins.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Synthetic checks run from public Middleware locations and can target public services; docs provide allow-list IPs for protected endpoints. Browser tests support authenticated user flows.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Full on-premises platform is documented for customer AWS EKS or Azure AKS. The current guide lists these targets, not a generic single-node install.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs via OTLP/gRPC or OTLP/HTTP over HTTPS; existing SDKs or a Collector can send directly or through a customer pipeline.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Logs can arrive via Middleware Agent/APM SDK, Windows Event Logs, custom logs API, AWS/GCP/Azure, FluentD, Fluent Bit, Journald and Logstash.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Hosted server setup: install the Linux agent or choose an APM language agent/SDK or OTel Collector, provide the target and ingestion key, configure collection, then verify data in APM.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: RUM setup: create an app and add the platform SDK/script and token. Synthetic setup: choose protocol, assertions, schedule, locations and alert destinations; allow-list public probe IPs for restricted targets.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: On-prem: customer supplies EKS/AKS, storage class, about 260 GB dynamically provisioned volumes, object storage, domain, TLS certificate, network egress and cluster-admin kubeconfig; Middleware shares the installation guide during onboarding.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: Browser RUM captures uncaught/runtime frontend errors, XHR/network errors and console errors; the error list groups events by matching message and stack signature and shows instances/affected users.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: APM traces can record exceptions and stack traces; OpsAI creates grouped issues from supported APM/RUM errors, performance problems and telemetry. Public limits on error event retention/drop counters by error type were not found.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: Browser stack frames can be symbolicated with uploaded source maps; version must match app.version.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: APM exception details include exception type, message and stack frames; iOS RUM installation guide asks for dSYM upload per app version.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: RUM supports app.version and environment attributes to compare error impact across releases and match source maps to builds.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: RUM setup can connect GitHub or Bitbucket repository and deployed commit for code context/OpsAI; APM endpoint view includes deployment/dependency investigation. A separate issue regression/fix workflow was not found.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: RUM session explorer connects errors with browser/mobile sessions, user, environment, network, console and actions; session recordings are enabled by default in browser installation options.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: RUM session recording masks sensitive inputs by default; recordings end after 15 minutes idle or 4 hours continuous activity.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: No per-session replay retention period, separate replay charge, or replay-only quota beyond RUM session allowance is stated in checked pricing and RUM docs.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Synthetic monitors support HTTP, SSL/TLS, DNS, WebSocket, UDP, ICMP, TCP and gRPC. HTTP assertions can check status, latency and response content.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Multistep API tests chain requests and pass values between steps; browser tests record/replay real interactions and support Basic, Digest or NTLM authentication. Private endpoints may need probe-IP allow-listing.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Synthetic setup permits configurable frequency; guide recommends 30–60 seconds for critical APIs and 1–5 minutes for non-critical checks. No minimum/maximum interval by plan or maximum timeout is published in checked pricing/setup pages.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Browser tests can be scheduled, with examples at every five minutes, daily or weekly; a fixed minimum and maximum interval by plan are not stated.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Synthetic setup lists North Virginia, California, Hong Kong, Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Frankfurt, London, Paris, Central Canada, São Paulo, Bahrain and Cape Town. Each configured endpoint ping counts as one synthetic check.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: A private probe installation or customer-selectable private location is not described in checked synthetic setup/pricing docs.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Synthetic notification settings can require a chosen number of failures across all locations before alerting and can repeat notifications on an interval.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Public maintenance-window behavior for pausing synthetic checks or suppressing alerts is not described in the setup/pricing pages checked.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: SSL/TLS validity/expiration and DNS resolution are supported synthetic check types.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Log Explorer supports full-text/keyword search, attribute filters, AND conditions, raw JSON details, anomaly/pattern views, trace correlation and live/near-real-time logs.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Log Explorer Download exports selected columns and a selected number of records. Enterprise customers can use their own blob storage as a cold-query store; FAQ says no log rehydration charge.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: APM includes distributed trace waterfall/flame graph/span/map, endpoint latency/error breakdown, service map, continuous profiling and database monitoring; logs/host metrics can be correlated to a trace. Detailed query-level monitoring is documented for PostgreSQL and MongoDB; do not generalize that query inspection to every database integration.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: No fixed per-host quota or seat charge is listed for hosted plans; ingestion charges depend on telemetry usage. The public pricing table does not map every APM feature to a plan gate.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: Customer can sample in SDK or OpenTelemetry Collector using head/tail sampling; Middleware Trace Explorer's “Adaptive Sampling” affects trace-list statistics and does not change the trace list.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: Rate measurement for customer-sampled trace payloads is not fully specified beyond the shared telemetry GB meter and uncompressed calculator description.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: Browser and mobile RUM capture sessions, app/page performance, Core Web Vitals, network activity, errors/crashes and replay; allowance is 1,000 sessions free, then $1 per 1,000 sessions.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: RUM sessions can correlate frontend errors/slow pages to backend traces. Mobile SDK guides cover iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter; each has separate platform requirements.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Status Page is a public beta. Hosted mwstatus.com slug is documented; custom domain and removal of Middleware branding require active paid billing. Name/logo/theme/font are configurable.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Maximum pages/services and plan-based page limits were not found in pricing, beta overview, configuration, or getting-started pages.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Subscribers can opt into email and receive a message when incidents are created or updated; status page has a Subscribe toggle. Public Slack subscribe is listed as not yet available in the beta overview.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Subscriber caps, subscriber import limits and extra notification charges are not stated in the reviewed pages.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Status health can be derived from linked synthetic monitor results and incident updates; services can also be added manually. Status page polls recent uptime data from the last 10 minutes.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Incident workflow supports Investigating, Identified, Update, Monitoring and Resolved states with a public timestamped history; each saved update notifies subscribers.

facts.label: Schedule and grace rules
facts.value: Not applicable: no scheduled-task heartbeat/check-in monitor is documented. Synthetic schedules test endpoints, and Kubernetes job failure alerts are infrastructure alerts rather than a missed-run scheduler.

facts.label: Job failure signals
facts.value: Not applicable as a dedicated job monitor: no check-in ping API or start/success/failure heartbeat workflow was found in the product overview or docs.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: On-prem evaluation tier: AWS EKS 3 × m6i.xlarge or Azure AKS 3 × D4s_v5; up to 25 GB/day; total 12 vCPU/48 GB. Standard tier: 4 × m6i.2xlarge or 4 × D8s_v5; up to 500 GB/day; 32 vCPU/128 GB.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: High-volume sizing: 6 × m6i.2xlarge or 6 × D8s_v5, about 1 TB/day, 48 vCPU/192 GB; add one 8-core node per additional 100 GB/day.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Prerequisites include Kubernetes v1.25+, Helm 3.8+, kubectl, OpenSSL, default dynamic storage class (~260 GB volumes), customer S3/Blob, domain/TLS, network egress and cluster-admin kubeconfig.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Log Explorer offers a Download action with selectable columns and record count. Public API access is documented, but export formats/rate limits for all signal types are not established.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Customer owns uploaded data and may request deletion; the public terms say data is held for up to 30 days after termination for export/recovery, then may be deleted. Privacy policy permits account deactivation and access/erasure requests through support; a self-serve telemetry deletion workflow is not fully specified.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Browser RUM masks sensitive values/passwords by default before upload; all inputs or CSS-selected elements can be masked, blocked or ignored. Network capture is on by default, but request/response headers and JSON/plain-text bodies are not recorded by default because they can contain credentials/personal data.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Log Pipeline supports filtering/dropping data; privacy policy identifies logs, traces, metrics and performance data as customer data and potential personal data.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Hosting FAQ says SaaS services default to AWS/Azure in the US, with other regions/providers by request. GDPR page says processed personal data may be stored in AWS in US, Europe, Canada and India. Exact signal/account mapping is not explained.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: BYOC/custom contracts advertise data-residency control; on-prem data is kept in customer's cluster and own S3/Blob. GDPR page links adopted Standard Contractual Clauses; a public DPA was not located from checked legal/compliance pages.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Middleware; canonical URL https://middleware.io/. The official FAQ explicitly distinguishes this observability company from generic middleware/message-broker software.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Active hosted service and active product updates; release notes list v2.8.6 on 2026-11-04. No shutdown, sunset, or acquisition notice found in checked official pages.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: No official acquisition, closure, or sunset announcement was published in the checked blog, product-update archive, press-release page, docs changelog, or current offer pages.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: The public hosted service terms grant a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable right to use the service for internal business purposes.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: No public software license for the complete on-prem platform or public full-platform server repository was found. On-prem install access is provided for enterprise customers by the vendor.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Public docs, community Slack, support@middleware.io and contact form are published. Free plan says community support; no free response SLA is listed.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: PAYG includes a dedicated Slack/MS Teams channel; custom contract advertises dedicated account team and 24×7 support, with no response-time target in the public pricing page.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Customer provisions and operates Kubernetes, storage, domain, SSL and network dependencies. Middleware supplies an installation guide during onboarding; release note says on-prem platform is deployed with Helm.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Public on-prem-specific upgrade, backup, restore and security-maintenance procedures were not found in the on-prem page, prerequisites, changelog, or security pages checked.

facts.value: File and directory checks can detect existence, timestamp, checksum, size, content-pattern, permission, ownership and link-count changes.

facts.label: How billing works

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Yes. The GPLv3+ Agent is free for commercial or personal use and can be installed on any number of systems. The dashboard is free to use with it under NCUL1.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: APM starts at $15/node/month annually or $18.75 monthly and includes Infrastructure; each APM node adds 25 million app log events and 25 million trace spans per month.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Monthly node billing counts the maximum active nodes in the period, excluding offline/stale nodes and the top 10% of spikes. Annual commitments bill overage nodes at the standard rate.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Logs and traces use separate pooled quotas. Extra log events or trace spans cost $0.10 per million with annual rates or $0.125 with monthly rates.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: If renewal payments fail, the billing guide says Netdata retries weekly for 15 days; after three failed attempts the Space moves to Community and unsupported notification methods are disabled after 24 hours.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Pricing describes usage estimation, pooled quotas, and node usage reporting. I found no documented hard monthly spending cap that stops charges.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Agent metrics use three dbengine tiers by default: per-second data for up to 14 days, per-minute for 3 months, and per-hour for 2 years; each tier has a 1 GiB size limit.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Metric disk limits are soft targets, not hard caps. Agent may temporarily exceed configured size while it writes and rotates whole files; operators must leave disk headroom.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: In-place system logs follow systemd journal, Windows Event Log, or macOS unified-log retention. Linux journal time-based deletion is off by default; size is typically limited by journald settings.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Centralized OTLP logs default to up to 7 days, 1 GiB indexed data, or 100,000 indexed files, whichever retention limit is reached first. S3-compatible offload is optional and uses the customer's object store and lifecycle policy.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: OTLP traces have separate defaults of up to 7 days, 1 GiB indexed data, or 100,000 files, whichever limit is reached first. S3-compatible offload is supported.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Netdata Cloud stores node and user metadata, chart and metric names, labels, collectors, alert configuration, and status changes; metric samples and logs remain on Agents and Parents. Cloud does not publish a sample-retention period because it does not store those samples.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Agent installation is not capped by user, host, metric, container, or project quotas. Free local monitoring works on any number of Agents, subject to local capacity.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Cloud Community allows access to five nodes at a time and one custom dashboard per Room. Business unlocks unlimited nodes and custom dashboards; pricing says users are not charged per seat.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: Paid Cloud roles include Admin, Manager, Troubleshooter, Observer, and Billing. Room-scoped roles and sensitive-data permissions control access; SSO and SCIM are paid features.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Infrastructure nodes add 20 million application-log events/month to a shared account pool; APM nodes add 25 million. Overage is charged per event, not by raw or compressed GB.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Agents collect per-second metrics, auto-discover infrastructure, calculate anomaly signals, and evaluate health alerts locally.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: System logs from Linux, Windows, and macOS are queried from the operating system's local log store.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: OpenTelemetry logs and traces can be stored and indexed by the Agent; paid Cloud plans unlock centralized Logs Management and the Traces explorer.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Agents can run HTTP, TCP/UDP, ping, DNS, certificate, domain-expiry, and browser-journey checks.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Both. Netdata Agents and Parents run on the customer's systems. Netdata Cloud is a separate SaaS control plane; Enterprise can also run Cloud On-Prem, including air-gapped installations.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Netdata has no required per-language SDK for infrastructure data. It collects through native Agent plugins and supports Prometheus, OpenMetrics, StatsD, Nagios checks, and OpenTelemetry.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: The OTel receiver accepts metrics, logs, and traces via OTLP gRPC; OTLP HTTP is optional. The current OTel plugin is unavailable on Windows and FreeBSD, and exponential histograms are not ingested.

facts.value: Local Agent alerts can use email, Slack, PagerDuty, Twilio, Telegram, Opsgenie, and other local integrations; external delivery-provider fees are separate.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Agent alerts have warning and critical thresholds, templates, delay/hysteresis, configurable evaluation, and local silencing.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Cloud supports notification silencing by Room, node, label, alert, role, and schedule. Community users can create Cloud silencing rules; UI configuration and team features vary by plan.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Netdata documents no native on-call rotation, incident escalation schedule, or escalation policy engine.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Agents support Linux, Windows, macOS, and FreeBSD, plus Docker, Kubernetes, cloud VMs, network appliances, and edge devices; support level differs by platform.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Installation often requires root on Linux or Administrator on Windows for broad metric collection. Agent listens on TCP 19999 by default; OTLP receivers use 4317 and optional 4318.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Native Agent collectors gather host, application, database, cloud, container, Kubernetes, SNMP, and hardware metrics.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Agent supports OpenTelemetry OTLP metrics, logs, and traces via Collector to Agent; Prometheus exposition, StatsD, and Nagios check inputs are also supported.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Metrics can be scraped from /api/v1/allmetrics or pushed through Prometheus remote write, Graphite, OpenTSDB, JSON, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, MongoDB, and other connectors.

facts.value: Linux installation uses the kickstart.sh installer or packages; it detects the system, installs the Agent and starts collection. Docker, Kubernetes, Windows MSI, macOS, FreeBSD, and automation paths are documented.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: For OTel, install an Agent with its OTel plugin and an OTel Collector, send application telemetry to the Collector, then export to the Agent's OTLP endpoint.

facts.value: Systemd journal, Windows Event Log, and macOS logs support searchable fields, full-text search, histograms, and live tail from the existing OS log store.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Centralized OTel log storage supports indexed search, live query, optional object-store offload, and query-through retrieval. Business access is required for Logs Management views.

facts.value: The OTel Traces explorer shows traces and spans, service/span filters, timing, attributes, status, and request waterfalls; RED views summarize rate, errors, and duration.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: No code-level CPU profiler or automatic database-query profiler was found in the Agent, OTel, and integration docs checked.

facts.value: Cloud trace quotas count spans, and overages are per million spans. I found no Netdata-side trace sampling control in the OTel ingestion and billing docs; sampling may be set upstream in the OTel SDK or Collector.

facts.value: Optional Real User Monitoring collects Core Web Vitals, page views, sessions, JavaScript errors, and clicks. Annual subscription starts at $250/month for 500,000 sessions; annual rate is $0.50 per 1,000, or monthly usage costs $0.625 per 1,000 sessions.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: Netdata can alert on metric thresholds and OTel span error status, and can search error log records. The checked product and OTel docs do not describe SDK exception-event grouping or duplicate-issue aggregation.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: I found no source-map upload, crash symbolication, or exception stack-trace processing workflow in the OTel, RUM, and integration pages checked.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: Deployment annotations can mark changes in time-series charts, but error grouping by release, regression tracking, and source-control links were not found in the checked docs.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: RUM records sessions and browser signals, but the checked RUM and privacy docs do not document replay video, breadcrumbs, or exception-linked session replay.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Agent-run synthetic checks include HTTP, TCP/UDP, ping, DNS, TLS certificates, domain expiry, and S3-compatible storage; browser journeys use Playwright.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: The HTTP endpoint collector defaults to a 5-second collection interval and 1-second request timeout; interval and timeout can be configured.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Synthetic checks run from the customer's Agents. API and uptime checks are not billed by run; Cloud Business node billing still applies to active connected Agents.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: HTTP checks can validate response codes, body regex, headers, auth, and TLS. Alerts can be silenced for a scheduled maintenance window; a shared multi-location confirmation rule was not found.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Synthetic checks include TLS certificate state and domain-expiry collectors; the pages checked do not state standard notification lead times before expiry.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: A standalone Agent typically uses 1–5% of one CPU core by default, 100–200 MB RAM on an empty system, 250–350 MB in typical production, and about 4 GiB disk at default retention.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Parent memory depends on metric count; docs estimate about 16 KiB per unique metric plus configured cache, or roughly 16 GiB for one million concurrent series. Parent disk should be sized for all children and tier retention.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Root is required for Linux installation and broad system metrics; Windows installation and service need Administrator. The Agent's OTel plugin is unavailable on Windows and FreeBSD.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Agent REST APIs query metrics, alerts, configuration, and metadata; export options include Prometheus, Graphite, OpenTSDB, and other databases.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Cloud nodes can be removed from a Space; Agent uninstall removes data on most Unix installs, while Windows MSI removal leaves the metric database and edited config until manually deleted.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Cloud roles gate access to logs, process lists, network connections, database query text, and other sensitive views. Cloud receives metadata; monitoring samples stay on the Agent and Parent.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls

facts.label: Enterprise and currency
facts.value: More than 200 monitors: custom pricing. New accounts EUR; USD available through support at fixed published rates; no other billing currency currently offered.

facts.label: VAT display wording
facts.value: Current pricing says EUR prices exclude VAT; terms say quoted EUR prices include applicable Belgian VAT where required. Wording unresolved as to displayed versus final price.

facts.label: Billing changes, cancellation and refund
facts.value: Monthly/yearly in advance; plan changes immediate and prorated; cancellation stops next renewal and preserves access to period end; new customers can request full refund within 30 days of first payment.

facts.label: Ongoing free service
facts.value: No ongoing free monitoring tier advertised; public offer is paid, starting EUR 15/month. A no-card 10-day trial and standalone free tools are separate.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: 10 days with all features; no credit card/payment information required.

facts.label: AI introductory allowance
facts.value: Product page says first five AI runs use Oh Dear's account; guide calls them first five AI calls. Afterwards use own provider key.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Solo: 2 monitors for EUR 15/month or EUR 150/year; USD 17/month or USD 170/year; all features, unlimited users/status pages/notification destinations; 10 pooled cron tasks.

facts.label: Capacity overflow and paid additions
facts.value: Standard bundles limit monitored sites; cron guide says upgrade for more tasks; task FAQ also offers paid task add-ons, with no public add-on rate.

facts.label: Cron ping rate and pruning
facts.value: Up to 5 pings/minute/check; extras ignored. Scheduled-task check acts on the latest ping within a minute; older successful events are pruned.

facts.label: Crawler and JSON limits
facts.value: Crawler stops at first 5,000 reachable pages or 20 minutes per monitor/run. Uptime JSON assertions fail on invalid/empty or larger-than-2-MB JSON body.

facts.label: Known bill controls
facts.value: Flat selected subscription capacity; plan changes initiated in billing portal and prorated. AI frequency can be reduced and provider key/model chosen; own SMS provider has its own bill/caps.

facts.label: Hard caps and warnings
facts.value: User-set Oh Dear monetary cap, per-monitor AI token budget and spend-warning thresholds not established.

facts.label: General monitoring retention
facts.value: Privacy says monitoring data follows subscription plan, typically 1 to 2 years; exact plan-to-signal matrix not supplied.

facts.label: Check run records
facts.value: Approximately 10 days before run records are automatically pruned; per-type report endpoints can have different detailed artifact histories.

facts.label: Performance precision tiers
facts.value: Minute metrics roughly 14 days; hourly metrics a couple of weeks; daily metrics indefinitely.

facts.label: Application-health history
facts.value: Up to 30 days, keeping the most recent 30 results per health check.

facts.label: Lighthouse reports
facts.value: Six months of runs, scores, metrics and full Lighthouse report.

facts.label: Cron events
facts.value: Every failure or missed event retained in full; around last ten successful pings retained, with older consecutive successes pruned. Exact failure-history lifetime not specified.

facts.label: Webhook and public-page views
facts.value: Webhook delivery logs 5 days; status-page uptime history configurable 30/60/90 days, default 60.

facts.label: AI artifacts and total public-incident history
facts.value: Exact lifetime of AI prompts/responses/screenshots/raw provider responses and written status updates not established beyond generic run-list/general policy rules.

facts.label: Capacity and allocation
facts.value: Plans cover 2/5/10/25/50/75/100/150/200 monitor slots, with custom tier above 200; AI monitor is one slot; cron quota = five tasks × purchased site capacity, pooled freely.

facts.label: Users, teams and restricted access
facts.value: Unlimited users; Admin full access, Member cannot change team/billing settings, Guest read-only. Restrict people to selected sites/status pages. Each additional separate team needs its own subscription.

facts.label: Home country and buyer eligibility
facts.value: Immutable VOF, Hemelshoek 277, 2590 Berlaar, Belgium; VAT BE 0699.594.682. Users must be at least 18 or have parental consent; monitor only with proper authorization.

facts.label: Agency/reseller conditions
facts.value: Formal reseller agreement required for reselling/rebranding or billing clients primarily for Oh Dear-powered monitoring. Own sites or monitoring within a broader development/hosting/IT engagement need no reseller agreement.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Uptime/HTTP API assertions, ICMP/TCP, SSL, DNS/blocklists, domains, port scans, broken links/mixed content, sitemaps, synthetic performance/Lighthouse, application-health JSON, cron, AI browser checks, status pages and reports.

facts.label: Hosted/self-hosted delivery
facts.value: Vendor-operated monitoring/storage/status pages; configure public checks, expose a protected health JSON endpoint, or send cron pings. Management SDK and integration packages run client-side.

facts.label: Clients and runtimes
facts.value: Official PHP management SDK; cron examples for shell/cURL/wget, PHP including Laravel/Symfony, Python, Ruby, Node.js, Perl and Go; health works with any language returning required JSON.

facts.label: Alert channels
facts.value: Email automatically configured at signup; Slack, Vonage SMS, Discord, Telegram, Teams, Pushover, ntfy, Opsgenie, Google Chat, PagerDuty and signed webhooks; unlimited destinations.

facts.label: SMS costs and country scope
facts.value: Bring own Vonage API key/secret; country-based messages billed by Vonage. Oh Dear has no bundled SMS credits or native Twilio/MessageBird/AWS SNS integration per its FAQ.

facts.label: AI failures versus execution errors
facts.value: AI sends notifications when the prompt asks; repeated OK notifications held back by default. Error means check could not complete and does not send a notification.

facts.label: Routing and quiet hours
facts.value: Team, per-monitor, tag/tag-group/wildcard rules; per-site team override; each channel selects events and all/inside/outside business hours in team timezone.

facts.label: Acknowledgement and snooze
facts.value: Failing check acknowledgement silences repeated down alerts but keeps recovery, ending at recovery/timer. Healthy-check snooze mutes both directions until timer. Individual cron/health checks supported.

facts.label: Repeats and threshold controls
facts.value: Uptime default two confirmed-down minutes before alert; configurable. Hourly outage reminders until recovery or acknowledgement. Health: one alert per failing health check/hour plus recovery. AI can wait up to 20 failed runs.

facts.label: Webhook delivery failure
facts.value: Up to 3 delivery attempts; non-200 or timeout of 3 seconds or more fails delivery. After 48 hours of continuous failure without success, destination paused and team emailed.

facts.label: Native on-call escalation
facts.value: Native rotating on-call schedules and acknowledgement-based escalation chain not established in checked routing/acknowledgement docs.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: External URL/IP/port checks; protected HTTP health endpoint evaluated by customer's own application; cron sends outbound HTTPS to ping.ohdear.app, including behind firewall/proxy; AI uses a full browser.

facts.label: Monitoring inputs and API
facts.value: Customer health JSON pulled via HTTP plus secret header; cron GET/POST callbacks; AI provider key/browser execution; REST management/export uses Bearer token and JSON responses.

facts.label: Health schema bounds
facts.value: finishedAt timestamp must be from last 10 minutes; up to 50 checkResults, each with required name/label/status/message/summary/meta; meta up to 20 items.

facts.label: API access scope
facts.value: REST tokens can be restricted to selected monitors/status pages; full-account endpoints need full token. Read-only monitoring token uses Guest user permissions; MCP Connected Apps offer explicit read-only/read-write scopes.

facts.label: External/site setup
facts.value: Create account/team, choose monitor type and URL/hostname; configure check settings, primary location and alert channels. Multiple checks can share an HTTP site monitor.

facts.label: Health, cron and AI setup
facts.value: Health: run checks locally and expose schema/secret endpoint. Cron: create task schedule/grace and call starting/finished/failed callback paths. AI: create separate AI monitor, prompt/schedule/provider key and notification instructions.

facts.label: HTTP, network and site checks
facts.value: HTTP(S), API body/status/header assertions, ICMP ping, TCP port and optional welcome/command response strings; SSL/domain/DNS/blocklist/port scan; whole-site link/mixed-content and sitemap checks.

facts.label: AI browser flow coverage
facts.value: Full JavaScript browser, multi-step click/type/form/navigation, console/network inspection, screenshots, simple fetch and DNS; 5 simple fetches or 50 browser actions/check, maximum 5-minute execution.

facts.label: HTTP frequency and timeout
facts.value: Primary uptime check every 60 seconds; default HTTP timeout 5 seconds, configurable 1–10 seconds. Secondary runs immediately on primary failure.

facts.label: AI and health frequency
facts.value: AI every minute to once every 60 days; new AI monitor daily by default, maximum 5-minute run. Health default every minute, configurable minutes/hours up to 24 hours.

facts.label: Probe locations
facts.value: Primary selectable per monitor: Cape Town; Bangalore, Seoul, Singapore, Tokyo; Sydney; Toronto; Frankfurt, London, Paris, Stockholm; Sao Paulo; New York, Dallas, Los Angeles, San Francisco.

facts.label: Locations and billing counts
facts.value: One normal monitor has one 60-second primary and extra verification only on failure. For independent continuous regions, create duplicate URL monitors with different primaries; each uses site capacity.

facts.label: Private probes and AI geography
facts.value: Customer-installed private probe, static AI-browser location choice and AI multi-region execution controls not established.

facts.label: Confirmation, warning and recovery
facts.value: Primary failure invokes secondary; both down required for downtime. Primary down/secondary up becomes warning, counts online and sends no downtime notification. Default alert after two confirmed-down minutes; success sends recovery.

facts.label: Maintenance and history corrections
facts.value: Scheduled or API-started maintenance suppresses notifications and excludes failed checks from downtime. Recurring daily/weekly/monthly in team timezone; default one-hour window. Downtime records can be removed, changing uptime/status page.

facts.label: Certificate coverage
facts.value: Every 30 minutes; daily expiry warnings inside 14 days, or 7 days for Let's Encrypt; custom threshold 1–100 days. Checks each presented chain certificate, hostname/validity/changes.

facts.label: Domain schedule and expiry
facts.value: RDAP: weekly above one year, daily within year, twice daily within 90 days, every 4 hours within 30 days or expired; expiry warning default next 10 days, configurable; at most one notification/day.

facts.label: Domain TLD coverage conflict
facts.value: Guide prose says .de is unsupported, but its purported current supported-TLD list contains .de. .be remains explicitly described as unsupported.

facts.label: Page count, branding and domain
facts.value: Unlimited status pages on all plans; custom logo/colours and own domain with managed certificate. Page contains selected monitored sites, with reuse across multiple pages.

facts.label: Private page access
facts.value: Public by default; optional secret carried in URL restricts access. Account SSO is included, but status-page SSO not established.

facts.label: Custom-domain validation
facts.value: Per-page unique CNAME target from dashboard; optional _ohdear-challenge TXT for ownership verification, including Cloudflare-proxied DNS; Let's Encrypt CAA allowance needed.

facts.label: Subscriber channels and default quota
facts.value: Verified email, Slack and RSS; default 500 confirmed email subscribers across all pages in a team; pending/bounced excluded; ask support to raise limit.

facts.label: Subscriber hygiene and alert consolidation
facts.value: Email confirmation before updates, pending removed after 7 days, one-click unsubscribe, automatic hard-bounce/spam removal; flapping consolidated into one email update.

facts.label: Automatic and manual updates
facts.value: Can automatically post downtime to every page containing the monitor, with configurable message/template; manual updates/templates also supported; API control and public JSON/XML feeds.

facts.label: Schedules, timezones and grace
facts.value: Simple frequency in minutes or cron expression with server timezone; configurable grace; /starting does not reset fixed-frequency or cron expected deadline.

facts.label: Synced Laravel grace settings
facts.value: laravel-schedule-monitor sync overwrites dashboard grace from schedule definition; set graceTimeInMinutes in application code to preserve a custom value.

facts.label: Signals and captured data
facts.value: GET/POST completion ping; /starting, /finished and /failed paths; non-zero exit_code marks failure immediately; optional memory bytes, runtime seconds and failure_message up to 255 characters.

facts.label: Run events and rate limit
facts.value: Latest_result distinguishes pingStarting/pingFinished/pingFailed and late/endpoint-down states; only pingFinished success. Most recent approximately ten successful pings, failures/missed events retained; maximum 5 accepted pings/minute/check.

facts.label: Export
facts.value: Bearer-token JSON APIs for monitors, run history, uptime/downtime, metrics, AI responses and full single-report Lighthouse JSON; status subscriber list CSV; public status JSON/XML/RSS.

facts.label: Delete team and individual data
facts.value: Owner must cancel active paid subscription before deleting team in Team settings > General; deletion removes monitors, check/incident history, pages, maintenance, tasks and team tokens. Invoices retained for legal/accounting.

facts.label: Data erasure timing
facts.value: DPA: delete/anonymize personal data within 30 days of termination, legal retention excepted; active backup personal data maximum 60 days. Security schedule includes monthly backups 12 months and yearly backups up to 2 years.

facts.label: Transport, storage encryption and access
facts.value: TLS 1.2+ in transit. Security page explicitly says data is not currently encrypted at rest. Production MFA, least-privilege and SSH-key access; account 2FA/SSO and roles on every plan.

facts.label: Customer-controlled collection
facts.value: Application runs its own health checks and chooses JSON/message/meta returned; secret request header authenticates poller. Customer chooses AI prompt, URL, custom request headers/body and crawl exclusions.

facts.label: Redaction and AI privacy controls
facts.value: Default header/body/URL credential masking, prompt/screenshot scrubbing, customer-managed keys and AI-provider data residency/training settings not established.

facts.label: Signed callbacks
facts.value: HMAC-SHA256 signature in OhDear-Signature using team secret; up to 5 custom destination headers, sent only with valid TLS certificate; receiver should validate signature.

facts.label: Storage and residency
facts.value: Primary check results/settings/uptime/team data: Combell, Belgium; performance metrics ClickHouse Cloud EU; AWS backups/uploads/check reports Global; nodes AWS/DigitalOcean/Vultr worldwide; Cloudflare Global.

facts.label: DPA and transfer terms
facts.value: Public Article 28 DPA; customer controller or processor, Oh Dear processor/subprocessor; SCC Module Two/Three as applicable; public subprocessor changes and 30-day objection route.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Oh Dear; https://ohdear.app/; service contracted with Immutable VOF, Belgium.

facts.label: Shutdown, sunset and acquisition search
facts.value: Active paid service and 10-day trial; no actual Oh Dear shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in checked homepage/about/news/changelog/legal/status sources.

facts.label: Legacy integration migration notice
facts.value: Oh Dear's Teams guide recommends replacing legacy Incoming Webhook connectors with Microsoft Workflows; says legacy remains usable for now but will lose support in future.

facts.label: Hosted-service rights
facts.value: Service/software/proprietary technology rights reserved by Oh Dear; no complete-backend source license offered in the checked terms/docs.

facts.label: Management SDK source and license
facts.value: Official ohdearapp/ohdear-php-sdk repository; MIT license in LICENSE.md.

facts.label: Documentation and support
facts.value: Public feature/API/SDK/notification/status/FAQ docs; support@ohdear.app; security@ohdear.app for disclosure. Security disclosure response commitment 24 hours; no formal uptime SLA or service credits.
