facts.label: Billing model
facts.value: Project-level seat subscription plus active monitors and telemetry usage; prepaid notification and AI balances. Every invited person counts as a seat before acceptance. Fees exclude applicable taxes.

facts.label: Growth price
facts.value: $22/user/month monthly, or $20/user/month equivalent on annual billing.

facts.label: Scale price
facts.value: $99/user/month monthly, or $84/user/month equivalent on annual billing.

facts.label: Usage rate card
facts.value: Active monitor $1/month; telemetry $0.10/GB at 15-day retention; SMS $0.10/message, WhatsApp $0.10/message, voice $0.10/minute/call. AI $0.02/1,000 tokens. Session replay $2/GB at 15-day retention.

facts.label: Ongoing free cloud plan
facts.value: $0 seat/base plan, 1 public status page, 100 subscribers, custom domain/branding/SSL and unlimited Manual monitors. Email, push/app and webhook alerts are free. Active monitors and telemetry remain paid usage requiring a payment method.

facts.label: Self-hosted ongoing use
facts.value: Community software remains free at any scale; operator pays infrastructure, backups and external delivery/model suppliers. SAML/OIDC SSO is included in Community.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: 14-day trial for new paid accounts; existing-account upgrades are explicitly ineligible. Billing docs say an existing active trial carries over across a plan change, while a later plan change starts none.

facts.label: Entry paid capability
facts.value: Free base plus paid active monitor starts at $1/monitor/month. First paid seat tier is Growth $22/user/month, adding on-call, APIs/MCP, unlimited pages/subscribers and 500 workflow runs/month.

facts.label: Usage and loss
facts.value: Adding a payment method enables pay-as-you-go without changing plan. Free projects without one cannot create paid monitors or ingest telemetry; OTLP can return 402. Unpaid projects can become inactive and later be deleted.

facts.label: OTLP limits
facts.value: 4 MB/request HTTP and 4 MB/message gRPC; HTTP key request/minute limits can reject with 429/Retry-After. Size/encoding/auth failures use 413/415/401/422. 503 on startup is retryable; documented exporter permanent errors drop the batch.

facts.label: Spend controls
facts.value: Notification/AI prepaid balances stop sending/AI when funds are insufficient; owners are emailed. Recharge $20–$1,000; auto-recharge starts disabled and can be enabled with configurable thresholds.

facts.label: Whole-account cap
facts.value: No universal dollar cap or configurable total monitor/telemetry billing alert threshold found in pricing, Billing & Usage, retention or terms. Drop filters reduce billed data; key rate limits reduce requests.

facts.label: Telemetry retention
facts.value: Default 15 days; project-wide default can be changed on every plan/edition. Per-type/severity/status/service/resource overrides require Cloud Scale or self-host Enterprise. Changes affect new records, not existing expiry dates.

facts.label: Monitor, map and replay retention
facts.value: Pricing says Cloud active-monitor logs stored 90 days. Retention guide lists self-host defaults: monitor logs 1 day, monitor metrics 30 days. Source maps default 90 days; replay default 7 days.

facts.label: Account retention and deletion
facts.value: Terms allow export during subscription and by request for 30 days after account closure; active data is deleted after that window. DPA allows return/deletion on termination with legal exceptions and certification on request.

facts.label: People, projects and seats
facts.value: Cloud plans bill per user in each project; invitations count until removed. Free/Growth/Scale base pricing is $0/$22/$99 per user monthly. Scale advertises unlimited teams.

facts.label: Log meter and loss
facts.value: GB-ingested billing with retention multiplier; no exact public compressed-wire versus decoded/indexed byte-meter definition found. OTLP 4 MB transport limit and explicit dropped-batch/error handling documented.

facts.label: Extra telemetry costs
facts.value: Longer retention increases ingest GB rate proportionally; minimum seven billed days. No separate published query-scan/index/search/export price found in pricing/Billing & Usage/Logs Explorer.

facts.label: Country and eligibility
facts.value: HackerBay, Inc., Delaware, USA; DPA gives Dover, Delaware address. Hosted account requires age 16+ and contractual capacity; terms permit internal business or personal use subject to acceptable-use rules.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Uptime/synthetic/infrastructure checks, logs, metrics, traces, exception tracking, real-user monitoring/replay, incidents/on-call and status pages. Incoming Request monitors cover missed heartbeats.

facts.label: Cloud and self-host
facts.value: OneUptime Cloud plus full Docker Compose and Kubernetes/Helm deployment. Self-host Community and Enterprise use the same core stack/data, with separately licensed Enterprise modules.

facts.label: Instrumentation stacks
facts.value: OpenTelemetry SDK/Collector support for app logs/metrics/traces; browser OTel SDK for RUM/errors; docs expose language setup guides, plus agents/collectors for hosts, containers and serverless.

facts.label: Channels and base costs
facts.value: Email, push/mobile/desktop app and webhook alerts advertised free. SMS/WhatsApp/voice metered at published rates; personal methods support verification and on-call delivery rules. Slack/Teams and integration workflows are supported.

facts.label: Bring your own and countries
facts.value: Own Twilio removes OneUptime SMS/call charges but leaves Twilio supplier costs. Pricing claims worldwide coverage with high-risk-region caveat; no full country/rate matrix or included call/SMS credits found.

facts.label: Noise and escalation
facts.value: Growth+ on-call rules page levels until acknowledged/resolved, with configurable wait/repeats and schedules/teams/people. Initial escalation wait 30 minutes. Criteria can aggregate time windows, resolve automatically and suppress while parents are down or maintenance applies.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Public or custom outbound probe for websites, APIs, TCP/IP/DNS/cert/domain checks and real-browser flows; custom probes run inside private networks. Telemetry SDKs/collectors support app/container/serverless paths.

facts.label: Data inputs
facts.value: OTLP HTTP JSON/protobuf or gRPC, x-oneuptime-token; HTTP supports none/gzip/deflate/zstd. Logs from OTel, Fluent Bit/Fluentd/syslog use the same ingest processing controls. Heartbeat GET/POST/HEAD uses secret-key URL.

facts.label: Setup
facts.value: Cloud: account/project, payment method for paid checks/ingest, monitor/criteria/probes or ingestion key plus OTel SDK/collector, then notify users/status page. Browser and heartbeat flows need their own script/caller.

facts.label: Self-host setup
facts.value: Linux Docker Compose with Git/Node/npm or Kubernetes Helm; configure host/auth/storage/email/TLS and deploy probes. Community and Enterprise images/licensing differ.

facts.label: Error capture and grouping
facts.value: Exception span events, exception-attributed logs and qualifying Error/Fatal stack logs form issues. Service/type/normalized stack/message grouping; newer stack grouping omits line numbers/library frames/messages; late events do not falsely reopen fixed issues.

facts.label: Readable locations
facts.value: Browser source maps uploaded by service.name/service.version/bundle; lazy resolution gives original file/function/line and source context when sourcesContent exists. Maps not fetched publicly from app site.

facts.label: Release and regression
facts.value: service.version links occurrences to releases; resolve, resolve in next release, reopen/archive; new post-fix occurrence can mark Regressed. Deploy/change events provide correlation with telemetry.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: Occurrences show user counts/attributes, trace/span, release/environment, nearby logs, user session and replay when recorded. Browser/React Native replay is a separate integration with independent byte billing and retention.

facts.label: Check coverage
facts.value: Website/API, IP/ping/port, DNS/DNSSEC, NTP, SSL/domain, SQL/custom JavaScript, infrastructure and Playwright synthetic monitors are documented. API uses methods/headers/body, assertion criteria and secrets; mTLS supported for website checks.

facts.label: Intervals and timeouts
facts.value: Probe monitors: one minute to one week, default five minutes; SSL, custom JS and synthetics five-minute minimum. Website per-attempt timeout default/max 60 seconds; retries configurable up to 3 additional retries.

facts.label: Probe allowlist
facts.value: Official allowlist lists 172.174.206.132, 57.151.99.117, 34.44.60.111 and 35.209.152.168, with GET /ip-whitelist for a programmatic list.

facts.label: Origins and check counting
facts.value: Select hosted/global probes or custom private probes. Billing guide charges active monitors, not published per scheduled check or selected probe. A complete stable named-region list/count was not found in checked pricing/create/probe docs.

facts.label: Confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Probe criteria evaluated in order; first match decides status/alert/incident. Default agreement requires every enabled connected probe to agree, configurable lower. Time-window criteria supported; active scheduled maintenance stops probe checks and criteria.

facts.label: Expiry warnings
facts.value: SSL certificate monitor default expiry warning 14 days ahead; domain monitor default 30 days ahead, using RDAP/WHOIS Auto. Criteria can inspect validity/expiry, names/registration details.

facts.label: Search and archives
facts.value: Logs search/filter by time/service/severity/attributes, saved views, charts and live updates every 10 seconds; page CSV/JSON export. Self-host telemetry stored in ClickHouse; sizing docs explicitly say no automatic old-data move to object storage.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: OTel traces show waterfall/flame graph/service map, spans with latency/errors, service/operation insights and database-call spans. Profiling is another documented product/signal.

facts.label: Sampling and billing
facts.value: Collector/SDK-selected telemetry can be sent; server span drop filters sample matching records individually at 1–99% and count drops; dropped records are not billed. Sampling can remove exception evidence too.

facts.label: Real-user monitoring
facts.value: Browser OTel measures page/request traces, errors and Core Web Vitals; replay supports web and React Native with session correlation. Replay costs $2/GB at 15 days; default retention 7 days, configurable.

facts.label: Page allowances and branding
facts.value: Free: 1 public page/100 subscribers; paid: unlimited pages/subscribers and private pages/users. Custom domain, SSL and branding included all plans. Hiding Powered by OneUptime requires Cloud Scale or self-host Enterprise.

facts.label: Subscriber workflow
facts.value: Email/SMS double opt-in; Slack/Teams/webhook paths, resource selection, unsubscribe and announcement/incident/maintenance delivery. Email enabled by default, other channels off; global send-notifications switch suppresses delivery.

facts.label: Update source and history
facts.value: Monitor state/incidents plus manual/scheduled announcements and maintenance publish customer status. Configure affected resources, public pages and notifications; internal notes and public communication are separate.

facts.label: Schedule/grace behavior
facts.value: Incoming Request criteria detect Not Recieved In Minutes; reevaluated every 30 seconds, counting whole minutes and triggering once more than threshold has elapsed. First-match ordering is critical; monitor creation time starts missing-ping timing before first receipt.

facts.label: Job signals
facts.value: Secret URL accepts GET/POST/HEAD; body/header/JS criteria can report failure or recovery and retain request context. No distinct native start/success/fail endpoint family or automatic paired execution duration found.

facts.label: Requirements and sizing

facts.label: Confirmation and recovery
facts.value: Default downtime confirmation 60 seconds; recovery 180 seconds; configurable immediate start/recovery or custom periods with repeated multi-location verification.

facts.label: Routing, reminders and pause
facts.value: Choose destinations per check/heartbeat, HIGH/LOW priority; reminder interval configurable, API default 1,440 minutes, -1 disables. Pause stops running/pings; active incident stays open until resumed and passes.

facts.label: Webhook delivery semantics
facts.value: Events only for selected matching resources; status transitions and incident start/update/resolve; may be missed, duplicated or out of order; return 2xx quickly and confirm current status through API.

facts.label: Webhook history disagreement
facts.value: 2026-10-07 update and current API document delivery history/details; explanation page says dashboard does not show attempts/response codes.

facts.label: Native escalation and acknowledgement
facts.value: Native on-call rotations, acknowledgement-driven escalation chain and per-incident acknowledgement control not established.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: External HTTP/DNS/TCP and real-browser probes; private scheduled jobs may make outbound HEAD/GET/POST heartbeat request; official Vercel/Next.js completion-monitoring guide.

facts.label: Data/control paths
facts.value: External HTTP requests, DNS UDP/TCP queries, TCP connection/payload tests, Playwright browser execution and heartbeat callback; REST Bearer/OAuth API, CLI and MCP control.

facts.label: API permission model
facts.value: Organization-scoped token with resource READ/EDIT grants and optional expiry; EDIT includes READ. Token secret only shown at creation; replacement required to change grants/expiry. CLI uses OAuth.

facts.label: External and browser setup
facts.value: Create account via magic-link email, Google or GitHub; add URL/monitor type, interval, regions and alerts. Scripted browser: one Playwright Test script with at least one test block, select region/frequency and save.

facts.label: Heartbeat and status setup
facts.value: Create schedule/grace heartbeat and ping only after successful work; create page/components, optionally link checks, configure custom-domain CNAME and subscriber confirmation.

facts.label: HTTP assertions and authentication
facts.value: GET/HEAD/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; custom headers except User-Agent, body for POST/PUT/PATCH; Basic/Bearer/cookie auth; JSONPath/text/header/HTML CSS assertions and one status-code assertion.

facts.label: DNS and TCP checks
facts.value: DNS A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/NS/SOA/TXT over UDP/TCP, optional resolver; NOERROR default. TCP IPv4/IPv6, connection expected pass/fail, optional payload, response-text/time assertions.

facts.label: Real browser execution
facts.value: Standalone Playwright Test flow in Node.js 24; JavaScript rendering, interaction, locator assertions, login/checkout scripts; up to two minutes including startup/execution/cleanup.

facts.label: Uptime interval and timeout
facts.value: Hobby minimum 180 seconds; Pro 30 seconds. API default timeout 10,000 milliseconds (10 seconds); numeric configurable maximum/minimum not shown in checked rendered docs.

facts.label: Browser time/frequency bounds
facts.value: Browser check service limit two minutes; script example test timeout 90 seconds and action timeout 10 seconds are example settings. API interval is seconds; five-minute scheduling documented by vendor's workload example.

facts.label: Regions and current enumerations
facts.value: Reference lists US East/West, Europe, India, Australia, Japan. March 2026 browser announcement also includes UK; current API lists us-east-1/us-east-2/us-west-1/eu-central-1/eu-west-2/ap-south-1/ap-southeast-2/ap-northeast-1.

facts.label: Selection and counting
facts.value: One selected region executes per scheduled cycle; selecting several rotates rather than multiplies independent cycles. Separate pinned checks give each region its own scheduled flow.

facts.label: Private probe availability
facts.value: Installable customer/private-network probes not established in supported-region/API/script/deployment docs.

facts.label: Failure and recovery verification
facts.value: Initial failure rechecked in same region, other regions and Cloudflare network; confirmation/recovery periods before incident state changes. Exact numeric verifier quorum/retry cadence not published.

facts.label: Monitoring maintenance
facts.value: Paid recurring weekdays/local timezone/duration windows; uptime checks stop, heartbeat pings still recorded but missed-ping alerts stop. End returns pending, manually paused stay paused.

facts.label: Certificate checks

facts.label: Domain expiration
facts.value: Dedicated RDAP/WHOIS registration-expiry monitoring and pre-expiry warning windows not established.

facts.label: Status history and maintenance

facts.label: Schedules and grace
facts.value: Fixed interval in seconds/minutes/hours/days/weeks or cron expression/timezone; cron grace starts at scheduled local time; deadline evaluated about once/minute.

facts.label: Early-ping behavior disagreement
facts.value: 2026-09-23 changelog says every accepted early fixed-interval ping is recorded and restarts interval+grace countdown; explanation/API still warn early pings may not alter deadline/be recorded.

facts.label: Completion and missing-ping signal
facts.value: Secret oonchk.com URL accepts HEAD/GET/POST; body and query ignored. Missing scheduled success after grace creates incident/alerts; next accepted ping recovers. New monitor remains pending until first success.

facts.label: Start/failure/output protocol
facts.value: Separate start and success endpoints, explicit job-failure request signal, runtime/memory/exit-code or full output capture not established.

facts.label: Paused, muted and maintained jobs
facts.value: Pause ignores pings and stops monitoring; mute keeps ping recording but suppresses missed-ping states; maintenance records pings without recovery and returns pending on end.

facts.label: Retrieval/export
facts.value: JSON API/CLI lists checks, heartbeats, pages, components, incidents, subscribers and users; pagination generally page 1/per_page 20, continuing until total_count or empty page. Subscriber mode supports all or selected components.

facts.label: Account and resource deletion

facts.label: Inactive accounts
facts.value: Terms allow terminating an account after 6 months without login, after attempts to notify; provider may reallocate hosted status-page subdomains.

facts.label: Uptime credential variables
facts.value: Write-only secret variables can be replaced, not read after saving; exact secret values removed from check results, but encoded/modified values can leak. Supports uptime header values and Basic Auth fields.

facts.label: Secret limits and callback URLs
facts.value: Up to 1,000 organization variables, value up to 8 KiB; webhook URL templates can reference secrets and return only saved template. No automatic URL encoding or nested expansion.

facts.label: Transport and at-rest policy
facts.value: Privacy says stored monitoring data encrypted in transit and at rest; tokens/secrets have write-only handling. Webhooks are explicitly unsigned and cannot carry a custom authorization header per explanation.

facts.value: Active Hobby, Pro, Enterprise and 14-day trial offers. No OnlineOrNot service-wide shutdown, sunset or acquisition notice found in checked official product/about/changelog/legal/status sources.

facts.label: Ongoing self-host use
facts.value: Free AGPL-licensed software with operator-paid infrastructure. Self-host workspace feature limits must be explicitly configured; omitted keys fall back to free-plan limits.

facts.label: Trial

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan

facts.label: Resource quotas and overrun
facts.value: Pricing promises no monitor/page stoppage without notice and contact near/exceeding limits. Resource creation code rejects additions above count caps; soft-deleted monitors do not count, inactive monitors still do.

facts.label: API and ping limits
facts.value: API: 600 requests/minute and 100/10 seconds per key/token, 60 writes/minute; public status endpoints 120/minute/IP. Rate-limited calls receive 429 and Retry-After. Heartbeat token allows 6 pings/minute including /fail.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Fixed base subscriptions and explicitly purchased add-ons are published. No user-set dollar cap, bill warning threshold or guaranteed hard monetary limit found in pricing, quota/API docs or terms.

facts.label: Check-result retention
facts.value: 14 days from check time; older logs deleted. Uptime percentages and status history are stored/computed separately from response-log retention.

facts.label: Check-result retention
facts.value: 3 months from check time; older logs deleted. Uptime percentages and status history are stored/computed separately from response-log retention.

facts.label: Check-result retention

facts.label: Check-result retention
facts.value: 24 months from check time; older logs deleted. Uptime percentages and status history are stored/computed separately from response-log retention.

facts.label: Other data retention
facts.value: Account/workspace data lasts while active, then deleted/anonymized within 30 days, with legal/accounting/fraud exceptions. Billing records typically up to 7 years; application security/debug logs up to 30 days; integration tokens deleted within 30 days of removal.

facts.value: OpenStatus SAS, 122 Rue Amelot, 75011 Paris, France. Terms apply French law and prohibit illegal, phishing, spam or infringing use.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Multi-region synthetic uptime and response-time monitoring, status pages, subscriber communications and incident response. Heartbeat/cron monitoring is in gradual rollout.

facts.label: Hosted and complete self-host
facts.value: Managed SaaS plus full Docker Compose/Helm stack. Full self-hosting requires operator-deployed private probes; a probe connected to hosted SaaS is not the entire self-hosted product.

facts.label: Status-page-only deployment
facts.value: Lightweight self-host setup runs database, migration job, dashboard and status-page app; it omits automated monitoring, analytics, API server and probes.

facts.label: SDK and stack compatibility
facts.value: External probes do not require an application SDK. Official programmatic surfaces include Node.js/TypeScript, Python and PHP SDK docs, CLI, Terraform, MCP and JSON/ConnectRPC API.

facts.label: Operator notification channels
facts.value: Email, Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams Workflows, Google Chat, Telegram, WhatsApp, generic webhooks, Ntfy, PagerDuty, OpsGenie and Grafana OnCall are documented.

facts.label: Delivery charges and limits
facts.value: Hosted email needs a recipient address; WhatsApp needs an international number. No per-message tariff, destination-country matrix or separate included SMS/voice entitlement found in pricing/channel docs.

facts.label: Noise and incident handling
facts.value: Automatic incident opens when at least half the configured regions report error; single-region checks use that region. One open incident per monitor; acknowledgement and manual/automatic resolution supported. Degraded triggers alerts without opening an automatic incident.

facts.label: Escalation boundaries
facts.value: PagerDuty/OpsGenie/Grafana OnCall integrations delegate escalation. A native timed escalation tree, repeat-alert schedule or per-recipient quiet-hours rule is not published in the checked monitor/channel/incident docs.

facts.label: Public and private deployment fit
facts.value: Public HTTP/TCP/DNS/ICMP/gRPC probes cover network-reachable apps. Pro/Scale private-location Docker/Kubernetes probes run behind firewalls with outbound platform connection and result reporting.

facts.label: Input and telemetry direction
facts.value: API/SDK/CLI/Terraform configure resources; heartbeat GET/POST/HEAD accepts job health. OTLP over HTTP exports monitor metrics to another backend; no general customer OTLP/syslog/log/error/trace ingestion documented.

facts.label: Hosted setup
facts.value: Create/sign in to workspace; add monitor URL/name, interval, regions and assertions; configure/attach notification channels; create page/components and own-domain DNS as needed. Heartbeats must be enabled in the workspace before integrating the secret ping URL.

facts.label: Self-host setup
facts.value: Run full or lightweight Compose/Helm services; apply migrations, configure authentication/email and workspace limits. Full stack additionally needs working Tinybird ingestion, separate probe deployment and scheduled private-location health job.

facts.label: Active check types
facts.value: HTTP/HTTPS methods, body/header/status assertions, TCP connect, DNS A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/NS/TXT, ICMP echo and gRPC Health/Check are documented.

facts.label: HTTP auth and assertions
facts.value: Custom token/basic-style Authorization headers and request bodies; up to 20 headers and 10 assertions each for status, body and header. Follow redirects default true, up to 10. JSONPath assertions have a write-surface limitation.

facts.label: Intervals and timeout
facts.value: Hobby: 10m/30m/1h. Starter adds 1m/5m. Pro/Scale add 30s. HTTP timeout default 45 seconds, allowed 0–300000 ms; degraded threshold separately configurable.

facts.label: Probe origins and counting
facts.value: Published 28-region network spans Fly, Railway and Koyeb; selected public regions run in parallel. Hobby cap 6, Starter 6/monitor, Pro/Scale advertised 28; public location reference currently lists 27 entries.

facts.label: Failure confirmation
facts.value: HTTP retry default 3 total attempts, range 0–10; 0 maps to default, 1 is a single attempt. At least half configured regions must error to open an incident; single-region fails on its own error. Auto-resolution follows the region agreement state.

facts.label: Maintenance
facts.value: Scheduled windows affect page component display/history; they do not exclude downtime from uptime calculations. Active incidents/reports outrank maintenance; maintenance does not establish a monitor alert mute.

facts.label: Certificate/domain expiry
facts.value: No native certificate- or registration-expiry reminder schedule, notice windows or separate expiry entitlement found in HTTP/DNS references, monitor overview or pricing.

facts.label: Status-page features
facts.value: 1 pages and 3 component allowance. No custom domain, subscribers or password gate.

facts.label: Status-page features
facts.value: 1 pages and 20 component allowance. Own domain/password included; custom theme +20/month, white label +300/month; email-domain auth/IP restriction each +100/month.

facts.label: Status-page features
facts.value: 5 pages and 50 component allowance. Own domain/password/custom theme included; white label +300/month; email-domain auth/IP restriction each +100/month.

facts.label: Status-page features
facts.value: 10 pages and 500 component allowance. Own domain, password, custom theme, white label, email-domain auth and IP restriction included.

facts.label: Private-page behavior
facts.value: Password page, approved-email-domain magic links and IPv4 CIDR restriction are separate access modes. IPv6 allowlist access is unsupported. Private feeds use the password query parameter; indexing can be disabled on paid plans.

facts.label: Subscribers and delivery
facts.value: Subscribers are included on paid plans; README states no per-subscriber charges. Public email uses confirmation; owner-added email confirms consent without verification. Email/webhook/Slack subscriptions, component scopes and RSS/Atom/JSON feeds are documented.

facts.label: Webhook subscriber reliability
facts.value: Subscriber webhooks: 5-second timeout, up to 3 retries/4 total attempts for network/timeouts, 5xx or 429; other 4xx permanent. Shared custom header supported; operator notification webhooks have no HMAC signature.

facts.label: Update sources and history
facts.value: Monitor-linked components update automatically; static components need manual reports/maintenance. Public reports have investigating/identified/monitoring/resolved updates and per-component impacts, with explicit notify. Status bars show 30 or 45 days; full logs use separate retention.

facts.label: Schedule and grace
facts.value: Heartbeat period 1 minute–30 days; grace 1 minute–7 days. Deadline = last ping + period + grace. Checked every minute; alerts may arrive up to a minute later. No alerts before first ping; pause suppresses alerts and resume restarts deadline.

facts.label: Job signals and history
facts.value: Plain GET/POST/HEAD ping reports completion; /fail reports failure and can attach first 10 KB of output in POST body. Next plain ping recovers. No distinct native start event, paired runtime measurement or stdout capture beyond supplied body documented.

facts.label: Full-stack requirements
facts.value: Docker Compose or Helm; libSQL, migrations, dashboard, status page, API, workflows, Tinybird Local and ingest server; separately deployed private probe. Tinybird CLI needed for analytics setup; health cron every 5 minutes.

facts.label: Lightweight requirements and sizing
facts.value: Status-only: libSQL volume, migration job, dashboard and status page. No workload-qualified CPU/RAM/disk recommendation found for the fixed endpoint/subscriber scenarios.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: CLI exports monitors/pages/component groups/channels/private locations to Terraform; monitor logs can be listed/fetched through CLI/API. Public feeds expose page state/reports/maintenance. Privacy describes dashboard workspace export/deletion and data-portability requests.

facts.label: Hosted sensitive data

facts.label: Jobs covered

facts.label: Cloud edition

facts.label: Community edition
facts.value: Complete self-hosted service on Docker plus Postgres, or Cloudflare Workers plus Postgres/Hyperdrive; optional external regional probes.

facts.label: Languages / integration
facts.value: No SDK needed for external checks. Heartbeat accepts HTTP GET/POST from any capable language or scheduler; database probes need no application instrumentation.

facts.label: Channels / pricing
facts.value: Email, Slack, Discord, Teams, Telegram, PagerDuty, Lark/Feishu, generic webhook, ntfy and iOS push; every channel available on every hosted plan.

facts.label: Hosted email limits
facts.value: Free 100, Lite 2,000, Starter 15,000, Team 60,000 emails/month shared with subscribers; sends by Cloudflare Email Service.

facts.label: Chat destinations
facts.value: Slack and Discord use incoming/channel webhooks; Teams needs Workflows; Telegram needs bot token/chat ID; Lark optionally signs; ntfy uses topic/server and optional bearer token.

facts.label: PagerDuty / phone costs
facts.value: Events API v2 triggers/resolves using incident id as dedup key; PagerDuty handles rosters/phone calls. Acknowledge separately in OpenUptime; sync is one-way.

facts.label: Self-host mail / push
facts.value: Configure verified mail sender plus SMTP/Resend for Docker or Cloudflare Email Sending for Workers; absent transport logs mail instead of sending. APNs credentials required for self-host iOS push.

facts.label: Confirmation / dependencies
facts.value: Failure threshold 1–10, default 3; recovery threshold 1–10, default 1. Same-project dependency down suppresses dependent incidents/alerts; maintenance silences incidents/alerts while checks continue.

facts.label: Acknowledgement / escalation
facts.value: Incident acknowledgement records assignee; unacknowledged incidents can repeat up to 10 mobile reminders, optional email, and escalate through up to 3 channel levels.

facts.label: Delivery retries / webhook security
facts.value: Generic webhook JSON POST: any 2xx delivered, 10-second timeout, up to 3 attempts over about 6 minutes. Requests currently unsigned; HTTPS secret URL advised.

facts.label: Hosted environment fit
facts.value: Public HTTP(S), TCP, DNS, WebSocket, MCP and database targets; private/internal addresses refused by default. Heartbeats need outbound HTTP to the service.

facts.label: Self-host / private fit
facts.value: Docker/Node can reach trusted private networks with ALLOW_PRIVATE_TARGETS; optional signed regional probes on Docker/Node 22/Vercel.

facts.label: Heartbeat ingestion
facts.value: Tokenized /api/heartbeat/<token>, HTTP GET/POST; accepted ping updates health and can resolve an incident. No API key required; token is credential.

facts.label: API / agent automation
facts.value: REST JSON over HTTPS with scoped API keys or OAuth-backed Streamable HTTP MCP. Workspace/project scope and roles enforced.

facts.label: Hosted setup
facts.value: Sign up, select workspace/project, create monitor type/target/interval/threshold, choose alert channels; optional status page and paid custom-domain DNS verification.

facts.label: Self-host setup
facts.value: Docker Compose app+Postgres with stable auth secret/public URL, migrate on start; or two Workers with Postgres/Hyperdrive, minute scheduler and optional queue. Configure mail, HTTPS and optional probes.

facts.label: HTTP / assertions
facts.value: GET/HEAD/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/OPTIONS; expected status default 200, keyword contains/absent, custom headers and up to 16 KiB body for body-capable methods.

facts.label: Other check types
facts.value: TCP, DNS record assertions, PostgreSQL/MySQL/Redis handshake without credentials; WebSocket handshake and optional message/reply; EVM/Solana sync checks; MCP discovery with optional schema/tool tests.

facts.label: Hosted schedule / timeout
facts.value: Free min 300s, Lite/Starter 60s, Team 30s; API range 30–86,400s subject to plan floor. Timeout 1,000–30,000ms, default 10,000ms.

facts.label: Self-host scheduler
facts.value: Workers Queue mode supports sub-minute work; inline mode checks up to 40 due monitors/minute and cannot truly run a 30-second schedule. Docker has its own scheduler.

facts.label: Hosted region count / geography
facts.value: Free uses auto; Lite/Starter up to 3 regions/monitor, Team up to 5. Region list is deployment configured; public docs do not guarantee today's hosted city list.

facts.label: Regional check charging
facts.value: Every chosen region costs one credit each run; single selected non-auto region runs only there. Manual regional diagnostic costs one credit even though not recorded.

facts.label: Self-managed probes
facts.value: Docker or Node 22 probe on any appropriate host; Vercel functions pinned to configured regions; default bundle has five region IDs. Probe HMAC signatures require shared secret and ≤60s skew.

facts.label: Failure / recovery vote
facts.value: Strict majority of responding regions by default, tie up; configurable minRegionsFailing. Unreachable probes excluded; all unavailable HTTP/TCP/WebSocket fall back auto, MCP stays inconclusive.

facts.label: Maintenance / pause
facts.value: Checks continue in maintenance with no incidents/alerts; one-off or daily/weekly recurrence, IANA timezone and bounded series. Pause/resume resets recovery streak.

facts.label: Hosted SSL
facts.value: Lite+: automatic HTTPS certificate read about every 6h, warning 14/7/3/1 days, configurable 1–90; automatic reads cost no credits and do not create incidents.

facts.label: Domain registration expiry
facts.value: Community domain type and hosted product page use RDAP on explicit registered domain; default daily, hourly–daily range; warn 1–365 days, default 30.

facts.label: Page components / access
facts.value: Public pages, ordered/grouped monitor components, theme and response-time options. API accepts at most 200 components/page; no numeric page-count cap stated.

facts.label: Custom domains / branding
facts.value: Cloud Lite+ managed one hostname/page with CNAME/TXT verification; Team hides OpenUptime branding. Managed per-page hostname binding is not included in Community.

facts.label: Subscribers / mail cost
facts.value: Double opt-in email and RSS; 5,000 subscriber cap per page. Subscriber updates and maintenance reminder emails share workspace monthly notification allowance.

facts.label: Subscriber controls
facts.value: Can select components; confirmation, one-click unsubscribe and owner removal. Public subscribe rate limits include 200/page/hour and per-IP/address limits.

facts.label: Sources / history
facts.value: Automatic monitor-driven status/incidents plus manual public/internal updates and maintenance; public root cause/postmortem only after explicit publication.

facts.label: Feeds / embeds
facts.value: RSS, SVG badge, JSON summaries, iCalendar maintenance and embeddable live summary. Public MCP access can be disabled, but page/feeds remain public.

facts.label: Heartbeat schedule / grace
facts.value: Expected ping interval rather than cron expression; grace API 0–86,400s, default 0. Product form lists none/1/5/15 minutes.

facts.label: Failure signals / lifecycle
facts.value: Missing ping after interval+grace creates failure; GET/POST ping can recover after recovery threshold. No separately documented start/end/fail signal or hung-run duration/output capture.

facts.label: Docker requirements
facts.value: Docker Compose v2; app container plus Postgres; persistent pgdata, stable auth secret, configured public origin/HTTPS and outbound mail. Published-image docs list amd64 and arm64.

facts.label: Workers requirements
facts.value: Two Workers, reachable Postgres through Hyperdrive, cron and optional paid Queue; Node.js 22+ and pnpm deployment toolchain.

facts.label: Sizing
facts.value: No workload-specific CPU/RAM/disk, Postgres volume or database connection sizing published for the directory's workloads.

facts.label: Export / portability

facts.label: Deletion
facts.value: Account export/deletion in Account settings; owners remove monitors/pages/subscribers. Delete monitor also deletes its results; project deletion removes its contents.

facts.label: Credentials / access controls
facts.value: Request headers/bodies and channel secrets masked for members; owner/admin needed to retain secrets while changing target; cross-origin redirect strips credentials and can refuse body forwarding.

facts.label: Data exposure / telemetry
facts.value: Hosted privacy lists targets, headers, results, sessions, channels and subscribers; functional cookies, aggregate cookie-free analytics and Google Fonts. Community analytics off unless configured.

facts.label: Hosted residency / DPA
facts.value: Cloudflare Workers/Hyperdrive/Email Service and an unnamed Postgres provider; actual database country, selectable residency, backup locations and public DPA not specified.

facts.label: Self-host data location
facts.value: Operator chooses Postgres/host and mail/probe providers. Stateless regional probes hold no database credentials and store no check results.

facts.value: Security fixes land on main; policy advises latest release or main. Public changelog active; official GitHub Releases currently empty despite example image tags in docs.

facts.value: Log ingestion quotas, byte meters, log sampling, and log retention tiers are not applicable to the metrics database.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Log scan, index, archive, and retrieval charges are not applicable to this self-hosted metrics product; it has no vendor usage bill.

facts.label: Data retention and local block layout
facts.value: Samples are written to successive two-hour TSDB blocks. Each block has chunks, an index, and metadata; chunk segment files are 512 MB by default.

facts.label: Write-ahead log and crash recovery
facts.value: The current head block remains partly in memory and is protected by a write-ahead log (WAL). WAL segments are 128 MB; Prometheus keeps at least three, and higher-ingest servers may keep more to preserve two hours of raw data.

facts.label: Retention compaction headroom
facts.value: Compaction can temporarily need both source and new blocks on disk. Larger blocks cover up to 10% of retention or 31 days, whichever is smaller, so the size limit can be exceeded briefly during compaction.

facts.label: Retention-size safety margin
facts.value: Prometheus recommends setting the retention-size limit to no more than 80–85% of disk allocated to Prometheus, leaving 15–20% for compaction. Expired blocks are cleaned in the background and may take up to two hours to remove.

facts.label: Storage sizing formula
facts.value: The official rough estimate is retention seconds × ingested samples per second × bytes per sample; Prometheus reports an average of about 1–2 bytes per sample. It is a planning estimate, not an exact disk reservation.

facts.label: Percentage-based retention option
facts.value: The YAML retention configuration has an experimental storage.tsdb.retention.percentage option that caps Prometheus block storage as a percentage of total disk and adjusts when the volume is resized. The config docs warn startup can fail if Prometheus cannot query total disk capacity.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: The official project pages reviewed do not publish a project home country or regional buyer eligibility. The software is available as a public open-source project; this is not a vendor account offer.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Collects and stores numerical application and system metrics as time series; evaluates PromQL rules and can alert on metric conditions. It can track an application's error-count metric when that metric is instrumented, but it does not capture exception events or group error reports.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: The Prometheus server is self-hosted. Official distribution is through precompiled binaries and Docker images; the project does not advertise a first-party hosted Prometheus subscription on its product pages.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Official client libraries: Go, Java/Scala, Node.js, Python, Ruby, and Rust. The docs also list community libraries for other languages, including C/C++, Dart, .NET/C#, PHP, and Swift.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Alertmanager supports configured integrations including email/SMTP, webhooks, Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty, Telegram, OpsGenie, and others. Prometheus itself does not send the final notification; third-party delivery services may charge separately.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Alertmanager can group related alerts, route them through a configurable tree, silence alerts for a time, inhibit lower-level alerts when a higher-level alert is active, and control grouped notification timing and repeats.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Prometheus runs as a server process from official Linux, macOS, and Windows binaries, or as a Docker image. It has a web UI, but is not a browser or mobile monitoring agent.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Default path is Prometheus scraping an instrumented/exporter HTTP metrics endpoint. The core server also supports the Prometheus text and OpenMetrics exposition formats. Optional receivers accept OTLP metrics over HTTP and Prometheus Remote Write, but both receivers are disabled by default; Remote Write receive is documented as a low-volume use case, not a replacement for scraping. The Pushgateway is a separate component for short-lived batch-job metrics.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Download and run the server or Docker image; provide a YAML prometheus.yml; configure scrape jobs and targets; instrument code with a client library or deploy an exporter; add recording/alert rules as needed; configure Alertmanager separately for routed notifications.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: The main Prometheus server is a standalone binary with no external dependencies. Official installation paths include Linux, macOS, Windows, and Docker.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: No fixed minimum or recommended CPU and memory size for a defined workload was published in the docs checked. Disk use depends on sample rate and retention; the storage guide gives a rough sizing formula and says observed use averages 1–2 bytes per sample.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: Not an error-event tracker: no exception capture, issue grouping, or handled/unhandled event quotas are part of the Prometheus metrics server. Error counters can be exported as metrics and used in PromQL rules.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: Stack traces, source maps, native crash symbols, and source-code error locations are not applicable to the metrics server's documented function.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: Error issue-to-release, regression, and fix tracking are not applicable to the metrics server's documented function.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: Error-event breadcrumbs, affected-user context, request payloads, and session replay are not applicable to the metrics server's documented function.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Core Prometheus scrapes configured metrics endpoints. Arbitrary website, DNS, port, browser, or transaction checks are outside the core server. A separate Blackbox Exporter can probe endpoints, but is not bundled as the Prometheus server.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Synthetic uptime-check intervals and timeouts are not applicable to the core metrics server. Its metric scrape interval and timeout are configurable (documented defaults: 1 minute and 10 seconds).

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: External probe regions and billable check counts are not applicable to the core self-hosted server. A scrape target is configured by the operator; it is not a distributed vendor probe.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Vendor probe retry confirmation and maintenance windows are not applicable to the core server. Scrape status is exposed as metrics, and operators define their own alert rules.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Managed certificate, domain, and DNS expiration checks are not applicable to the core metrics server.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: Log search, live tail, structured log query, and archived-log retrieval are not applicable. PromQL searches metric time series; it is not a log query interface.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: Prometheus can store and query latency metrics if the app exposes them, but it does not provide distributed request traces, service maps, database spans, or code profiling as an APM product.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: APM trace sampling and trace-volume billing are not applicable. Prometheus scrape/metric relabeling controls are for metric samples, not a priced trace-ingestion plan.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: Browser/mobile real-user monitoring, user sessions, and front-end freezes are not applicable.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Hosted customer-facing status pages, page counts, custom domains, and branding are not applicable to the core Prometheus server.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Status-page subscribers and public incident update channels are not applicable. Alertmanager recipients are operational alert destinations, not status-page subscribers.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Public status-page incident updates and incident history are not applicable to the metrics server.

facts.label: Schedule and grace rules
facts.value: Cron schedule syntax, time zones, missed-run grace periods, and job-duration controls are not applicable to the core server's feature set.

facts.label: Job failure signals
facts.value: A separate Pushgateway can retain batch-job metrics for Prometheus to scrape. Explicit run-history/check-in signals and missed-job alert semantics must be instrumented and configured by the operator; the core server is not a dedicated heartbeat monitor.

facts.label: Exporter ecosystem coverage
facts.value: Official exporter documentation lists integrations across operating systems and hardware, databases, storage, web servers, orchestration, cloud APIs, messaging, and other monitoring systems. Examples include Node Exporter, JMX Exporter, SNMP Exporter, cAdvisor, and Blackbox Exporter.

facts.label: Exporter maintenance status
facts.value: Some exporters are maintained in the Prometheus GitHub organization and marked official; many others are community maintained. The project says it cannot vet every third-party exporter.

facts.label: Target discovery and integration hooks
facts.value: Prometheus includes service-discovery mechanisms and supports file-based discovery as an integration interface when a discovery system is not built in. The integrations docs also list HTTP and webhook-based hooks.

facts.label: Scrape input and exposition
facts.value: The normal collection path is an HTTP scrape of a configured target. Prometheus accepts its own exposition format and OpenMetrics; instrumented applications can use the listed client libraries, or exporters can translate third-party metrics.

facts.label: Alert rule behavior
facts.value: Rules are evaluated on a configured interval. A for duration keeps a condition pending before it fires; keep_firing_for can keep a firing alert active briefly after the condition clears.

facts.label: Alertmanager component boundary
facts.value: Prometheus evaluates alert rules and sends alerts to Alertmanager, a separately installed project component. Alertmanager handles deduplication, grouping, routing, silences, inhibition, and delivery to configured receivers.

facts.label: Default notification timing
facts.value: Alertmanager's default route waits 30 seconds before the first grouped notice, checks a changed group every 5 minutes, and repeats an unchanged firing group every 4 hours. Route settings can override these values.

facts.label: Routing and receiver setup
facts.value: Alertmanager routes by labels through a routing tree and can send to configured receivers such as email, webhook, Slack, PagerDuty, and other listed integrations. Receivers require operator-supplied endpoint credentials.

facts.label: Silences, inhibition, and time windows
facts.value: Operators can silence matching alerts, inhibit a lower-priority alert while a related higher-priority alert is firing, and set active or muted route time intervals.

facts.label: Alert notification templates
facts.value: Alertmanager supports its default notification templates and operator-written Go templates for message content.

facts.label: Alertmanager high availability
facts.value: Multiple Alertmanager instances can form a cluster and synchronize alert state. Prometheus should send alerts directly to every Alertmanager instance, rather than through a load balancer, so peers can continue receiving during a failure.

facts.label: Blackbox probe types
facts.value: The separate Blackbox Exporter probes HTTP, HTTPS, DNS, TCP, ICMP, and gRPC endpoints. Its module configuration also supports Unix sockets and WebSockets.

facts.label: Blackbox probe result and thresholds
facts.value: A probe returns probe_success and timing metrics. HTTP modules can require selected status codes or response-body/header conditions; the default accepted HTTP status codes are 2xx and the default method is GET.

facts.label: Blackbox probe location
facts.value: A Blackbox probe runs from the location where the operator deploys that exporter. The project documents no vendor-run multi-region probe fleet or public check-location allowance.

facts.label: TLS certificate expiry signal
facts.value: An HTTPS Blackbox probe exposes probe_ssl_earliest_cert_expiry as a Unix timestamp after a TLS connection, allowing the operator to alert before a server certificate expires.

facts.label: Minimum CPU and memory
facts.value: The official installation, storage, and operations pages checked do not specify a minimum CPU or RAM size for a defined target workload. Capacity depends on active series, scrape rate, query/rule load, and remote-write configuration.

facts.label: Disk and filesystem needs
facts.value: Use a local POSIX-compliant filesystem for the TSDB. Prometheus explicitly does not support NFS, including AWS EFS, for local storage; allocate disk from the workload estimate plus WAL, head, compaction, and free-space margins.

facts.label: Remote-write compute overhead
facts.value: Remote write adds memory, CPU, and network work. The docs report about 25% higher memory use for many users, but label churn, queued shards, sample rate, and backend latency change the result.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: PromQL query results are available through the stable /api/v1 HTTP API. Optional TSDB admin endpoints can create local snapshots and delete selected series; the admin API is disabled unless --web.enable-admin-api is enabled. Remote Read and Remote Write support connections to external systems.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Metric relabeling can drop samples or remove/keep labels before ingestion. There is no published automatic PII, password, request-body, or secret scrubber. The security docs say not to expose Prometheus component endpoints publicly without protection; TLS and basic authentication are available but described as experimental.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: The operator selects the local TSDB path and any configured remote-storage destination. Vendor-managed region selection and a vendor DPA do not apply to the self-hosted project.

facts.label: Local durability and backups
facts.value: The local TSDB is single-node and has no built-in clustering or replication. Prometheus recommends snapshots for backups; a raw copy can miss data since the last completed block, typically about two hours.

facts.label: Remote storage directions
facts.value: Prometheus can write its samples to a remote URL, receive remote-write samples, read samples from a remote URL, or serve samples through its remote-read endpoint. Remote read is not a stable API; Remote Write 1.0 is standardized and 2.0 remains experimental.

facts.label: Remote storage choices
facts.value: The official integration catalog lists compatible remote-storage projects such as Cortex, Grafana Mimir, Thanos, and VictoriaMetrics, alongside commercial systems. These are separate products or projects, not Prometheus-hosted storage.

facts.label: Remote-write outage and resource behavior
facts.value: Remote write retries failed requests, but unsent data can be lost if the endpoint remains down for more than two hours. It commonly increases memory use by about 25% according to user reports cited in the docs; actual CPU, memory, and network needs depend on data shape and queue settings.

facts.label: Agent mode
facts.value: The same Prometheus binary can run as an Agent that scrapes and remote-writes metrics with a smaller temporary WAL. It disables local queries, recording rules, alerting, and the full local TSDB; the WAL buffer is limited to about two hours.

facts.label: Federation
facts.value: One Prometheus server can scrape selected series from another through /federate. The docs describe hierarchical aggregation across data centers and cross-service federation; selection uses match[] selectors.

facts.label: Public endpoint exposure
facts.value: Prometheus warns that component HTTP endpoints can reveal all time-series data and operational details, and can be overloaded. Do not expose /metrics, component APIs, or /pprof publicly without suitable network controls and protection.

facts.label: TLS and client authentication
facts.value: Prometheus components support TLS, including client certificates. The security guidance sets TLS 1.2 as the default minimum for the Go projects; an operator can configure a different supported minimum.

facts.label: HTTP basic authentication
facts.value: Basic authentication is supported; without TLS it sends credentials in cleartext. Prometheus hashes server-side basic-auth passwords with bcrypt.

facts.label: Administrative and lifecycle endpoints
facts.value: The admin API and HTTP-triggered reload/shutdown lifecycle endpoints are disabled by default. Enabling them exposes mutating controls to callers who can reach those endpoints.

facts.label: User roles and built-in RBAC
facts.value: The official security and HTTPS/authentication pages describe endpoint-level TLS and basic authentication, but do not publish named user roles, a team directory, or a built-in role-based permissions model for the server UI.

facts.label: Blackbox exporter target access
facts.value: The security docs warn that anyone able to call Blackbox Exporter's /probe can make it connect to arbitrary URL-parameter targets. Restrict access to the exporter to prevent server-side request abuse and credential leakage.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Prometheus; official URL https://prometheus.io/

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: No former name or rebrand statement was found in the official overview, project blog, or repository checked.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Active community project. Latest release 3.16.0, dated 2026-11-04. CNCF graduated project since 2018-08-09. No shutdown, sunset, or acquisition notice found in the official sources checked.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: The project is CNCF-hosted, with its own community governance; it is not a company product with customer enrollment.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: Apache License 2.0. Official source repository: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Public docs, GitHub issue trackers/discussions, CNCF Slack, IRC, Matrix, user and announcement mailing lists, and a public Discourse forum. No response-time SLA from the core project is published. The project site has a separate third-party commercial support/training list.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Operators manage installation, upgrades, persistent data, retention, backups, and endpoint security. Prometheus recommends TSDB snapshots for backups; release notes and migration docs are public. LTS releases receive selected high-severity fixes for one year on a best-effort community basis.

facts.label: Standard minor-release support
facts.value: A new minor release cycle starts about every six weeks. Minor releases generally stop receiving bug fixes after the next cycle begins, so users affected by a bug may need to upgrade to the latest release.

facts.label: Current long-term support release
facts.value: The download page lists 3.13.5 as the current LTS patch. The LTS table gives the 3.13 branch dates as 2026-07-01 through 2027-07-31. LTS receives selected high-severity fixes, defined as CVSS 7.0 or higher, on a best-effort basis.

facts.label: Upgrade compatibility and migration
facts.value: The project promises API stability for mature APIs and says upgrades should generally be straightforward, while warning that new features can still bring regressions. Breaking changes are documented in release notes or migration docs.

facts.label: Security-fix response policy
facts.value: The security policy says the project strives to release security fixes within seven days for Prometheus and named core components.

facts.label: Support commitment
facts.value: Prometheus offers public community channels and a list of outside support and training providers, but publishes no core-project response-time or resolution SLA.

facts.label: Billing unit and base plans
facts.value: Traffic is metered as monthly website page views; pages may be grouped into a logical website using one token.

facts.label: Monthly and annual rates
facts.value: Essentials is $37/month or $34/month with annual billing; Professional is $96/month or $88/month with annual billing. Free is $0/month.

facts.label: Currency code and commitment
facts.value: The page shows a dollar sign but no ISO currency code. It supports monthly or annual billing; the exact annual invoice total, tax treatment, and minimum commitment beyond the selected plan are not stated.

facts.label: Added traffic capacity
facts.value: Extra traffic can be bought in plan-specific blocks and allocated among websites; the public page has a dynamic selector but no fixed rate in its text.

facts.label: Ongoing Free plan
facts.value: Free is advertised at $0/month for solo projects and personal websites; it includes one user, one website, 1,000 page views/month, 24-hour retention, Core Web Vitals, and email performance notifications.

facts.label: Free commercial eligibility
facts.value: The pricing page describes Free as for solo projects and personal websites; terms and pricing do not define a test for commercial-use eligibility.

facts.label: Free card requirement
facts.value: Card requirement for retaining the ongoing Free plan is not stated on the public pricing and billing pages checked.

facts.label: Trial duration and feature level
facts.value: New accounts receive a one-time 14-day trial with Professional features and limits; the docs say anyone in the organization can start it.

facts.label: Trial card and conversion rules
facts.value: Whether a card is required or an account automatically converts or charges at the end of the trial is not stated in the pricing docs or terms checked.

facts.label: Smallest paid plan for RUM
facts.value: Essentials starts at $37/month, or $34/month on annual billing; includes 75,000 monthly page views, 3+ websites, unlimited users, and 30-day retention.

facts.label: Smallest paid plan for browser error monitoring
facts.value: Professional starts at $96/month or $88/month on annual billing; includes 500,000 monthly page views, 10+ websites, unlimited users, 90-day retention, and Error Monitoring.

facts.label: Traffic cap behavior
facts.value: Capacity is metered per minute. For example, 100,000 monthly views is allocated at about 5 per minute after rounding and buffer; over-limit events in a minute may be excluded, and the counter resets next minute.

facts.label: Bursts and purchased capacity
facts.value: Traffic bursts may be partially buffered based on prior traffic, and customers can buy more capacity; billing docs say capacity additions are prorated for the remaining term.

facts.label: Spend alerts and hard dollar cap
facts.value: No separate account-wide spend cap or financial budget alert was found in the pricing, traffic-limit, and billing pages checked.

facts.label: Usage visibility
facts.value: The account usage page shows total traffic and over-limit traffic for the previous 30 days; no financial alert threshold or automatic plan upgrade is documented.

facts.label: Retention by plan
facts.value: Pricing lists 24 hours on Free, 30 days on Essentials, 90 days on Professional, and custom retention for Custom.

facts.label: Retention extensions and signal split
facts.value: Separate retention rates or distinct limits for errors, activity, Lighthouse, CrUX, and raw data were not stated in the pricing and guide pages checked.

facts.label: User limits
facts.value: Free includes one user; Essentials and Professional include unlimited users; Custom is described as custom.

facts.label: Website limits
facts.value: Free includes one website; Essentials lists 3+; Professional 10+; Custom allows a custom count.

facts.label: Alert-recipient limits
facts.value: A separate number of notification recipients or per-recipient charge is not stated in the pricing or docs pages checked.

facts.label: Log intake and loss
facts.value: Request Metrics is not documented as a log-ingestion or log-management product; its browser activity/events are application analytics, not a searchable log allowance.

facts.label: Log query and extra-data charges
facts.value: No log query, scan, indexing, or archive charge applies to the documented product scope.

facts.label: Vendor home region
facts.value: TrackJS LLC is a Minnesota limited liability company with offices in Minneapolis, United States.

facts.label: Buyer eligibility
facts.value: Terms require compliance with U.S. export controls and prohibit use by embargoed persons or destinations; no complete supported-country list was found.

facts.label: Supported buyer-country list
facts.value: A full list of supported or excluded buyer countries is not published in the pricing or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Browser real-user performance monitoring, synthetic Lighthouse performance tests, web-resource diagnostics, analytics, and Professional-plan browser error monitoring. Detection and diagnosis, not a public status page.

facts.label: Standard hosted service
facts.value: Free, Essentials, Professional, and Custom plans are offered as a hosted Request Metrics service.

facts.label: Custom dedicated or on-premises service
facts.value: The End User Data page says dedicated instances or on-premises installations are available by contacting the company. Public implementation detail and plan boundaries are not stated.

facts.label: Supported runtime and integrations
facts.value: Browser JavaScript agent is documented; named integration guides cover Next.js, Shopify, and WordPress. The Next.js guide says the agent runs client-side only.

facts.label: Other application SDKs
facts.value: Native mobile, server-runtime, and backend language agents were not documented in the browser-agent and integration pages checked.

facts.label: Email alerts
facts.value: Free includes email performance notifications; the pricing matrix also lists help via email.

facts.label: Other alert channels and costs
facts.value: SMS, voice, push, chat, and webhook alert support and rates were not found in the pricing, FAQ, or docs pages checked.

facts.label: Performance budgets and notifications
facts.value: Professional includes performance budgets; the pricing matrix also lists performance notifications.

facts.label: Noise controls and escalation
facts.value: Grouping, delay, mute, acknowledgement, escalation, and on-call routing rules were not found in the plan matrix, docs overview, FAQ, or user guides checked.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Browser agent loads from the Request Metrics CDN, an NPM module, or a script tag; customers may bundle or serve the file from their own origin. It still sends data to the vendor unless a separate custom full-service deployment is arranged.

facts.label: Browser and private network scope
facts.value: Docs cover websites, browser users, and public Lighthouse crawler IP; private-network server agents or private probes are not documented.

facts.label: Telemetry input
facts.value: The browser agent collects page performance and user activity and exposes calls for custom events, metadata, user identification, and custom tracked errors.

facts.label: General monitoring protocols
facts.value: A general log, metrics, trace, OTLP, syslog, or server ingestion endpoint was not documented in the product docs and API reference checked.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Docs describe creating an account and website, previewing the site scan, selecting pages, then adding the JavaScript snippet, NPM module, or script tag and deploying it. A scan can run weekly even without installing the agent.

facts.label: Error coverage
facts.value: Professional lists Error Monitoring; browser-agent guides expose custom error capture and the user guide says RUM can detect errors. The documented scope is browser/client-side.

facts.label: Automatic capture and grouping
facts.value: The docs support tracked errors and report browser errors, but a public description of grouping, issue merge/ignore controls, and dropped-event counters was not found in the pricing, user guides, FAQ, or agent reference checked.

facts.label: Error locations
facts.value: Error guide and marketing material describe stack traces and affected sessions for browser errors; the public browser agent exposes error tracking.

facts.label: Source maps and code mapping
facts.value: Source-map upload, source-code mapping, and symbolication steps were not found in the browser-agent docs, user guides, or integrations checked.

facts.label: Release metadata
facts.value: Browser agent metadata can include an application code version, but no automated release/deploy integration or regression workflow is documented in the agent reference, pricing, or integrations pages checked.

facts.label: Fix and regression workflow
facts.value: No release association, resolved-in-version, regression alert, or deployment comparison workflow was found in the pricing, guides, or agent documentation checked.

facts.label: User and session context
facts.value: Professional lists User Activity; guides describe session timelines, affected sessions, and user actions. Default browser activity avoids form input values and does not record video.

facts.label: Video replay
facts.value: The end-user data guide explicitly says the service does not keep video sessions.

facts.label: Synthetic check type
facts.value: Lighthouse tests scan selected public website pages for performance, with desktop and mobile diagnostics. They are page-performance tests, not a published HTTP/API availability monitor or scripted user-flow check.

facts.label: Test schedule
facts.value: Product page says selected pages are scanned weekly and can be tested on demand.

facts.label: Timeout and configurable frequency range
facts.value: A configurable interval range and test timeout were not found in the synthetic-test, getting-started, or pricing docs checked.

facts.label: Published crawler location
facts.value: The synthetic-testing guide publishes one crawler IP address, 148.113.208.106, for firewall allowlisting. It gives no city, country, selectable-region list, or private-probe option.

facts.label: Location choices and metering
facts.value: Regional test selection, private probes, and per-location billing rules were not found in the crawler, pricing, or getting-started pages checked.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Retry/vote rules for failing synthetic runs and a maintenance-window feature were not found in the synthetic, pricing, notifications, or FAQ pages checked.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry checks
facts.value: Certificate-expiry and domain-expiry monitoring are outside the documented performance-test offer and were not listed in the pricing or synthetic-test docs.

facts.label: Backend request diagnosis
facts.value: The verified product is browser real-user and synthetic web performance monitoring; no server traces, database query diagnosis, or backend code profiling were documented.

facts.label: Trace sampling and billing
facts.value: No server trace sampling controls or trace-based billing unit are documented; the published meter is website page views.

facts.label: Real-user performance signals
facts.value: RUM covers page load, LCP, CLS, INP, FCP, TTFB, resource timing, browser/device differences, and user activity. Free lists Core Web Vitals; Essentials adds RUM; Professional adds budgets and traffic analytics.

facts.label: Log search and archives
facts.value: No log search, archive, or log-retrieval service is documented in product, pricing, or data API pages.

facts.label: Customer status-page limits
facts.value: No customer-facing status-page product or page/component/domain limits are listed in the pricing or product docs checked.

facts.label: Status-page subscribers
facts.value: No status-page subscriber service or outage-notification channel is documented in pricing or user guides.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: No incident/status update workflow or public status-page integrations are documented in product or pricing pages.

facts.label: Job schedules and grace rules
facts.value: No cron, scheduled-job, or heartbeat monitor is described in product or pricing pages.

facts.label: Job failure signals
facts.value: No job start/end ping, missed heartbeat, job output, or schedule-failure signal is documented.

facts.label: Custom on-prem requirements
facts.value: On-premises installation is advertised, but the docs, pricing, and terms pages checked do not publish a supported architecture, dependencies, or CPU, memory, and storage sizing.

facts.label: Data export
facts.value: Home page describes CSV export from reports. A read-only JSON Data API returns RUM summaries and per-URL results, with up to 90 days requested subject to plan retention and a documented rate limit of 100 requests/minute per website.

facts.label: Data deletion and cancellation
facts.value: Pricing docs say cancellation closes the account immediately and purges its data; no refund is made, while paid funds remain as account credit for possible resubscription. DPA describes personal-data deletion within the service and destruction at termination.

facts.label: Default end-user privacy
facts.value: The browser agent says it uses no cookies, stores a session timestamp in local storage, hashes the website token with IP and browser user agent then discards the IP, and does not keep video sessions. Activity collection avoids input values and records generic element attributes.

facts.label: Custom personal or sensitive data
facts.value: The agent permits user IDs, events, and arbitrary metadata that may identify people; the customer is told to obtain consent. The DPA prohibits sending sensitive data or special-category personal data.

facts.label: Configurable sensitive-field scrubber
facts.value: A server-side scrubber or configurable sensitive-field mask was not found in the browser installation, agent reference, end-user data, or DPA pages checked.

facts.label: Marketing-site privacy policy
facts.value: The privacy policy says the company website may use cookies and collect visitor IP and account/contact data; this is a different processing scope from the browser agent's end-user monitoring claims.

facts.label: Marketing data residency claim
facts.value: Homepage states Request Metrics data is resident in Canada.

facts.label: DPA, storage, and subprocessors
facts.value: Public DPA revision 3.1 identifies OVH hosting in Montreal, AWS offsite backup/cloud storage in Seattle, and Mailgun transactional email in the United States. The DPA is completed and emailed to the company.

facts.label: Residency claim versus processing locations
facts.value: “Data is resident in Canada” on the homepage is broader than the DPA's Seattle backup and U.S. Mailgun disclosures. Exact residency scope by data type and backup is not reconciled publicly.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Request Metrics; canonical site is requestmetrics.com.

facts.label: Availability
facts.value: Current product and service pages are active; the blog index carries a security post dated 2026-10-31 and the product blog lists a 2025-12-22 feature post.

facts.label: Acquisition, shutdown, or sunset notice
facts.value: No such notice was located in the official blog, product blog, company page, terms, or current product pages checked.

facts.label: Hosted software license
facts.value: The terms describe the service and agents as proprietary and grant a limited, non-transferable use license; they do not offer an open-source license.

facts.label: Public source repository
facts.value: No public Request Metrics service repository or source license was linked from its website or documentation pages checked.

facts.label: Custom deployment license
facts.value: A separate license or deployment agreement for the advertised on-premises offer was not published on the pricing, docs, or terms pages checked.

facts.label: Public docs and support
facts.value: Public docs and FAQ are available; the plan matrix lists help via email, while Custom adds dedicated customer support and staff training. No contractual response-time target was found.

facts.label: Custom on-prem upkeep
facts.value: Upgrade, backup, restore, security-update, and supported-release instructions for the complete on-prem service were not found in docs, terms, or product pages checked.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Subscriptions automatically renew under the terms; current Stripe portal cancellation returns the workspace to Free on the displayed end date. Failed subscription payment allows five days to update the card before moving to Free.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Free shows critical/high finding titles and counts of other findings. Evidence, affected addresses and fixes require paid plans. Only outage/recovery/reminder notifications are included; finding/certificate-threshold notifications are paid.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: Signup docs request name, email, password and agreement to terms, without a card step. Marketing says no card is required to start. No explicit commercial-use exclusion found, but a current Free commercial-use grant is not stated.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: Marketing advertises a 14-day free trial with no card. Current signup starts on Free, and rebuilt plan docs do not explain how a current paid-plan trial is activated or ends.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Default older pricing view: Personal 10k USD 41.59/month equivalent with yearly selected, USD 499.10/year or USD 49.91 monthly. Team 20k USD 103.73/month equivalent, USD 1,244.80/year or USD 124.48 monthly.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Adding a property, member or status page above quota is blocked. Paused properties and pending invitations still count. Remove/archive resources or upgrade to make room.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: When the monthly workspace notification quota is exhausted, notifications stop until the next period. Monitoring and the dashboard continue; the owner is emailed. Test messages do not count.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: An on-demand scan costing more than the balance does not start. Scheduled checks and notifications continue; already-running or unverified active scans are not charged again.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Manual owner-only credit purchase and pre-scan insufficient-balance rejection; shared workspace balance and dated ledger. Monthly credit expires, purchased credit lasts 12 months.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: Quota usage shows properties, members, clients, pages and notifications; no user-set dollar cap, configurable low-balance threshold or per-property credit budget found.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: 3 months of history viewable in the app.

facts.value: 12 months of history viewable in the app.

facts.value: Public status item 'With history' shows a 90-day strip and uptime percentage. Migrated history before January 1, 2026 and raw check results did not move.
