facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: Privacy policy says services are offered worldwide; no exhaustive buyer-country or sanctions eligibility list found.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Hosted website availability, configuration/expiry/security checks and public status communication; each website receives the same 17 robots.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Phone-style lab page-speed tests and aggregated real Chrome visitor speed data; not an instrumented backend trace or application error tracker.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Vendor-hosted browser service. Adding a website starts externally run checks; no service installation on the monitored host is required.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: No complete self-host distribution, deployment guide or private-probe installation found in the current product docs.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: No client library is required for the documented external website checks or Google's aggregated real-user speed data.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Free: email only, with any number of personal email channels. Paid: email, Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, generic webhook, Zapier, Pabbly, Telegram, PagerDuty and Pushover.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: SMS stopped in the November 2 rebuild; old SMS channels no longer send. Native phone-call delivery is not established by the current channel list.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Numeric current monthly notification caps, paid overage price, country restrictions and external-service total not fully published. Pushover needs its own license after its trial; PagerDuty requires a separate account/service.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Rules route workspace-wide, by property or by check to one channel each; severity/type/dimension filtering; property/check rules can replace general routing. Rules can be paused.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Notifications are not grouped or sent as daily summaries. Five critical findings in one minute send five notifications. Outage threshold default 2 minutes; selectable right away/1/2/5/10/15 minutes. Reminders off or every 30 minutes/1 hour/4 hours.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Outages can be acknowledged, muted for 1 hour/8 hours/1 day/1 week/until changed, ignored or resolved. Acknowledging leaves notifications on. A manually resolved ongoing problem opens a new event on its next measurement.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: No native timed multi-person escalation/on-call rotation policy found. PagerDuty handles on-call response using settings in the user's PagerDuty service.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Public HTTP/HTTPS websites on ports 80/443. Addresses pointing into private networks, other protocols and other ports are rejected. Generic APIs, mail servers and server/IP checks are outside the current property model.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Firewall allowlisting by User-Agent 'Robot.alp User Agent 1.0' and the published IPv4/IPv6 list. Requests blocked with 401/403/429 or Cloudflare challenge are treated as unmeasurable, with no outage event.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Customer log/error/metric/trace ingestion is not part of the documented website-property offer. Public-source reads and external requests supply measurements. A generic channel sends outbound JSON POST notifications, not inbound telemetry.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Create/verify an email account; add the website address; Robotalp creates the property and all robots. Default account email channel and workspace rule are created automatically. First results fill in as checks finish.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: For Vulnerability and Exposed-file scans, prove ownership with a DNS TXT record or home-page meta tag, then press Verify. Security coverage remains partial until verification; other checks start without it.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Current website checks include HTTP/HTTPS availability with redirects and status codes, content assertions, certificate/domain/DNS, broken links, lab/real-user speed and externally visible security checks.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Content rule supports comma-separated must-contain and must-not-contain words, searched in visible text or HTML. A mismatch generates a notification/event without counting as downtime.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Request method/headers/regions cannot be chosen. Current property setup rejects non-web/private/custom-port addresses; migration excludes API checks with extra settings and browser-action web checks.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Availability: Free every 300 seconds; Solo/Team/Agency every 60 seconds. Schedule is fixed by the plan and cannot be customized. Immediate extra confirmation follows failure.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Availability attempt fails if the site does not answer within 30 seconds. No user-configurable timeout range is documented; request behavior is not user-selectable.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Robotalp selects several regions; users cannot choose regions. Scheduled runs, including documented failure confirmation, do not spend scan credits. No fixed one-/three-location offer can be selected.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Current regional/city list, number of normal regions per check, private-probe installation and per-region manual-scan charging are not published in the checked current docs. Public IPv4/IPv6 allowlist is available.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: One failed region triggers immediate confirmation from every region. An outage requires failure in more than one; recovery closes the event after success in more than one region. Single-region failures send no event/alert.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: One-off maintenance windows can cover a whole property or one robot. Measurement continues; covered outages do not lower score or open events. Whole-property pause stops all measurement and retains the quota slot.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Certificate validity/expiry plus TLS/cipher checks. Free scans daily; paid every 6 hours. Manual-renewal findings at 30/14/7 days, high finding at 7 days for automatic-renewal certs; expired/invalid is Critical.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Daily public WHOIS/RDAP expiry and transfer-lock checks on every plan. Attention at 14 days; expired/missing registration creates a critical finding, with paid finding notifications. Some TLDs lack published dates.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: DNS checks name-server changes, dangling CNAME, DNSSEC and CAA information. Free daily; paid hourly. Critical/high findings notify only on paid plans.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Current page quotas: Free 1; Solo more than Free; Team more than Solo; Agency more than Team. Exact paid counts and independent item caps are not public. Each item is one whole website property, once per page.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Free has no own-domain support. Solo/Team/Agency support own domains; each page has one custom-domain field, CNAME setup and automatic certificate provisioning.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Pages are public and cannot be made private. Language/theme/colors/font are open to all. White label is absent on Free and included with Agency; Solo/Team entitlement must be checked in the account.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: No visitor subscriptions by email or RSS; no subscriber quota, delivery allowance or subscriber add-on to price for the documented current status pages.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Automatic state from Robotalp property measurements. Users cannot post announcements; page has no past-event list. Optional history is a 90-day uptime strip; running/upcoming maintenance is shown.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: Daily reads of Google's Chrome visitor data over the last 28 days, at the 75th percentile, separately phone/desktop: LCP, INP and CLS. Low-traffic sites may have no data. No SDK install, event/session allowance or separate session rate is specified.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: No current measurement export format, bulk download, archive destination or replacement public data API documented in the checked current guide set.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Deleting a property archives it, stops measuring and frees its quota slot. History remains for the plan retention period and returns if the address is added again; re-verification is required.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Account profile accepts a deletion request that can be withdrawn. The account continues working and is not deleted immediately.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Account deletion completion deadline, retained-data/backup purge timing and delivery format for a portability request are not published.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Only the owner can delete a workspace; this closes it for everybody and removes its properties, robots, members and settings. The action cannot be undone; the separate user account remains.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Privacy policy gives access/correction/deletion/portability rights to covered individuals, subject to exemptions; account tools or contact requests are the stated route.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Channel URLs are shortened in lists; keys/tokens are not shown there. Channel settings are personal and hidden from teammates. Webhook custom JSON body/headers allow selecting the outbound payload.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Public status pages omit findings, health score, likely outage causes and diagnostic reasons; only state and optional history/dimensions are exposed.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: No default field redaction, request-body/password filter, scan-result exclusion rules or plan-specific sensitive-finding storage controls found.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: No current monitoring storage country, selectable residency region or per-signal data-location guarantee found.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: No published downloadable/signable customer DPA found in the checked privacy/terms or current documentation navigation.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Privacy's dated processor list names Limestone Networks, AWS and Digital Ocean for requests/storage, plus Nexmo, 2Checkout and PayPal. Current billing docs use Stripe and current migration removes SMS. Current complete processor inventory is unresolved.

facts.value: Notification groups can have multiple channels and multiple instances of the same integration. No numeric alert-rule/group/recipient maximum located in pricing, alert docs or integrations.

facts.label: Log meter and read usage
facts.value: Write usage is total uncompressed OTLP bytes sent; read usage is uncompressed bytes traversed by an operation. Logs Usage shows 14 days of both.

facts.label: Record/rate limits and loss
facts.value: No numeric maximum log-record size, server ingest-rate limit, complete retry/loss guarantee or dropped-record counter specification found in general and Ruby/Node log docs.

facts.label: Query and extra-data fees
facts.value: Log scan/read volume is measured, but no separate USD read/scan/query/index/export tariff or included read allowance found in usage/billing docs, pricing and FAQ. Paid log write overage is USD 0.46/GB.

facts.label: Marketplace billing
facts.value: AWS, DigitalOcean and Heroku have separate billing/account workflows. AWS quantities/renewals change through the Marketplace agreement; DigitalOcean handles plan changes/cancel through its Add-On controls.

facts.label: AWS daily quota
facts.value: AWS Marketplace docs say exceeding the daily transaction limit restricts detailed traces and, on some plans, charts for the rest of that day; upgrade by amending the Marketplace agreement.

facts.label: DigitalOcean suspension
facts.value: Unpaid DigitalOcean invoices temporarily disable the Scout organization; paying reactivates it and data is retained during the suspension window.

facts.label: Vendor country and buyer eligibility
facts.value: Legal operator Zimuth, Inc.; home country/incorporation address and complete buyer-country list not found in about, contact, terms or privacy. Delaware governing law and US telemetry hosting are published but do not establish the company's home.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Application performance monitoring, request/job traces, errors, logs, query analysis, memory/N+1 insights, threshold alerts and statistical endpoint/job anomalies.

facts.label: Adjacent product boundary
facts.value: October roundup says Scout Trails is a separate product with its own signup and free beta; Scout MCP is a read-only connection to this monitoring account.

facts.label: Delivery model
facts.value: Vendor-hosted platform with customer-installed language/log agents. Docs say Scout handles the service. No complete self-hosted backend installation offer established.

facts.label: Supported stacks
facts.value: Ruby/Rails, Sinatra/Rack; Python Django/Flask/FastAPI; Node Express/NestJS; PHP Laravel/Symfony; Elixir Phoenix. Dedicated current Node docs confirm support even where older overview lists omit it.

facts.label: Log language gates
facts.value: Ruby and Python logging packages; Elixir built-in from agent 2.0+, Node built-in from 2.0.2+. PHP logging is on the roadmap.

facts.label: Alert channels
facts.value: Email, Slack, webhooks, PagerDuty, Splunk On-Call/VictorOps and Opsgenie are documented notification channels.

facts.label: Delivery fees and credits
facts.value: No native SMS/call country coverage, included phone-message credits or per-recipient delivery tariff published in pricing/alert integrations.

facts.label: Error triage and noise
facts.value: Group by error type/location/request components; assign priority/owner, bulk resolve, defer to a date/time or reactivate. Critical endpoints give new errors high priority; recurrences reopen resolved groups.

facts.label: Threshold notifications
facts.value: Alerts evaluate web/job performance metrics; notification groups route open and closed events to all configured channels. Daily/weekly digest and insights emails are separate optional summaries.

facts.label: Anomaly controls
facts.value: Per-monitor sensitivity, direction and minimum duration 1–60 consecutive anomalous minutes. Notify once when a live event opens; no repeat, resolved or retrospective notifications. Close after three normal minutes or 10+ minutes silence.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Application agents on servers/containers and hosting platforms; Heroku, AWS Marketplace and DigitalOcean procurement advertised. Core agent handles supported native platform communication; Node logging uses direct OTLP.

facts.label: Local development versus RUM
facts.value: Ruby DevTrace is a no-signup, in-browser local development profiler. FAQ sends users to dedicated browser/RUM tools for that job; no production browser/mobile RUM agent established in current Scout platform docs.

facts.label: Data ingestion
facts.value: Agent-collected metrics/traces use Scout's reporting service; FAQ describes serialized JSON over SSL. Log agents send uncompressed OTLP-formatted data using log ingest credentials.

facts.label: Read credentials and API
facts.value: Public read API uses X-SCOUT-API; ingest Scout Key is different and cannot read account/API data. Hosted MCP is read-only and scoped to accessible organizations.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Install language agent/gem/package, set monitor=true, app name and Scout Key, then deploy. Enable errors and logging separately where required; logs use their own ingest key. Node must initialize before instrumented packages.

facts.label: Capture paths and SDK differences
facts.value: Ruby supports automatic unhandled exceptions and manual Error.capture. Python captures Django/Celery failure signals; caught errors require manual capture. Node supports Express error middleware, NestJS exception filter and captureError; PHP/Elixir have dedicated agent capture.

facts.label: Grouping and triage
facts.value: Errors group by type, code location and request components. UI records counts/recency, endpoint priority and owner; resolve/defer/reactivate/bulk actions documented.

facts.label: Readable locations
facts.value: Complete server-side stack traces and request context; GitHub integration shows source code and deploy/commit context. Trace CODE/SQL views expose backtraces and sanitized queries.

facts.label: Source maps and native symbols
facts.value: No browser JS source-map upload, dSYM, ProGuard/R8 or minidump processing workflow/limit found in error, Node, trace docs, public schema or official-domain searches.

facts.label: Release and recurring fixes
facts.value: revision_sha can identify builds; Git integration adds branch/tag/diff deploy markers and code context. Resolved errors automatically reactivate if the error occurs again. Can open pre-filled GitHub or Linear issues.

facts.label: Context
facts.value: Errors can include stack, request URI/method/params/session/custom attributes and user identification when configured; logs correlate through transaction IDs and custom context.

facts.label: Replay
facts.value: No visual DOM/video session replay or replay quota/price found in features, error/log docs, current FAQ or supported agents. Local DevTrace is a development profiler.

facts.label: Searching and live inspection
facts.value: Initially loads 10K recent records, with more loadable; pre-load time/content/attribute filtering and browser-side severity/endpoint/regex filters. Pause/resume controls log loading.

facts.label: Archives and longer history
facts.value: Standard log docs explicitly recommend sending data to another location for longer retention. Enterprise can negotiate custom retention; no automatic customer archive/rehydration workflow documented.

facts.label: Performance diagnosis
facts.value: Request/job timelines and aggregate summaries, slow SQL, code backtraces, N+1 detection and memory-bloat insights. Large SQL statements over 16K characters are not collected for sanitization overhead reasons.

facts.label: Profiling method
facts.value: AutoInstruments instruments Ruby controller code; auto-instrumented spans below 5 ms are folded into parent time. Explicitly instrumented spans are retained. ScoutProf is unsupported.

facts.label: Sampling controls
facts.value: Ruby/Python sample_rate defaults 1.0 and accepts 0.0–1.0, with endpoint/job overrides and ignore lists. Ruby 6 uses fractional configuration. Detailed-trace selection separately scores throughput, deviation, duration and time since last saved trace.

facts.label: Sampling versus invoice
facts.value: Pricing counts traced requests/jobs, while agent docs distinguish captured metrics from selectively saved detailed traces. No explicit invoice formula for applying request sampling versus full observed traffic found in pricing, FAQ, configuration or in-depth guides.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: FAQ identifies browser RUM as a job handled with another product, while Scout agents and DevTrace focus on server performance/local development. No native browser/mobile production RUM allowance or session price established.

facts.label: Full-backend host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable to the hosted edition researched. Local agents, DevTrace and self-hosted MCP are client tools; no complete backend self-host installation offer established.

facts.label: Programmatic retrieval
facts.value: Public OpenAPI exposes JSON metrics, endpoints/jobs, traces, error groups/occurrences, insights and anomalies. Trace pages permit up to 100 results with limit/offset; normal trace lookback seven days, errors/anomalies 30 days.

facts.label: Bulk log export
facts.value: No documented complete raw-log download, archive export, log API endpoint or export price found in log docs, current OpenAPI, MCP docs, pricing or FAQ. Log MCP/CLI access is explicitly still roadmap.

facts.label: Deletion and cancellation
facts.value: Terms say cancellation terminates access and data deletion is immediate/permanent; charges continue until transmission ceases. Privacy directs account/organization deletion requests to Support.

facts.label: Backup purge details
facts.value: No separately documented full backup-erasure deadline, self-serve granular deletion workflow or post-cancel recovery/export grace period found in terms, privacy, compliance or API.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Ruby errors default-filter password and s3-key; ignored exception defaults include RecordNotFound/RoutingError. URL query reporting can be reduced to path only; job parameter capture defaults off. Python remote-IP collection defaults on.

facts.label: Logs and Node error data
facts.value: Set log severity/capture controls before export. Node middleware captures query/body params and session context; custom context propagates to logs, so avoid sending secrets there.

facts.label: Encryption and SSO
facts.value: Security page states encryption in transit and at rest. SAML SSO and enterprise provisioning available on Enterprise; BAA can be requested.

facts.label: AI integration data handling
facts.value: Privacy says Scout does not train AI models on customer data. Connected AI providers process returned monitoring data under their own policies; connections can be revoked.

facts.label: Telemetry storage
facts.value: Scout says monitoring data is stored/processed on AWS in the United States. No customer-selectable EU or additional telemetry region established in checked privacy/security/compliance pages.

facts.label: DPA and subprocessors
facts.value: Compliance docs make a DPA available by contacting Support; no public full DPA at guessed /dpa or complete telemetry subprocessor list found in checked pages. Stripe named for payments.

facts.label: Identity and operator
facts.value: Scout Monitoring; https://www.scoutapm.com/; also called Scout APM in docs and terms. Operator named as Zimuth, Inc.

facts.label: Availability and current news
facts.value: Active Free/paid offer, October 2026 product roundup and public service status. No whole-product closure or sale of current Scout APM found in checked blog, ScoutApp/newsletter/changelog categories and official-domain searches.

facts.label: Historical acquisition
facts.value: Official 2017 post says Scout's original server-monitoring product was acquired by Pingdom in summer 2017 and renamed Pingdom Server Monitor; Scout then focused on APM.

facts.label: Component retirement
facts.value: Scout FAQ says ScoutProf was deprecated, replaced by AutoInstruments and is no longer supported. Ruby repository README still calls ScoutProf beta.

facts.label: Platform and client code licenses
facts.value: Hosted service is proprietary under Terms. Ruby v6.0.0 agent uses MIT, with bundled rusage explicitly under Artistic License 2.0; current Python agent LICENSE is MIT.

facts.label: Help and support
facts.value: Public docs, email and Discord human support. Paid plans get priority; Enterprise premier support. FAQ describes business-hours support; no fixed numerical response-time guarantee published in checked support/pricing terms.

facts.label: Full-backend upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable to vendor-operated backend. App owners still update their agents; public agent/core changelogs are available.

facts.value: A web HTTP request or background job is one trace; database queries inside a request are not billed separately.

facts.label: Per-request event limits
facts.value: Troubleshooting guide says a request can exceed 100 unique event descriptions or 2,048 total spans; complex traces can lose detail or be pruned.

facts.label: Real-user browser/mobile performance
facts.value: Not applicable to this server-side Ruby APM offer; reviewed features and setup pages describe the app-side agent, not browser-session or mobile RUM collection.

facts.label: Error grouping and capture
facts.value: Not applicable: FAQ explicitly says Skylight does not provide dedicated error tracking.

facts.label: Error stack traces and source maps
facts.value: Not applicable: source locations are for performance trace events, not readable error stack traces or error source-map processing.

facts.label: Error release and fix tracking
facts.value: Not applicable to error issues; deploy markers and GitHub commit links give performance context, but no error regression lifecycle is documented.

facts.label: Error context and replay
facts.value: Not applicable: no error-tracking or session-replay product is documented in the FAQ or feature pages.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Not applicable: no complete self-hosted backend is offered in public deployment documentation.

facts.label: App deletion
facts.value: App owners can permanently delete an app from its settings page; support docs say deletion is permanent.

facts.label: Account cancellation
facts.value: Account owners can cancel from account settings after removing the agent; paid usage already incurred must be settled.

facts.label: Data retrieval and export
facts.value: MCP beta exposes selected aggregate performance data and deploy metadata. No bulk telemetry export, standard archive destination or general download procedure was found in support, account, pricing or terms pages.

facts.label: Post-termination deletion timing
facts.value: Terms allow customer data to remain in backups, archives and disaster-recovery systems until deleted in the ordinary course or as legally required; no fixed purge deadline is stated.

facts.label: Data sent from agent
facts.value: FAQ says the agent sends endpoint names without parameter values, generic call-stack descriptions, sanitized SQL, response times and generic OS/framework metadata.

facts.label: Built-in minimization
facts.value: Request parameters and SQL bind values are scrubbed locally; docs say private user data is not collected by the agent.

facts.label: Excluding sensitive code
facts.value: Skylight.mute can disable instrumentation around a block of code that should not be traced.

facts.label: Contractual prohibited data
facts.value: Terms say the service is not designed for customer personal data, classified data or ITAR-related data, and require customers not to submit these absent a separate agreement.

facts.label: Data region and DPA
facts.value: No telemetry storage region choice, default region or DPA was found in support/security pages, privacy statement or terms reviewed.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Skylight; https://www.skylight.io/; no older product name identified in the checked current pages.

facts.label: Current operator
facts.value: Tilde, Inc.; its contact page gives an address in Portland, Oregon, United States.

facts.label: Current availability
facts.value: Current product and pricing pages offer the hosted service; the official status page reported all systems operational at the time checked.

facts.label: Acquisition or service closure
facts.value: No acquisition, shutdown or whole-service sunset notice found in the checked product blog, Tilde company pages or official-domain searches.

facts.label: Component activity
facts.value: The agent repository showed activity through July 11, 2026; the product blog lists the MCP beta announcement dated May 27, 2026.

facts.label: Sunset search
facts.value: No product or agent retirement notice found in the current blog, support pages or Ruby-agent changelog reviewed.

facts.label: Ruby agent source license
facts.value: The public Ruby-agent LICENSE.md grants limited installation/execution and verbatim-copy rights, while prohibiting modification and other use absent a separate agreement. It is not an OSI-approved open-source license.

facts.label: Hosted backend license
facts.value: Skylight's hosted platform is proprietary; terms grant service-access rights and reserve provider IP. No backend source repository or backend license was identified.

facts.label: Documentation
facts.value: Public support site includes setup, instrumentation, account, troubleshooting and feature guides.

facts.label: Support channel and commitment
facts.value: Support is available at support@skylight.io and through in-app messaging; no public response-time SLA was found in support or terms.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Not applicable: users do not operate the complete Skylight backend; they install and maintain the app-side agent.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Base Status Page offer is US$99/month, billed monthly. Pricing also allows a yearly payment, but no annual amount or discount appears in the accessible page text.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: The base page includes 1,000 subscribers and five team members. Additional team members are available from $5 monthly each; the page does not show a rate for extra subscribers, additional pages or the private-page add-on.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Enterprise offer describes dedicated account management, flexible billing and custom EULA but gives no public price.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: Pricing says customers pay monthly or yearly by card or payment link; the invoice help page says monthly or annual invoices can be viewed, paid and downloaded in the account. The annual rate, minimum term and any annual discount are not published in the pages checked.

facts.label: How billing works
facts.value: The Terms page is linked from the official site but its body did not load in this research view. Renewal, cancellation, refund, tax and commitment clauses could not be checked.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: The current public offer lists a seven-day free trial and paid status-page plans from US$99/month; no continuing free plan is listed.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: Current pricing says the trial lasts seven days and requires no credit card. It says the customer chooses a monthly or yearly payment after the trial, but does not explain auto-charge or refund terms.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: The Help Centre’s “Create a new status page” guide says to start a 14-day free trial with no card required. It is last updated 2023-11-21, while the current pricing page says seven days.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: The lowest public paid offer is Status Page at US$99/month. It includes one base status-page offer with 1,000 subscribers, five team members, incident metrics, component subscriptions, email and Slack/Teams/Google Chat notifications, custom domain, REST and Status APIs, team SAML SSO and team role-based access.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: When subscriber count exceeds its limit, the Subscribe button stays active, but Sorry sends email and SMS notices only to the first X subscribers. It displays an upgrade alert; removing old subscribers is another option.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Five team members are included; additional team seats can be added from $5/month each. No maximum seat count or failed-invite behavior at five seats is stated.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: Public pricing shows extra pages and subscribers as configurable inputs/add-ons, but no public cap behavior or overage rate for those quantities was found in pricing or the relevant Help Centre pages.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: The subscriber limit alert recommends upgrade but does not itself stop new subscriptions; the guide says the first X subscribers continue to receive email/SMS. It is not a spending cap.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: No public hard-spending cap, account-level spend alert, add-on budget control or overage stop was found in pricing, billing help or the Terms page fetch.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Marketing says Sorry keeps a complete incident history; API docs expose paginated current and past notices. No fixed retention period or deletion-after duration for incident notices was stated in the accessible docs.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Public Status API returns a 30-day uptime summary for components with metrics enabled. Public pages show a past-30-day uptime view.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Activity Reports says notice activity goes back to account history; notification counts for email/SMS are available from 2026-02-07 onward. This is a report-data boundary, not a general storage-retention statement.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: The current Privacy page’s body did not load, so data-subject retention periods and data deletion after account cancellation could not be verified.

facts.label: People, apps and projects
facts.value: Base offer includes five management-team members and 1,000 subscribers. Additional team members start at $5/member/month; the pricing page exposes inputs for status-page count and subscriber count, but not readable per-unit rates.

facts.label: People, apps and projects
facts.value: Multiple status pages are sold as an add-on; Collections group multiple pages in one subscriber experience. The Collections page says enabling Collections is free when the account has more than one page, but gives no rate for adding those pages.

facts.label: People, apps and projects
facts.value: Team Members can have Owner, Page Admin, Page Configuration, Team, Publishing and Billing roles, with access limited to selected status pages. The pricing page gives five base team seats and a from-$5 monthly extra-seat rate.

facts.label: People, apps and projects
facts.value: The subscriber-cap guide explains which email/SMS subscribers are notified above the cap, but it does not say whether the 1,000 included subscribers are counted per page or across the account.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: The UK Companies House record gives a registered office in London, England. Sorry’s security page says its support team is based in the UK. No buyer-country restriction or supported-country list was found.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: The current Terms page’s content could not be read in the research view, so any country or customer-type restrictions contained only in those Terms could not be checked.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Publishes public or private service-status pages, incident updates, scheduled maintenance and general notices; sends customer or internal-team notifications. It does not monitor customer infrastructure, but accepts alerts from external monitors.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Sorry sells a hosted status-page service. Public status pages use Sorry-hosted subdomains or a customer custom domain; management, notice and subscriber flows are in the hosted service.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Pricing, product pages, Help Centre and API docs describe hosted service use; no complete self-hosted edition or installation guide was found.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Sorry accepts human-written notices, page data and external monitoring triggers; there is no application SDK that instruments a customer runtime. Language/framework support for error capture does not apply.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Base pricing lists email, Slack, Microsoft Teams and Google Chat. The integration page also describes Intercom, email providers (Postmark, Mailgun and SendGrid), and monitor integrations.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: SMS requires connecting a customer-owned Twilio Messaging Service. Sender registration and availability vary by recipient country; Twilio’s usage and number charges are outside the public Sorry price.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Sorry supports SMS through Twilio, but SMS is sent only when an incident is created/resolved and when scheduled maintenance is created/completed.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Enterprise pricing includes dedicated account management and personalized support, while base pricing advertises UK-based human support. The page does not publish response-time or channel-specific support service levels.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Subscribers can choose components to follow; publishing an incident against selected components notifies only subscribers of affected components. Operators may publish to the page without notifications, or use the configured notification channels.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: SMS is limited to incident start/resolution and scheduled-maintenance start/completion. Email and chat can be chosen as configured notice channels; no repeated-alert schedule or escalation timer was found.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: External monitor automations can choose the affected component and opening/closing notice text, then publish only or publish and notify subscribers. Pingdom integration requires a paid Pingdom plan and Sorry Configuration role.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Sorry is a hosted web status page with public/custom-domain and private/authenticated page modes. It uses a customer’s CNAME and automatically provisioned TLS certificate for custom domains.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: No monitoring agent or private-network probe is part of Sorry. External monitoring systems connect by API, webhook or inbound email and must be operated separately.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: The Sorry REST API is version 1, requires HTTPS, and is rate-limited to 10 requests per second per token; excess requests receive HTTP 429. It supports status pages and notices.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: External monitoring inputs include API/integrations and inbound email. The Help Centre documents Pingdom automation; product pages list New Relic and UptimeRobot among integrations.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: The Status API is for a customer’s subscribers or systems to read the status page’s current state, components and notice history. It is an output API, distinct from the REST API used to update the page.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: To start, create a Sorry account/status page, add components, choose page branding/domain and notification channels, then add subscribers or connect an external monitoring automation. No local service needs to be installed for the status page itself.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Sorry states that it does not monitor customer infrastructure; checks must be run by an external monitor such as Pingdom, New Relic or UptimeRobot.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Sorry does not execute customer checks, so it has no built-in check interval or timeout. Those values belong to the external monitor.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Sorry does not run probes. Probe locations and run-counting rules are set by the connected monitoring provider.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Sorry receives status signals from external monitor integrations or email and publishes a configured notice; the monitor’s retries and maintenance handling are outside Sorry.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Sorry provides and automatically renews TLS certificates for hosted/custom status-page domains, but it is not a domain or certificate-expiry monitor for customer infrastructure.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: The base offer includes one status-page base plan, one custom domain, and the core branding and status-page features. Additional pages are an add-on; no public per-page rate was readable.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Private status pages are a paid add-on. Public pages are accessible for customer communication; private pages support authentication, including Google, Microsoft, Slack, Okta or SAML 2.0 identity providers.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Collections group multiple status pages into one subscriber experience; Sorry says Collections itself is free once an account has more than one page. Existing page custom domains redirect to a path under the Collection’s primary domain when pages are combined.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Sorry Audiences was announced to let a public page show different components, metrics and notice history to named users or groups. The announcement still labels it “coming soon,” with an October target that has passed; current availability is not confirmed.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Pages can show an uptime graph and incident metrics; metrics can be enabled/disabled for components. No maximum component or sub-component count was found in pricing, component docs or API docs.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Base page includes 1,000 subscribers. When the limit is reached, Sorry continues collecting subscribers but sends email and SMS notices only to the first X; it shows an upgrade alert. Extra-subscriber prices are not published.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Subscribers can select the components they want to follow; component subscriptions route a notice only to subscribers of affected components, while “All status updates” subscribers receive all notices.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Email, Slack, Microsoft Teams and Google Chat are listed in the base plan. SMS uses the customer’s Twilio setup; SMS triggers are incident creation/resolution and scheduled-maintenance creation/completion.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Email and SMS can use double opt-in. Sorry can send email through configured providers such as Postmark, SendGrid or Mailgun; provider charges are not included in a published Sorry per-message rate.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Operators can manually post incident, planned-maintenance and general notices. Notice states include investigating, identified, recovering, resolved/false alarm and scheduled, underway, complete/cancelled maintenance.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: External monitors can trigger notices through the REST API, monitor integrations such as Pingdom/New Relic/UptimeRobot, webhooks or inbound email. Sorry is the communication endpoint, not the monitor.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Activity Reports summarize incident, maintenance and general notices, notification counts and subscriber totals. Notice activity goes back to account history; email/SMS totals are available from 2026-02-07.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: The vendor’s own status page currently says all systems are operational and displays release notes and operational events; the latest visible update was dated 2026-11-04.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Subscribers can be exported as JSON through the API, 500 records per page by default, or an export can be requested from support.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: The REST API can delete a status page; the API documentation says this also deletes its notices, components and subscribers. Individual subscribers can also be deleted through the subscriber endpoint.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: How long backups or deleted account data remain after cancellation could not be checked because the Terms and Privacy bodies were not readable; the security page describes short-lived backups but not post-cancellation deletion.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Subscriber records can include email, phone, names, nickname, company, tags and channel details. Email and SMS subscriptions can use double opt-in; admins can search/remove subscribers and import only contacts who consented.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Security page says traffic is HTTPS and email addresses/passwords are encrypted at rest; the database and backups are encrypted. It does not describe masking or redaction for subscriber details, notice text or external monitor payloads.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: The Privacy page body could not be read, so the full personal-data categories, lawful bases, subprocessors and customer deletion rights were not verified from that policy.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Security page describes encrypted databases/backups and global CDN delivery, but does not name data-storage regions. The privacy page did not expose its body in the research view.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Sorry’s Help Centre says it can issue a DPA to customers who request one. A DPA is linked from the site footer, but the Google Drive page opened a sign-in screen and the document contents could not be checked.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Current product is Sorry™ (the official pages also use SorryApp). No earlier product name was found.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Sorry is actively offered with a public pricing page, Help Centre and current service-status page. The service page reported “All systems are go!” and recent operational updates through 2026-11-04.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: The latest official blog list checked showed posts through 2026-09-21. Product release notes are published on Sorry’s own status page; no separate newsroom page was found in the site navigation or the newsroom search. No acquisition or shutdown notice appeared in those sources.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Sorry™ Audiences was announced as in final development with an October 2026 target. The official September 21 post still says “coming soon”; the current status feed checked through November 4 has no Audiences launch notice. The feature’s current release state is not confirmed.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: The official UK Companies House record lists SORRYAPP LTD (company number 09036295) as a private limited company, incorporated 2014-05-13, with active status in the registry. Sorry’s site footer names SorryApp LTD.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: Not applicable to the listed hosted product: the official offer describes the hosted Sorry service, and I found no self-hosted edition or source repository for the complete service.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Public Help Centre covers getting started, pages, components, notices, roles, notifications, integrations, billing and legal help. Current plans advertise real-human support based in the UK; no guaranteed response time appears in the plan.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Enterprise includes dedicated account management and personalised support. The current pricing page does not publish a response-time SLA or 24/7 support entitlement.

facts.label: Billing unit
facts.value: Each status page has its own paid subscription and invoice. An account can manage multiple pages and choose a different plan for each page.

facts.label: Published plan prices and quotas
facts.value: Basic $79/month, 500 subscribers, 5 team members, 5 metrics; Standard $149/month, 2,000 subscribers, 20 team members, 20 metrics; Plus $349/month, 5,000 subscribers, 50 team members, 50 metrics.

facts.label: Enterprise starting price
facts.value: Enterprise is sales-led and starts at $999/month; detailed quotas and price above the published starting figure require a quote.

facts.label: Annual billing
facts.value: The pricing page advertises a 5% discount for annual subscriptions.

facts.label: Payment processing
facts.value: Credit-card transactions are processed by Stripe; Status.io says its servers do not store payment details. Invoices can be viewed or downloaded as PDFs in the account.

facts.label: Purchase orders
facts.value: Custom billing methods are available to Plus customers. Purchase orders require a 12-month commitment.

facts.label: Taxes and recurring charges
facts.value: Terms say subscriptions renew with automatic charges at the end of each chosen period; unless an invoice states otherwise, taxes, levies and duties are extra.

facts.label: Refunds and cancellation
facts.value: Customer cancellation does not entitle the customer to a refund under the published Terms. If Status.io terminates access without cause, it says it will prorate a refund for prepaid unused time.

facts.label: Ongoing free plan
facts.value: The current plan listing shows Basic, Standard, Plus and quote-led Enterprise, with no ongoing $0 plan described.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: The pages checked do not specify a trial duration, card requirement, eligibility rule, or trial-to-paid auto-charge terms.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: Basic is the lowest listed paid plan at $79/month; it includes 500 subscribers, 5 team members, 5 metrics and one public status page.

facts.label: Subscriber over-limit behavior
facts.value: The pricing page publishes subscriber caps, but the pages checked do not say whether new subscriptions are blocked, charged, or automatically upgraded after a cap is reached.

facts.label: Event capacity beyond standard plans
facts.value: Status.io says unusually high incident or maintenance volume and longer historical storage may require a High Capacity add-on or custom pricing; no public rate is listed.

facts.label: Hard spend cap and usage alerts
facts.value: A customer-enforced Status.io spend cap or subscription usage alert is not described on pricing, billing, or high-capacity pages.

facts.label: SMS billing control boundary
facts.value: Twilio or Vonage bills the customer separately by message; a Status.io SMS rate limit is available, while provider-side billing alerts are recommended. These controls do not cap the Status.io subscription.

facts.label: Status-chart history
facts.value: Status Charts display component status over the previous 90 days; incident events, optional maintenance events and optional calculated uptime percentage can appear.

facts.label: Incident and maintenance history
facts.value: Public pages show up to 1,000 incidents and 1,000 maintenances at a time; older items remain in the account. Dashboard lists have similar approximate caps, and API list responses are paginated/limited.

facts.label: Notification log export
facts.value: Subscriber notification logs can be exported for up to 30 days; Status.io says the limit is higher for Enterprise, without publishing the Enterprise duration.

facts.label: Other stored-data retention
facts.value: A general retention duration for account, incident, integration and metric data while the account remains open is not given in the reviewed privacy, security, terms or history pages.

facts.label: Visitor log and closed-account retention
facts.value: Privacy says status-page visitor web-server logs are kept for approximately 30 days. On account closure, it says account references are removed from databases/shared services, while backup references may remain up to 30 days; the deletion guide says pages and history are permanently deleted.

facts.label: Subscriber, team and metric allowances
facts.value: Basic: 500 subscribers, 5 team members, 5 metrics. Standard: 2,000, 20, 20. Plus: 5,000, 50, 50.

facts.label: Pages per account and separate billing
facts.value: An account may manage multiple status pages; each is independent, can use its own plan, and receives separate billing. A maximum number of pages per account is not stated in the guide checked.

facts.label: Team roles
facts.value: The guide describes Owner, Admin and Limited roles; page team members are included with each page subscription.

facts.label: Container and component quantities
facts.value: The pricing page describes components and containers but its extracted plan matrix does not expose a reliable per-tier quantity for either.

facts.label: Vendor home region
facts.value: About identifies the operating team as based in Monmouth County, New Jersey, United States.

facts.label: Buyer eligibility
facts.value: Terms require account holders to be over 18 and prohibit use that violates U.S. law or export controls. A broader supported-country or buyer-eligibility list was not found.

facts.label: Jobs covered
facts.value: Hosts public and private system status pages; manages incidents and planned maintenance; sends status communications; can display selected third-party service health and monitoring metrics.

facts.label: Detection boundary
facts.value: Monitoring integrations can toggle component status, and Status.io checks selected third-party service APIs. The reviewed pages do not describe direct checks of the customer’s own application endpoints or collection of its exceptions.

facts.label: Hosting model
facts.value: Status.io offers a vendor-hosted status platform. The reviewed official pages describe no complete self-hosted Status.io edition or customer-run server package.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Status.io is not documented as receiving application instrumentation or error events from language agents. Its API client libraries are for managing the status service, not for collecting app errors.

facts.label: Status notification channels
facts.value: Published channels include email, webhook, SMS, Slack, Microsoft Teams, IRC, Twitter/X, RSS and iCalendar. The plan comparison’s per-tier channel checkmarks are not reliably readable in the fetched text.

facts.label: SMS delivery price
facts.value: Status.io does not add an SMS fee. Customers use their own Twilio or Vonage accounts and pay the provider per message; international rates vary.

facts.label: Status.io human support
facts.value: Pricing says every plan includes 24/7 human support. The support guide publishes support@status.io and in-dashboard help; no response-time target was found.

facts.label: Incident notification choice
facts.value: Incident creation and updates can be published to the status page with subscriber broadcasting optional; the editor allows selecting affected components/containers.

facts.label: Planned-maintenance notification choice
facts.value: Maintenance can be scheduled, started, updated and completed; broadcasting can be chosen per update, and automated maintenance can start/end without intervention.

facts.label: Subscriber topic selection
facts.value: Subscribers can receive all components by default or choose specific components/containers, and can change preferences through a unique management link.

facts.label: Alert grouping, escalation and repeat schedule
facts.value: Rules for grouping monitoring alerts, escalating between on-call recipients, or repeating notifications on a timer were not found in Status.io’s incident, subscriber, integration or pricing pages.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Browser-based, vendor-hosted dashboard and customer status pages; the vendor operates the service on AWS with warm failover environments including DigitalOcean. No customer-side monitoring agent or self-hosted deployment is documented.

facts.label: Incoming status updates
facts.value: Monitoring systems can send an email with UP or DOWN in its subject to an address tied to a component/container; Status.io then toggles the displayed state.

facts.label: Monitoring integrations
facts.value: The integration page lists monitoring tools including Pingdom, New Relic, Datadog, Dynatrace, Nagios, UptimeRobot, Uptime.com, StatusCake, LogicMonitor, AWS and Zabbix. Any monitor able to send up/down emails can use email triggers.

facts.label: Developer API
facts.value: Status.io publishes a Developer API for account-side operations such as managing status-page resources. The public documentation labels it API v2.

facts.label: Public Status API
facts.value: A public GET API returns current overall status, components and container status for consumers.

facts.label: External-service health display
facts.value: Status.io checks selected third-party service APIs or public status pages, may run transactional/ping/availability tests, refreshes data so it is no more than five minutes old, and sends no notifications for these checks.

facts.label: Logs, traces and error-event intake
facts.value: No ingestion path for application logs, traces, exception events, OTLP or application telemetry was found in the product overview, integration list, Developer API, or help index.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: A documented setup is to create a status page, add components/containers, set page URL and visibility, configure design and subscribers, then connect monitoring integrations or create incidents and maintenance events.

facts.label: Page types and purpose
facts.value: Status.io offers public status pages and private pages restricted through an identity provider or IP access controls. A distinct audience-specific page product was not found.

facts.label: Public page allocation and domain
facts.value: Each plan includes one public status page. The pricing page lists custom domain and a secure TLS/SSL subdomain among plan features; each extra page needs its own subscription.

facts.label: Private-page identity-provider access
facts.value: Private-page access relies on an external identity provider and can use SAML or OIDC depending on the viewer setup. Private page authentication has separate settings from team-member SSO.

facts.label: Private-page IP access
facts.value: IP access control allows a page to be limited to configured IPv4/IPv6 ranges; setup requires a custom domain and TLS/SSL.

facts.label: Audience-specific page or customer groups
facts.value: No separate page type that assigns different customers/groups distinct status-page views was located in current features, pricing or private-page docs. Component subscription preferences are published instead.

facts.label: Page branding and styling
facts.value: Pricing says plans include customizable design; feature pages advertise design controls and custom HTML, JavaScript and CSS. Exact plan gates for each customization are not readable in the current pricing text extract.

facts.label: Subscriber caps

facts.label: Audit-log export

facts.label: Deployment fit

facts.value: Website monitors send HTTP requests; ping monitors send ICMP requests. Website settings accept GET, POST, PUT, or PATCH, headers, basic authentication, response-code and content checks.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: StatusGator has a REST API, webhooks, and private-status integrations. These expose or connect status data; they are not a general OpenTelemetry or log-ingestion service.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Published API rate limits are Free 15, Starter 30, Team 60, Corporate 60, and Enterprise 120 requests per minute.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Create an account, add a service/website/ping/custom monitor, select components or test settings, then configure email/chat/SMS or webhooks. A board also has a hosted status page.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Website setup uses a URL and optional expected response, content, interval, region, timeout, retry, method, headers, or Basic Auth settings. Ping setup uses a hostname/IP and optional regions, timeout, and retries.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Service Monitor follows a catalog of third-party SaaS/cloud providers using their official status pages, APIs, or other published status signals, with Early Warning Signals.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Website Monitor supports HTTP/HTTPS websites and API endpoints, availability checks, expected response codes, redirects, and optional keyword/content checks.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Ping Monitor sends ICMP requests to a hostname or IP address to check network reachability.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Custom Monitor is manually controlled; the owner creates incidents and maintenance instead of having StatusGator run a check.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: The checked StatusGator monitor docs do not describe DNS record, TCP-port, browser-script, or private-location synthetic checks as native monitor types.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Service Monitors are checked every 5 minutes; users cannot select a faster service-page polling interval in the checked docs.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Website and Ping checks can be configured from 1 to 5 minutes. The docs do not state a plan-specific minimum interval.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Website timeout options are 5, 15, 30 seconds (default), or 60 seconds. Ping timeout is configurable from 5 to 60 seconds.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Plan-level quota is expressed as monitor count, but the current public pricing/help pages do not say whether one-minute website or ping intervals are restricted by plan.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Website and Ping monitors can use eight named regions: US East, US West, EU West, AU East, UK East, AP South, AP Southeast, and AP Northeast.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Users select one or more of those probe regions. Alert logic can require all selected regions to fail or trigger when any selected region fails.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Pricing counts monitors and does not publish a per-region, per-probe, or per-run charge. It does not explicitly say whether multiple selected locations affect the monitor quota.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Website checks support retries before alerting, including immediate alert on first failure or additional consecutive retries. The public help text does not specify a universal retry count for every monitor.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Ping monitors support consecutive failed-check sensitivity; the help example says two retries means three consecutive failed checks before alerting.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Region logic can trigger on any or all selected failures. If a provider status page is unreachable, the service monitor shows its last known status.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Website and Ping monitors can be paused and resumed. Custom monitors support manually scheduled maintenance and incidents.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Trust page points to TrackSSL as StatusGator's certificate visibility platform and the integrations list includes TrackSSL. The StatusGator monitor docs do not define direct certificate or domain-expiry checks or their plan limits.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: One board contains one hosted status page. Page count by plan therefore follows boards: Free 1; Starter 1; Team 3; Corporate 5; Enterprise more by agreement.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Free supports 1 page because it includes one board; the exact public/private feature gates for Free are not clearly stated in plan text.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Starter supports 1 page because it includes one board.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Team supports 3 pages because it includes 3 boards.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Corporate supports 5 pages because it includes 5 boards.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Enterprise supports more than 5 boards/pages by custom agreement; its exact page count is not published.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Status pages support public access, password protection, or authenticated access; Enterprise includes authenticated email or SAML status-page login.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: All status pages receive a StatusGator-hosted statusgator.app subdomain. The help page supports a custom domain through a CNAME and automatic Let's Encrypt certificate.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Page settings support logos, favicon, themes, one-to-three-column layouts, colors, titles, links, hidden monitors, and page-specific analytics.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: The company says branding can be white-labeled on some plans and the help guide supports removing the StatusGator footer. The exact paid tier is not stated in readable plan text.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: The page can be cached at the CDN and updates about every 2 minutes; page viewers can set browser refresh to 1 minute, 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 1 hour, or never.

facts.label: Status-page limits and branding
facts.value: Status-page subscriber limits by plan: Free 100; Starter 500; Team 1,000; Corporate 1,000; Enterprise more. Whether the number is per page or account is not stated.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Visitors can subscribe to email updates for all monitored services or select only services they follow; confirmation is normally emailed unless skipped by an admin.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: The plan table caps status-page subscribers at Free 100, Starter 500, Team 1,000, Corporate 1,000, and Enterprise more by agreement.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Subscriber updates are by email. SMS is an admin alert integration for paid plans and is not documented as a status-page subscriber channel.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Owners can add and remove subscribers, choose all services or selected services, restrict email domains, and allow outage reports from viewers.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: Paid plans can customize subscriber email branding with logo and sender details. The help page does not name the exact qualifying tier.

facts.label: Subscriber notifications
facts.value: StatusGator does not publish a separate charge per status-page subscriber or subscriber email; plan subscriber counts apply.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Pages can display third-party Service Monitors, website and ping check results, and custom monitors. Automated check state and manually authored custom incidents are distinct sources.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Custom incidents support maintenance notices, major/minor severity, and phases from investigation through resolution; each update may notify subscribers.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Provider service incidents and Early Warning Signals can flow to a status page from the monitored component or service; page owners can hide selected monitors.

facts.label: Status update source
facts.value: Status page history duration follows the plan's historical-data allowance: 1, 3, 6, 12, or 24 months across Free, Starter, Team, Corporate, or Enterprise.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Historical reports can be exported as JSON, CSV, or Excel for board history, status changes, component changes, and component summaries.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: The API provides programmatic status data. Privacy policy says users can request a machine-readable copy of personal data by email.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: Users can delete a profile; deleting an organization requires downgrading to Free first. The privacy policy says personal data is deleted within 30 days after account deletion.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: The service stores selected providers/components, user and account details, notification settings, integration credentials, and status-page subscriber emails. It says it does not sell user data.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Privacy policy says TLS is used for the website and email; Trust page says data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and pages/API use HTTPS/TLS. Security documentation also says hosted pages require HTTPS.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Website monitors can include custom headers and HTTP Basic Authentication credentials. The reviewed help, privacy, and security pages do not describe per-field secret masking or credential redaction controls.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Trust page says customer-data access is limited to selected engineers handling production issues and lists role-based access, audit logging, offsite backups, and data erasure procedures.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Privacy policy says StatusGator stores customer data on US-based servers and transfers data to the US for users elsewhere.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Privacy policy lists processors including Google Analytics, Google Workspace, Stripe, Freshdesk, Bugsnag, Sendgrid, Postmark, HotJar, and ProfitWell.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: A public DPA was not linked from the Terms, Privacy, or Trust pages checked. Whether a DPA is available on request is not stated there.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: StatusGator; no former name is listed on its About page.

facts.label: Availability and changes
facts.value: Listed active in apps.md. Current public plans and help center are live; the official blog and changelog show product updates dated through 2026-11-02.

facts.label: Vendor service status
facts.value: StatusGator's own service-status listing reported it up when checked; it showed the last officially acknowledged incident on 2026-08-29.

facts.label: Acquisition or shutdown notice
facts.value: No StatusGator acquisition, shutdown, or sunset notice was found in the official blog, changelog archive, In the Media archive, or About page checked.

facts.label: Current owner
facts.value: StatusGator is a service of Nimble Industries, Inc. The company About page says Nimble Industries was formed as a holding company for StatusGator; it also describes TinySeed as an investor.

facts.label: License and source code
facts.value: No public source repository, self-host package, or software license for the hosted platform is offered in the official product pages checked; website terms reserve intellectual-property rights.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Public support center, quick-start guides, email hi@statusgator.com, and ticket submission are available. No public numerical response-time guarantee was found.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: The paid plan page lists chat, help-desk, monitoring, incident-management, and status-page integrations with tier gates; feature comparison check marks are not readable in extracted page text for every feature.
