facts.value: The official download and license pages describe free, ongoing self-hosted use but do not publish a separate trial period, card rule, or trial-specific terms.

facts.label: Trial
facts.value: Zabbix Cloud advertises a five-day free trial. The Cloud FAQ says a trial node without a payment method is stopped and deleted after the trial ends; Cloud terms allow charges after a trial when applicable.

facts.label: Smallest useful paid plan
facts.value: There is no required paid software tier. Paid support starts with Silver at €245/month billed annually; paid support is optional and does not change the free software license.

facts.label: When a limit is exceeded
facts.value: There is no vendor usage quota or self-hosted overage bill. Local disk, database, CPU, and collection-process capacity are finite; the operator must size the system and choose retention.

facts.label: Bill controls
facts.value: There is no Zabbix software usage bill to cap or alert on. Provider-level spend caps, alerts, or budget rules are not Zabbix controls and depend on the chosen infrastructure provider.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Item history stores each received value. Per-item history can be set from one hour to 25 years or disabled; global housekeeping can override item settings. The API currently documents a 31-day default.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Trends keep hourly minimum, maximum, average, and count for numeric values. The API documents a 365-day default; the configured period can be extended up to 25 years.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: Trigger, service, internal, discovery, autoregistration, session, and audit data each have housekeeping controls; event types can have separate periods. Default housekeeping runs hourly.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: ClickHouse can hold item history values, including log and text types, but Zabbix housekeeping does not remove ClickHouse data. Its own storage policy must be configured in ClickHouse.

facts.label: Data retention
facts.value: OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs are read from a configured telemetry data source. Zabbix does not publish one retention period for that external data source; retention depends on the selected backend.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: The product does not charge per host, device, application, user, metric, or alert. Zabbix subscription material confirms unlimited counts for those measures; actual throughput is limited by the deployment resources.

facts.label: People, apps, and projects
facts.value: User access is controlled through user types, configurable roles, user groups, and host-group permissions. No fixed self-hosted seat allowance is published.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Agent log and logrt items filter and stream matching lines; maxlines-per-second controls how many new lines an agent sends. There is no vendor ingest meter for self-hosted logs.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: Zabbix sizing guidance estimates about 500 bytes per text/log value, but says actual size cannot be predicted exactly.

facts.label: Log allowances and loss
facts.value: OTel logs can be queried from the configured telemetry data source. Zabbix does not publish a separate log ingestion rate or quota for its self-hosted OTel path.

facts.label: Query and extra-data charges
facts.value: Zabbix charges no per-query, per-index, or per-export fee for self-hosted data. Costs for ClickHouse, databases, disks, and backups belong to the operator or provider.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: Zabbix SIA is registered in Latvia and lists its headquarters in Riga, Latvia.

facts.label: Home region and eligible buyers
facts.value: No country-by-country buyer restrictions for downloading the self-hosted software were found in the license, download, or privacy pages checked.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Collects and evaluates metrics from servers, networks, applications, databases, virtual machines, cloud services, and other IT resources. It can monitor errors represented as metrics or log/trace data, but its primary product is general monitoring, not issue-based exception tracking.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Trigger rules evaluate collected values and create problem events; actions can notify, create tickets through integrations, or run remote commands.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Agent log items can monitor local and rotated files, filter lines, and extract values. Zabbix 8.0 also queries OpenTelemetry logs through a telemetry data source.

facts.label: Jobs it covers
facts.value: Zabbix 8.0 adds OpenTelemetry application performance monitoring for traces, metrics, and logs.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Both: the complete server, frontend, agent, proxy, and database can be installed by the user; Zabbix Cloud is a separate vendor-managed service.

facts.label: Hosted and self-hosted options
facts.value: Official package, source, virtual appliance, container, and cloud-image distribution paths are listed.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: A proprietary per-language SDK is not required for basic collection: agents, network protocols, HTTP/API checks, and templates collect data. Zabbix 8.0 APM uses OpenTelemetry SDKs and collectors rather than a Zabbix-specific language SDK.

facts.label: Languages and frameworks
facts.value: Agent 2 includes plugins for database and infrastructure systems such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Docker, and others.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Media types include email, push notification, SMS, custom scripts, and webhooks. Zabbix includes no notification credits or delivery allowance; SMTP, SMS gateway, or third-party webhook services may charge separately.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Email can use a configured SMTP server or the predefined Gmail and Office365 options. The sender must configure a working account and mail service.

facts.label: Alert channels and costs
facts.value: Webhooks can connect actions to external services, and push notification is a listed delivery method. Availability and provider cost depend on the integration and destination service.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Actions support trigger, service, discovery, autoregistration, and internal events; conditions decide when operations run.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Escalations can delay or repeat notifications and pass unresolved incidents to another user or group. They can also run remote commands; there is no published maximum number of steps.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Media can be restricted by active time window and severity. Failed sends retry up to 100 attempts, default 3; retry interval can be 0–3600 seconds.

facts.label: Alert noise and escalation
facts.value: Maintenance periods suppress notifications according to their configuration; escalation steps can pause or continue through maintenance based on the action setting.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Server and proxy run on supported Unix-like platforms; agents are available for Windows, Linux, macOS, AIX, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, Solaris, and other documented systems. Agent 2 has a newer Windows minimum of Windows 10 / Server 2016.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Official Docker and Compose files deploy the server, frontend, and relational database in containers. Persistent data is stored in configured volumes.

facts.label: Deployment fit
facts.value: Proxies can collect from remote sites or private networks and forward to a central server over one TCP connection.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Zabbix agent and agent 2 support passive checks requested by server/proxy and active checks sent by the agent. The agent collects local operating-system and application data.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Agent log and logrt items stream matching local or rotated log lines as active checks. Lines can be filtered or transformed before sending.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Agentless inputs include SNMP, ICMP/TCP/UDP simple checks, HTTP agent, database monitor, JMX, IPMI, SSH, Telnet, external checks, and trapper items.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Zabbix can collect Prometheus line-format metrics through an HTTP master item and dependent items with Prometheus preprocessing.

facts.label: Sending data in
facts.value: Zabbix 8.0 APM queries OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs from a configured telemetry data source. Telemetry collection is enabled through a proxy with APM support or an OTel collector; the server itself is not the direct OTel receiver.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Standard setup installs a supported operating system, web server, database, and PHP; then installs Zabbix server, frontend, and an agent, imports the initial schema, and completes the frontend wizard.

facts.label: Setup path
facts.value: Ready-made templates can be linked to hosts to collect common Linux, Windows, database, network, and service metrics; custom items and triggers can be added.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Web scenarios perform ordered HTTP request steps and can check status codes, response text, and authentication flows. They collect response time, response code, download speed, and failed-step information.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Simple checks cover ICMP reachability and packet loss, TCP/UDP service availability and performance, and DNS checks.

facts.label: Check types
facts.value: Browser items can run JavaScript with a WebDriver endpoint to simulate browser interactions such as navigation, clicks, and form entry.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: Web-scenario update intervals accept time suffixes; each step has a timeout. The current docs give no universal plan-like minimum interval for self-hosted checks.

facts.label: Check frequency and timeout
facts.value: A newly created web scenario is checked within 60 seconds; step attempts can be configured up to 10, with one as the default.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: There is no built-in vendor probe-location allowance for self-hosting. Checks run from the Zabbix server or an assigned proxy; operators can deploy proxies in their own locations and networks.

facts.label: Probe locations and check counting
facts.value: Zabbix Cloud has five selectable regions on its public page, and Cloud Proxy can be deployed for distributed monitoring. Region names are not listed in text on the public marketing page.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Web checks can retry up to 10 times for network problems; default is one attempt. A wrong response code or required string mismatch is treated as a failed step without repeating it.

facts.label: Failure confirmation and maintenance
facts.value: Maintenance periods can suppress problem notifications for planned work.

facts.label: Certificate and domain expiry
facts.value: Zabbix provides a documented agent 2 template/check for website SSL certificate monitoring.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: The API can query history by type, host, item, time range, and search conditions; the frontend also shows latest data and monitored log items.

facts.label: Searching and archives
facts.value: No archive tier or separately priced retrieval service is published for self-hosting. ClickHouse or another external telemetry backend has its own search and retention controls.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: Zabbix 8.0 APM displays and filters OpenTelemetry traces and spans, including service name, span status, timing, attributes, and errors, when connected to a supported telemetry data source.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: Trigger expressions can evaluate historical values and anomaly-related functions, including moving baselines, forecasts, and percentiles, for configured metrics.

facts.label: Slow-request diagnosis
facts.value: No code profiler or automatic database-query profiler was found in the APM and item-type docs checked.

facts.label: Performance-data sampling
facts.value: Zabbix docs reviewed do not publish a Zabbix-side trace sampling rate, sampling control, or sampling-based billing rule. Sampling can be configured upstream in the OpenTelemetry instrumentation or collector.

facts.label: Real-user performance
facts.value: No real-user browser or mobile performance product was documented in the product pages, APM docs, or current feature list checked. Browser items are synthetic checks, not real-user monitoring.

facts.label: Error grouping and coverage
facts.value: The checked Zabbix 8.0 docs describe trigger problems and OTel span errors, but do not document SDK exception-event capture, issue grouping, or duplicate-error aggregation as an error-tracker workflow.

facts.label: Readable error locations
facts.value: No source-map upload, native crash symbolication, or exception stack-trace workflow was found in the current APM, item-type, or integration pages checked.

facts.label: Release and fix tracking
facts.value: Release/deployment grouping, regression alerts, and source-control linking for application exceptions were not found in the docs, release notes, or integration pages checked.

facts.label: Context and replay
facts.value: OTel traces expose span attributes and request-flow timing, but user-session replay and error breadcrumbs were not found in the APM, browser, or privacy docs checked.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: A standard installation needs a supported Unix-like operating system, Zabbix server, web frontend, PHP, database, and optionally agents/proxies. Supported server database choices include MySQL/Percona/MariaDB or PostgreSQL; ClickHouse is an optional history or telemetry data source with different behavior.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Official starting size for a small deployment: 1,000 monitored metrics, 2 CPU/vCPU cores, 8 GiB RAM; example EC2 shape m6i.large or m6g.large.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Official starting size for a medium deployment: 10,000 monitored metrics, 4 CPU/vCPU cores, 16 GiB RAM; example EC2 shape m6i.xlarge or m6g.xlarge.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Official starting size for a large deployment: 100,000 monitored metrics, 16 CPU/vCPU cores, 64 GiB RAM; example m6i.4xlarge or m6g.4xlarge. A separate database server is recommended for large installations.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Official starting size for a very large deployment: 1,000,000 monitored metrics, 32 CPU/vCPU cores, 96 GiB RAM; example m6i.8xlarge or m6g.8xlarge.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Database disk depends on new values per second, retention, data type, and database engine. Zabbix estimates about 90 bytes per numeric history value and around 500 bytes per text/log value; 50 values/second for 30 days is about 130 million values or 10.9 GB numeric history.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Proxies support SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL and buffer collected data locally. Hybrid buffering protects data by flushing to database when stopping or when the buffer reaches limits; memory-only buffering can lose unsent values.

facts.label: Self-host requirements
facts.value: Dependencies vary by checks: PHP and a supported web server for the frontend; libcurl for web monitoring; fping for ICMP checks; net-snmp for SNMP; a Java gateway for JMX; and ClickHouse for the documented alternative history/APM store.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: The JSON-RPC 2.0 HTTP API retrieves history and configuration; history.get can filter by host, item, and time.

facts.label: Export and deletion
facts.value: The API supports removing hosts and clearing history; housekeeping removes expired data. The reviewed docs do not describe a one-click full export of all monitored history.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: Logs, item values, macros, and OTel spans may contain sensitive content. Agent log items can match or transform lines before sending, but no universal PII or secret redaction setting was found in the checked docs.

facts.label: Sensitive-data controls
facts.value: The security docs recommend restricting network ports and enabling component encryption. Encryption protects component communications but does not redact collected values.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: For self-hosting, the operator chooses the infrastructure, storage region, and retention setup. Zabbix's public privacy policy covers personal data it processes as a company, not the operator's local Zabbix data.

facts.label: Storage regions and data terms
facts.value: Zabbix Cloud advertises five regions; its privacy policy says account data is kept in EU data centers and customer content remains in the region selected for the Cloud node. The marketing page does not name all five regions in readable public text.

facts.label: Product identity
facts.value: Zabbix; https://www.zabbix.com/

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Zabbix 8.0.0 LTS is the latest release listed, dated 2026-11-05. The same release list shows maintenance releases 7.4.16, 7.0.32, and 6.0.49 dated 2026-10-20.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Zabbix 8.0 LTS: full support through 2029-11-30; limited support through 2031-11-30.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: Standard releases are released every six months and supported for 12 months; LTS releases are released every 1.5 years and supported for five years.

facts.label: Availability and product changes
facts.value: No product shutdown, sunset, or acquisition notice was found in the current release list, official blog index, pressroom, or release notes checked.

facts.label: License and code
facts.value: GNU Affero General Public License v3 (AGPLv3) for Zabbix 7.0 and later. Official Zabbix source repository: https://git.zabbix.com/projects/zbx/repos/zabbix/browse

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Public manuals and quickstarts are available. Community help is available through the Zabbix forum; no community-project response-time SLA is published in the checked support pages.

facts.label: Help and documentation
facts.value: Paid subscriptions include defined response targets and access to Zabbix experts; Silver is 8x5 with a one-day initial response, while higher tiers have shorter response targets and 24x7 coverage at some levels.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Zabbix 8.0 LTS receives full support through 2029-11-30 and limited critical-fix support through 2031-11-30. Standard releases have a shorter 12-month lifecycle; the project publishes supported-branch dates.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Before major upgrade, the official guide says back up the database, configuration, PHP files, and binaries; the server applies required database schema patches during startup.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: The upgrade guide gives package, container, and source upgrade paths. Proxies should be upgraded; an older proxy may have limited functions, and proxies outside the supported version window stop communicating.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Zabbix publishes a responsible-disclosure security policy and security advisories; maintained releases receive high priority. No guaranteed public patch-time SLA was found for self-hosters.

facts.label: Self-host upkeep
facts.value: Native high availability is available for Zabbix server: multiple server nodes share one database, with one active node and standby nodes. It does not remove the need to protect the database and frontend.

changes.label: Closing
changes.text: Pivoted from monitoring to AI compute (2026-09-02)

changes.label: New owner
changes.text: Parent SolarWinds bought by Turn/River (2025-04-15); accounts moving to SolarWinds Observability
